events.title: PA: Attend Allegheny County Board of Health Meetings!

location.venue: Allegheny County Courthouse Gold Room, 4th Floor

events.description:
**Join us at the next Allegheny County Board of Health (BOH) meeting to demand that all new fracking be prohibited in Allegheny County.** 

It can no longer be denied: Fracking can't be done without threatening human health and climate stability. Just as recently as 2023, a state-funded health study in southwest PA found that fracking correlates with increased rates of asthma and low birth weight, as well as sharply elevated risk of childhood lymphoma _(5-7 times the national average)_.

Per the Pennsylvania Disease and Prevention Control Act of 1955, "Local boards and departments of health shall be primarily responsible for the prevention and control of communicable and non-communicable disease... in accordance with the regulations of the board and subject to the supervision and guidance of the department." *This means that the Allegheny County BOH is responsible for and has the power to enact policy to prevent the incredibly harmful effects of fracking!*

**RSVP to receive details and reminders, as well as talking points for submitting in-person and written comments.** See you there!

**_The BOH requires speakers to sign up at least 72 hours prior to the meeting. Sign-up instructions are provided in the "How to Prepare" section of the mobilize registration confirmation email and reminder emails_**

events.title: Compost Hub Support: Sepulveda Garden Center
events.description:
At our Compost Hubs, food scraps collected from the community are transformed into nutrient-rich compost, and we need your help to make it happen! As a Compost Hub Support Volunteer, you’ll gain hands-on experience working alongside our knowledgeable Compost Managers. Get ready to leave feeling accomplished, a little sweaty, and brimming with new compost knowledge. 

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:
Roll up your sleeves and dive into a variety of engaging activities, whether it’s managing a three-bin system, tending to a compost pile, sifting finished compost, or exploring a mix of everything. There’s something for everyone, from beginners to seasoned pros! Plus, our Compost Hubs are situated in LA County’s most cherished green spaces: community gardens, urban farms, and beautiful parks. Join passionate community composters, learn to turn food scraps into rich compost, and connect with the local food system. 

#### MORE INFO: 
* You will be working outdoors! Shade levels vary by site.
* Activity level can be adjusted to your comfort and abilities; just communicate with your Compost Manager.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome!
* Bathrooms are available at this location. 
* If you sign up, we ask that you show up! We rely on volunteers, like you, to achieve our mission.  
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under the age of 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT: 

VOLUNTEER WAIVER: Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. You can access the e-waiver at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver 

CODE OF CONDUCT: All volunteers are expected to adhere to our volunteer code of conduct. Please visit https://www.lacompost.org/codeofconduct to review.

events.description:
Join Magnified Voices as we show up to protect public education, empower our community, and advocate for Hillsborough County students and families.

Local school board decisions shape what happens in our classrooms, from funding and curriculum to student services, school policies, and community engagement. When families and community members attend meetings, stay informed, and speak up, we help ensure those decisions remain transparent, accountable, and centered on students.

Whether you are an experienced advocate or attending a school board meeting for the first time, your presence matters. 

Participants will have the opportunity to:
Learn about the issues affecting Hillsborough County Public Schools
Observe School Board discussions and decisions
Connect with other public education advocates
Support transparency and accountability
Help elevate the needs of students, families, and educators

You do not need to be an expert or speak during the meeting to make a difference. Showing up, listening, learning, and sharing information with your community are all powerful forms of advocacy.

Together, we can protect public education, empower our communities, and build a stronger future for every student, one meeting at a time.

events.title: Granville County Democratic Party Monthly Meeting
events.description:
Join us for the 2026 Granville County Democratic Party's Monthly Meeting! This is your opportunity to build grassroots power in your community, elect precinct leadership, and strengthen our Democratic movement ahead of critical upcoming elections.

At this meeting, we will:

✅ Hear from local leaders
✅ Learn about upcoming training and voter outreach opportunities

**Our June Meeting** will be a meet-and-greet with our awesome new state senator &2026 candidate, Sen. Haseeb Fatmi! Come out & get to know our representation, eat some good food, and mingle with likeminded friends! Come meet your neighbors, get involved, and help build a stronger, more organized Democratic Party.

Your participation is essential! North Carolina elections are decided by just a handful of votes per precinct, and your engagement makes the difference. 

---

Our JULY meeting will shift to a Saturday afternoon Adopt-a-Voter training luncheon. Join us for a training luncheon on Adopt-A-Voter, a voter outreach method that is outperforming every traditional tactic we have. 

Here's how it works: each volunteer is assigned about 15 low-propensity, left-leaning, but low-propensity voters from the voter file. You reach out on a regular schedule—by postcard, text, handwritten note, whatever feels like you—& you keep showing up for them between now & Election Day. You're not a stranger knocking on a door. You become a consistent presence. Someone they recognize. Someone who gave them a reason to show up.

You don't have to live in Granville County to do this. Out-of-state & out-of-district volunteers are welcome—& needed.

At this training, we'll cover: 
-How Adopt-A-Voter works & what the data shows 
-How to reach your 15 voters in a way that's sustainable 
-What's worked in the pilot—& what hasn't 
-How to become a Super Volunteer & coach a team of your own

Lunch will be provided. Space is limited, so please register so we know how many to expect.

North Carolina has a 12.6-point turnout gap between unaffiliated voters & Republicans. Those are our voters. They just don't know yet that someone's coming for them—in the best possible way.

Come learn how to be that someone.

---

💙 Let’s get organized and WIN in 2026!

RSVP now to be part of the movement!

Led by an Executive Council, comprised of students just like us, we believe that diversity is a strength, and that only when everyone has a seat at the table can we build an effective movement to prevent all gun violence in all communities.

events.title: Food Scraps Collection: Encino Farmers' Market
events.description:
As a volunteer, you’ll be right in the action, collecting food scraps from market-goers—the first step in a crucial process that turns waste into nutrient-rich compost. These scraps, gathered at local markets, are then processed at nearby green parks or gardens. Throughout your shift, you'll be guided by an experienced LA Compost staff member, who will act as your Compost Manager, offering insights and helping you share the benefits of composting with the public. The best part is that during your volunteer shift, you can take some time to shop at the market. Join us and be part of the composting movement that's transforming LA—one food scrap at a time!

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:
As a volunteer, you’ll play a hands-on role in guiding market-goers through the composting process, ensuring their food scraps are sticker-free, compostable, and ready to be turned into nutrient-rich compost. You’ll monitor for contamination, assist with tracking data, and serve as a friendly, welcoming host to our composting community. 

#### MORE INFO: 

* You'll be stationed at the LA Compost booth under a pop-up canopy within the farmers' market. There will also be seating available.
* You may be asked to assist with moving filled bins of material weighing 60+ pounds. We always offer team lifts; you will never be asked to lift bins if you prefer not to.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome!
* Bathrooms are accessible.
* If you sign up, please show up! We rely on volunteers like you to achieve our mission.  
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT: 
VOLUNTEER WAIVER: Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. Access the e-waiver at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver

CODE OF CONDUCT: All volunteers are expected to adhere to our volunteer code of conduct. Please visit https://www.lacompost.org/codeofconduct to review.

events.title: Team ENOUGH Welcome Session (For Young People Under 26)
events.description:
Are you a young person between 13 and 25 years old who is interested in taking action around preventing gun violence? Join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session to learn more about the different ways you can engage.

Team ENOUGH is a youth-led program whose mission is to educate young voices about gun violence and mobilize them to take meaningful action against it. Supported by Brady United, we harness the expertise and experience of today’s youth to advance our intersectional work across the country.

Led by an Executive Council, comprised of students just like us, we believe that diversity is a strength, and that only when everyone has a seat at the table can we build an effective movement to prevent all gun violence in all communities.

For us, preventing gun violence not only requires regulating access to firearms but also addressing how systemic racism and environmental factors cause this form of bloodshed to run especially rampant in communities of color. You cannot talk about gun violence without talking about police brutality, white supremacy, the broken criminal justice system, poverty, homophobia, access to affordable housing, or the often barriers separating disadvantaged populations from physical and mental healthcare.

So if you share this belief, join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session and become part of the movement to end gun violence in our lifetime.

events.title: AndersonDems Non-Fiction Book Club
events.description:
Join us for our Non-Fiction Book Club — a laid-back, come-as-you-are space to read, think, and talk about the real world with good people.

Each month we pick one nonfiction title (history, politics, organizing, biography, science — anything that helps us make sense of what’s happening) and spend about an hour swapping takeaways, questions, and “wait… did you catch that part?” moments.

No pressure: you do not have to finish the whole book to join the discussion. Bring your notes, your curiosity, and a friend. We’ll kick off with a quick recap, then open it up for conversation.

Choose a time that works for you: we’re hosting two identical sessions of the same book on the same day — 2:00 PM (afternoon) and 6:30 PM (evening).

2026 Book List

- January: Lawless — Leah Litman
- February: Separation of Church and Hate — John Fugelsang
- March: How to Stand Up to a Dictator — Maria Ressa
-  April: Democracy Awakening: Notes on the State of America — Heather Cox Richardson
- May: Giving Up Is Unforgivable — Joyce Vance
- June: Liar's Kingdom — Andrew Weismann
- July: Vigilante Nation: How State-Sponsored Terror Threatens Our Democracy — David N. Hurd and Jon D. Michaels
- August: The Death of Expertise — Tom Nichols

2025 Highlights: On Tyranny (Timothy Snyder) • The 1619 Project (ed. Nicole Hannah-Jones) • Navalny (Alexei Navalny) • Rediscovery of America (Ned Blackhawk) • Nexus (Yuval Noah Harari) • On Freedom (Timothy Snyder) • Who Is Government? (ed. Michael Lewis) • Erasing History (Jason Stanley) • Science Under Siege (Michael E. Mann)

events.title: Food Scraps Collection: Burbank Farmers Market
events.description:
As a volunteer, you’ll be right in the action, collecting food scraps from market-goers—the first step in a crucial process that turns waste into nutrient-rich compost. These scraps, gathered at local markets, are then processed at nearby green parks or gardens. Throughout your shift, you'll be guided by an experienced LA Compost staff member, who will act as your Compost Manager, offering insights and helping you share the benefits of composting with the public. The best part is that during your volunteer shift, you can take some time to shop at the market. Join us and be part of the composting movement that's transforming LA—one food scrap at a time!

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:
As a volunteer, you’ll play a hands-on role in guiding market-goers through composting, ensuring their food scraps are clean of stickers, compostable, and ready to be turned into nutrient-rich compost. You’ll monitor for contamination, assist with tracking data, and serve as a friendly, welcoming host to our composting community. 

#### MORE INFO: 
* You'll be stationed at the LA Compost booth under a pop-up canopy within the farmers' market. There will also be seating available.
* You may be asked to assist with moving filled bins of material weighing 60+ pounds. We always offer team lifts; you will never be asked to lift bins if you prefer not to.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome!
* Bathrooms are available
* If you sign up, please show up! We rely on volunteers like you to achieve our mission.  
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT: 
VOLUNTEER WAIVER: Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. Access the e-waiver at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver

CODE OF CONDUCT: All volunteers are expected to adhere to our volunteer code of conduct. Please visit https://www.lacompost.org/codeofconduct to review.

events.title: Sign-up For Democracy Action Network / Indivisible LA
events.description:
The Democracy Action Network (DAN) was founded in November 2024 by David Comfort in response to the re-election of Donald Trump. Emerging as a grassroots organization dedicated to defending democratic institutions, promoting civic engagement, and fostering inclusive democracy, DAN has quickly become a prominent force in the pro-democracy movement. With a nonpartisan ethos and a commitment to nonviolent resistance, DAN seeks to address threats to constitutional governance while building a broad-based coalition for democratic renewal.

Mission and Vision
DAN’s mission is to protect and strengthen democratic institutions, resist authoritarian tendencies, and promote an inclusive vision of democracy that upholds universal human rights and dignity. The organization operates on the principles of nonviolence, transparency, and participatory decision-making while fostering hope-centered messaging and constructive solutions. It aims to create sustainable organizing structures that empower communities and build long-term resilience against democratic backsliding.

Early Achievements
Since its inception, DAN has demonstrated its capacity for impactful action:

- February 22nd 2025: Organized a successful march and rally in West Hollywood, drawing hundreds of participants advocating for government accountability and democratic principles
.
- February 2025: Played a key role in coordinating protests at SpaceX, bringing attention to issues tied to corporate influence and public policy.

- Held weekly organizing meetings with 300 to 400 people attending.
- Developing a core group of activists and organizers

- March 22nd 2025: Held a really successful "March for our Constitution" at the Federal Building in Westwood / Los Angeles. Had over 2,000 participants and hosted speakers such as Martin Sheen and Maxine Waters


These events have helped establish DAN as a credible voice for democratic activism while galvanizing public support for its mission.

events.description:
When you sign up for this event, you’ll receive an email from **welcome@newletter.socialists.us** domain titled *“Instructions for the Upcoming SDA Zoom.”*

Please open it as soon as it arrives and acknowledge it. If you don’t see the email right away, be sure to check your spam folder.

Acknowledging this message is important — without it, you won’t be able to fully participate in our activities, since most of our coordination happens by email.

# Who are we?

We are a faction within the Democratic Party, and we consider ourselves both **Democrats** and **Socialists**.

**This group is not a space for discussing leaving the Democratic Party**. If that is your goal or perspective, this organization is probably not the right fit for you. 

We are active members of our local Democratic Clubs, and this space is dedicated to learning how to navigate and work effectively within the Democratic Party.

The agenda for the meeting is available here: https://socialists.us/direct/list/agenda?ZoomAgenda. 

We’ll be happy to answer any questions about our Manifesto and how it is built from the bottom up. You can read the Manifesto here: https://socialists.us/manifesto.

## We are Socialists

therefore, we believe in Free Education, Universal Health Care, Anti-Death Penalty, Pro-Abortion, Universal Basic Income, the Right to Unionize, the sanctity of the Separation of Church and State, and the belief that the Government should make life bearable for all and ensure citizens' Liberties.

events.title: Four Corners in Lenexa  Standing Rally
events.description: As citizens, we can’t let the policies and actions of the Federal Government and unelected billionaires be normalized, but we can only stop what’s going on by coming together.  A STANDING RALLY  will draw attention to the situation, encouraging our neighbors to join with us. We will rally every Saturday morning from 11 AM – 12 PM.  Stay for the full hour or come by when and for how long you can. We will peacefully line the sidewalk on all four corners of 87th Parkway and Maurer Road,  holding signs on issues that are most meaningful to us or just simply standing in support of our neighbors and our country.  If sitting is more comfortable for you, you are very welcome to bring mobility or lawn chairs!! There is room for everyone!
events.accessibility_notes:
Please be especially mindful of parking.  For example, if you live relatively nearby, please consider walking.  If you drive, there is street parking on the residential streets to the north and also a bit further on the south.  About ½ mile down on the west, there is a large civic campus garage at 17201 W 87th St. Pkwy.  In addition, on the SE, SW, and NW sides of the intersection, there are restaurants and shops with big, but commercially owned parking lots meant for customers, if you are one. Note that Lenexa Point on the NW side has recently put up signs, saying they will tow non-customer cars.  If you cross from one side of the street to another during the rally, please pay particular attention to cars turning right as you cross! 
Participants should bring their own signs (if they want to hold them).  Note that sticks supporting the signs can’t be pointed at either end.  Also, in designing content for the signs, please remember that children will be present.  Please stand only along the sidewalks parallel to the street and not on the grass.  However, also be sure to allow pedestrian access to the sidewalk and businesses.   We are not expecting issues, but keep in mind that a core principle behind our events is a commitment to nonviolent action.  Remember to de-escalate any potential confrontation with someone, who disagrees with you. And of course, follow directions from our excellent Lenexa police, if asked. We will not have speakers (but do expect lots of cars with horn honking in agreement). Finally, please note that all our organizers will be wearing lanyards and neon vests, if you have questions. See you soon.  Let’s show our neighbors “what Democracy Looks Like”!!
P.S.  If you want to post an inspiring (!) story about your experience, please add #FourCornersLenexa to your post!

events.title: Pop up demonstration for the protection of OUR Constitution

address_lines: West Genesee Street & West Lake Street

events.description:
To protectors of the US Constitution,

Mark Twain wrote, “Patriotism is supporting your country all of the time and your government when it deserves it”. We currently have a government regime led by a cruel, corrupt, lawless pathological liar supported by a group of authoritarian gaslighting sycophants. This regime does not deserve our support. It deserves our resistance!

The Framers of the U.S. Constitution created the Bill of Rights and placed Freedom of Assembly, Speech, and Petition of government grievances in the First Amendment in order for action to be taken in times like these.

EVERY SINGLE DAY this regime is violating our Constitution. This regime is invading sovereign countries. Masked lawless federal “agents” are kidnapping our neighbors and now killing citizens in our neighborhoods.

To be clear, we respect and appreciate ethical and community-minded law enforcement officers. We RESIST brutality, lawlessness, and lack of accountability by ICE.

This rally is part of a campaign of weekly “pop-up” rallies at various locations throughout Onondaga County. New weekly location will be announced every Monday for that Saturday. Raise your voice with a community of protectors of the Constitution and human rights by peacefully assembling together to exercise our First Amendment rights!

In the influential footsteps of Gandhi,  Dr. King, Thich Nhat Hahn, and Susan B Anthony, non-violence is not only a strategy for direct action to save our democracy, but a shared value in our personal conduct. We are a peaceful, yet assertive movement. Any suggestion otherwise is propaganda. We denounce political violence in the clearest and strongest possible terms. 

Additionally, we are an organization of VOLUNTEER activists, organizers, concerned community members, and other protectors of our Constitution. We care about our community and our country. We RESIST authoritarianism from the megalomaniac in the White House. We are NOT paid. Any suggestion otherwise is propaganda. 

Dealing with counter-protestors:

We have the First Amendment right of peaceful assembly free of threat or intimidation. We value a safe, welcoming, inclusive, and family-friendly atmosphere when we assemble to celebrate our Constitution.

Sadly, some of our neighbors do not value the First Amendment as we do and will approach us with taunts and hostility. Do NOT take the bait. Do not engage. Ignore them. It denies them the attention that they want.

Our power does not come from escalating with those who seek to disrupt our celebration of our Constitution. Our collective power comes from adherence to truth and morality, from the care of our neighbors, and from our discipline and dedication in saving our democracy. Stay focused on our goals. Take comfort knowing that all of our actions are in alignment our Constitution.

If you ever feel threatened by counter-protestors, don’t hesitate to call the police.

In the words of Dr. King, “Darkness cannot drive out darkness; only light can do that. Hate cannot drive out hate; only love can do that”.

events.title: Welcome to SURJ: Find Your Place and Take Action
events.description:
Are you a white person who is fed up with the current administration, committed to fighting racism, but not sure where to start? Join us to learn more about Showing Up for Racial Justice (SURJ) the largest organization in the US that explicitly brings together white people to fight racism and injustice.

On this one hour call we will:

- Get a short orientation to SURJ, meet people who are new, and hear from people who have been organizing with us for awhile. 

- Make sense of the current state of the world right now.

- Learn how to take action: join our Block by Block campaign, join our phonebanks to elect progressive candidates, find a chapter or circle near you, and make plans to take action in your own community.

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Our Harvest Farm Coop works out of a historic farm property in College Hill, and we have been working with them since 2018 when our local gleaning project started in Cincinnati. We currently have weekly events for this season at their College Hill location, starting at the end of June.  [*It's possible we will do gleanings at their other location in Warren County at some point during the season, and will create separate events if/when those happen.*]

Gleaning involves harvesting food that will not go to market, but is still good food. We then get it distributed right away to a local hunger relief recipient.

The work will happen in the farm's fields in a variety of weather. It may involve bending/stooping, some heavy lifting, and generally getting dirty. The extent of these conditions will vary each time.

Once registered, volunteers will receive specific instructions about where to meet at the farm, and any other pertinent details, in a confirmation email.

We will have a food drive benefiting Interfaith Community Services in Escondido the last Friday of every month. Please bring non-perishable, new food items. https://interfaithservices.org/

events.title: Community Connections: In-Person Phone-Banking With Equality Florida!
events.description:
Help Engage New Volunteers and Forge New Community Connections!

Do you want to help grow Florida LGBTQ+ people power and connect with other members of the community? Pride month is here, and that means we’re recruiting more volunteers than any other time of the year. That means we need dedicated volunteers like you to help ensure these new volunteers are plugged into the work!

We will be calling newly registered volunteers and helping them navigate their journey as a volunteer. Since phone banking is vital to the growth of any movement, this is an excellent chance not only to meet like-minded peers and build queer people power, but also develop valuable skills for activist work.

We will be providing free food and drinks!!

Don't have experience phonebanking? No problem!
Whether you're a veteran phone banker or have never tried it, we NEED your help! We will provide training for inexperienced phone bankers to ensure you start making calls with confidence!

events.title: NO NUKES VIGIL - Every Friday
events.description: The Santa Fe chapter of Veterans For Peace started this vigil in 2002 and have continued it every Friday at noon for 23 years. Its purpose is to bring awareness to the hundreds of billions of our tax dollars going to the production of new nuclear weapons here in our state. Many people, even many New Mexicans, are unaware that Los Alamos National Lab is currently building several new bomb factories to increase production of nuclear bomb cores (known as plutonium "pits") to reach a goal of 30 to 120 new pits per year. Each pit, on average, has the destructive power of 20 Hiroshima-sized bombs. Loud public outcry may be able to halt this waste of federal money, or at least slow it down until we elect a saner administration. Life on Earth is at stake.

events.title: Write Postcards for Democracy
events.description:
## Join Indivisible Greater Vancouver to write postcards for democracy!

**Thank you to the dedicated postcard writing volunteers who have written 9700+ postcards to get out the vote for the November 3 election!**
All of our postcards have been mailed. We wrote to voters in Ohio, Iowa, Texas, Maine, Alaska, and Michigan to get out the vote for Senate candidates. Research shows that postcards can increase Dem turnout by up to 1.3%, so we're making a difference!

Here's the plan going forward. All meetings at New Seasons (2100B SE 164th Ave, Vancouver):

*Saturday 10/31 - casual chat about last-minute GOTV ideas

*Wednesday 11/4 and Saturday 11/7 - meet to discuss election results (that's the last scheduled Wed. meeting)

*Saturday 11/14 and 11/21 - meet in case there's disputed election results and there are actions we can take

*Break through holidays until Saturday 1/9/27 - we'll start writing postcards to elected officials

 Thanks so much for all you do to defend democracy!

events.title: Food Scraps Collection: Culver City Farmers' Market
events.description:
As a volunteer, you’ll be right in the action, collecting food scraps from market-goers—the first step in a crucial process that turns waste into nutrient-rich compost. These scraps, gathered at local markets, are then processed at nearby green parks or gardens. Throughout your shift, you'll be guided by an experienced LA Compost staff member, who will act as your Compost Manager, offering insights and helping you share the benefits of composting with the public. The best part is that during your volunteer shift, you can take some time to shop at the market. Join us and be part of the composting movement that's transforming LA—one food scrap at a time!

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:
As a volunteer, you’ll play a hands-on role in guiding market-goers through composting, ensuring their food scraps are clean of stickers, compostable, and ready to be turned into nutrient-rich compost. You’ll monitor for contamination, assist with tracking data, and serve as a friendly, welcoming host to our composting community. 

#### MORE INFO: 
* You'll be stationed at the LA Compost booth under a pop-up canopy within the farmers' market. There will also be seating available.
* You may be asked to assist with moving filled bins of material weighing 60+ pounds. We always offer team lifts; you will never be asked to lift bins if you prefer not to.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome!
* Bathrooms are accessible
* If you sign up, please show up! We rely on volunteers like you to achieve our mission.  
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT: 
VOLUNTEER WAIVER: Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. You can access the e-waiver at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver 

CODE OF CONDUCT: All volunteers are expected to adhere to our volunteer code of conduct. Please visit https://www.lacompost.org/codeofconduct to review.

events.title: Stand Up, Speak Out: El Segundo Monthly Rally.
events.description:
Join us at the corner of Main & Imperial to protest the inhumane actions of the Trump administration!

This will be a family-friendly, dog-friendly, non-violent, no-vandalism, community event. We'll be staying on the grassy areas and out of the roads. Please keep it friendly, and if there is any negativity or counter-protestors, don't engage. We'll have folks on hand who can help de-escalate any situation if necessary.

What this event is:

* This is a stationary, “honk and wave” visibility event at a location that sees a lot of weekend traffic. Bring signs!

* This is a positive, peaceful, community-focused, and family- and dog-friendly event.

What this event is not:

* This is not a march, and there is no programming/planned speaker.

* This is not a civil disobedience event. We will not block roads, sidewalks, or the entrances of any buildings.

* We will not be engaging with any hecklers. The El Segundo Police Department is aware of the event and available to help assist to keep everyone safe if there are counter-protestors.

There are many other Indivisible events across LA, so if this doesn't sound like what you're looking for, please feel free to attend a different event.

Details:

* 10:30 AM to 12 PM

* Grassy area in front of the El Segundo sign at the corner of Main & Imperial in El Segundo. We will expand to the grassy area across Main if necessary.

* There is street parking along Imperial Avenue (not Imperial Highway) within El Segundo, as well as on the surrounding streets south of Imperial Ave.

* Please do not park illegally (i.e. blocking driveways or in the local businesses’ lots). We want to bring people in to our movement, not turn them off!

*Unfortunately, this location is not very accessible by public transportation. The 109 bus runs very sporadically, especially on the weekend. If you do plan to use public transit, we recommend you check on the possibility of using the Metro Micro service from the nearby Metro stations. We are a small, grassroots group of volunteers and are unfortunately unable to organize rides or fund taxis for you.

We can't wait to see you. We are looking forward to making our voices heard together!
This a local Indivisible event!

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*
events.accessibility_notes:
Safety first! Cars drive very fast on Imperial Highway, including in the right turn lane onto Main St. into El Segundo. For your safety, stay on the greenway (out of the street, out of the bike lane, and back from the curb). Be very careful when crossing the street and standing on corners.

We know it can get exciting out there, and tempting to step forward to make sure people see your sign, but please resist the temptation. Please look out for your fellow protestors as well.

By attending this event, you acknowledge the risks involved in attending, commit to participate non-violently and in accordance with the law, and to de-escalate any confrontations that may occur. You agree that you are solely responsible for any injury or damage to your person or property resulting from your event attendance; and to release, hold harmless and indemnify the organizers from all liabilities, claims and damages you incur through your attendance at the event.

events.description:
In honor of John Lewis Day, our teach-in examines how systemic racism drives and sustains the crisis of gun violence in communities of color. Far from random, this violence is rooted in decades of policy decisions, from redlining and housing segregation to underfunded social services and unequal law enforcement.

In this video training, we will explore how these interconnected systems have created conditions where gun violence thrives, making it a powerful form of racial injustice, and dive into how President Trump’s policies and funding cuts have exacerbated these inequalities. Join us to uncover the structural forces behind the headlines and carry forward John Lewis’s legacy by demanding lasting, systemic change, civil rights for all, and a democracy that works for everyone.

The training is given by Rachelle Hunley, Brady's Senior Director of Strategic Engagement, Aalayah Eastmond, our Cultural Community Engagement Manager, and JP Thomas, our Director of Organizing.

events.title: Weekly Vigil for Democracy at the Brooklyn Metropolitan Detention Center
events.description:
Join us in standing up for our neighbors, held at the notorious prison in our own back yard. For years, the Metropolitan Detention Center has had a reputation for inhumane conditions: rancid food, lack of heating in winter and oppressive heat in summer. In 2020, an inmate named Jamel Floyd was killed by corrections officers by excessive use of force. Now, ICE is using the Metropolitan Detention Center to house our immigrant neighbors -- mothers, fathers, sons and daughters -- who have been taken from their homes, schools, and workplaces and held in detention.

Our fellow organizers at Good Shepherd Lutheran Church in Bay Ridge are holding for a weekly vigil outside the MDC to call for the release of ICE detainees, and to stand against the inhumane treatment of our neighbors. Supporters are invited to bring signs, to sing or play music, and to solemnly bear witness in solidarity. Together we will build and strengthen the vital community connections.

* We gather first at the corner of 3rd Avenue and 29th Street.

events.description:
Across the country, families are feeling the consequences of federal overreach. From attacks on due process and civil liberties to efforts to silence the free press and limit public access to information, these actions threaten the foundation of our democracy.

Everyday people are paying the price while those in power play political games with our rights and freedoms. These are not just policy choices; they are moral decisions that test who we are as a nation and whether we will stand up for justice, truth, and accountability.

Democracy dies in the dark. Now is the time to raise our voices, defend our rights, and demand transparency and fairness from those who claim to lead in our name.

Join us every Thursday outside the Federal Building (880 Front Street, San Diego) to demand that Washington fund care — not chaos. Together, we can send a clear message:

Gather at 10:30am and speaking program begins at 11:00am

• Healthcare is a human right.

This is more than a protest! It’s a stand for dignity, justice, and the right of every family to live free from fear. Bring your friends, your signs, and your voice. events.title: IND Cobb - Board of Commissioner (BOC) Meetings
events.description:
Join our IND Cobb member liaisons who regularly attend the BOC meetings because all politics is local, and this has never been more true. Here's why you should start plugging in to local politics.

County commissioners make real decisions that affect your daily life - like taxes, law enforcement budgets, zoning, public health, and infrastructure. Yet most people never show up. Here’s why you should:

🔎 Accountability
When you’re in the room, it is harder for officials to make shady or unpopular decisions. 

🗣️ Your Voice Matters
At the local level, one person speaking up can actually shift policy. Commissioners notice when people show up - especially when they speak. But you don't have to speak. Your presence alone speaks volumes and our Democratic majority of Commissioners appreciate you making the effort to attend.

💰 They Control Your Tax Dollars
Millions in public funds are decided here. Want better services or to stop wasteful spending? This is where to start.

🔥 They Count on You Staying Home
Most meetings are empty. Your presence alone disrupts that status quo and reminds them who they work for.

🏛️ Local is Where Big Change Begins
Many bad (or good) policies start at the county level - like surveillance, book bans, or housing rules. Spot them early, and fight back locally.

Bottom Line:
If you don’t show up - they assume you don’t care.
Be there. Speak up. Keep them honest. Start with a Regular Meeting until you feel comfortable going to more.

events.title: Unite for Freedom
events.description:
📢 Gather with Indivisible Salmon Creek/Hazel Dell as we stand strong in defense of our freedoms. 

📍Join us at the northeast corner of NE 139th St & NE 20th Ave (near Walgreens) in the Salmon Creek area of Vancouver, WA.

⏰ We'll rally weekly from 3:00 - 4:00 pm. 

📅 Join us Thursday November 5, November 12, and November 19.

🪧 Bring a sign that reminds us all to defend FDR’s Four Freedoms: freedom of speech and expression, freedom of worship, freedom from want, and freedom from fear—or borrow one of ours. 

 ❤️💙 More importantly, bring a friend, and bring your joy.

💪 Your safety is our top concern. If you need assistance, please reach out to the organizers. If you are concerned about your ability to stand or walk outside during hot temperatures, please stay home!

🌡️ Even as temperatures rise, your safety remains our priority. If the weather forecast predicts a temperature of 90º or higher, the rally is automatically cancelled.

✊ As a reminder: IGV believes that nonviolent activism is the most powerful forced for lasting change. Peaceful protest allows us to make our voices heard with dignity, rooted in truth. We do not condone intimidation, threats, vandalism, blocking access to businesses or any other lawless actions.
If instigators or opponents attempt to break this commitment we will work to de-escalate—and, if necessary, end the event to protect everyone’s safety.

You can read more about Indivisible’s national commitment to nonviolence here:
🔗 indivisible.org/commitment-nonviolence

We also value and are guided by the research of Dr. Erica Chenoweth, whose work shows that nonviolent movements are significantly more successful than violent ones in achieving lasting social and political transformation:
🔗 Paths to Resistance – Harvard Kennedy School

Together, we stand strong, peaceful, and resolute—because nonviolence is not passive. It is powerful.

events.title: PA: Municipal Ordinance Project Resident Working Group
events.description:
Join Food & Water Watch’s **Municipal Ordinance Project (MOP)**  organizers for a resident-led working group focused on using **Pennsylvania-specific** local zoning laws to protect our environment, health, and neighborhoods.

We’ll explore how **Pennsylvania-specific** municipal zoning and land-use ordinances can help keep harmful industries out of our communities — and how everyday people like you can lead the charge.

Working group meetings can include:

* Q&A with experienced MOP organizers
* Time to connect and strategize with your neighbors
* Info on how local governments can use zoning to protect residents from threats like fracking, pipelines, heavy industry, and more.
* Trainings on topics such as how to read/write ordinances, or how to build and leading a local ordinance campaign

Whether you're a long-time advocate or just getting started, this is your chance to plug into a powerful local movement, supported by the team behind some of the most effective grassroots zoning victories in Pennsylvania!

**After you RSVP, please review the "How to Prepare" section of your confirmation email that contains pertinent background info on PA zoning that'll better prepare you for our meeting together!**

*Please note: This working group is intended for residents and local grassroots organizers who are interested in working within their own municipality or county to advance zoning or ordinance-based protections. If you're not sure whether this applies to you, feel free to attend and ask!*

events.title: Demand Your Representative Support the We the People Amendment (H.J.Res.54)
events.description:
**Corporate money is corrupting our democracy, and our lawmakers know it.**

For decades, billionaires, lobbyists, and big business have bought access and influence while everyday people are ignored. Through a combination of court rulings like Citizens United and unchecked loopholes, our political system has become rigged in favor of the ultra-wealthy.

The We the People Amendment (H.J.Res.54) is a bold, constitutional solution to take our government back.

For years, Congress has failed to rein in big money, hiding behind weak bills and partisan gridlock. The Supreme Court opened the floodgates with atrocious decisions like Citizens United, and our lawmakers have done next to nothing to stop it.

This amendment pulls no punches. It:
- Declares that constitutional rights belong only to human beings, not artificial entities, including corporations and PACs
- Establishes that money is not speech, giving the people the power to regulate campaign spending
- Requires full transparency of all political expenditures—no more dark money, no more secrets

This amendment is backed by a massive majority of Americans across party lines—**more than 80%**. But Congress continues to delay, deflect, and protect the very system that enriches them. **We the people are fed up.**

**That’s where you come in.**

We're building a movement to demand change and to hold every lawmaker accountable who stands in the way. Use this form to send a powerful message to your elected officials demanding they cosponsor, publicly support, and advance H.J.Res.54. **It takes just one minute to make your voice heard, but the impact is real.**

**We're done waiting. Flood their inboxes. Flood the streets. Let’s take our country back.**

# The Underground: LIVE FREE California Statewide Organizing Huddle  
## Gather. Plot. Move.  

The Underground is where California comes to **plot repair, representation, and power.**  

**Thursdays at 5-7 PM PT**, this statewide huddle brings communities together in rhythm:  

- **Repair** → The fight for real repair: land, housing, education, dignity, and the policies that make them real.  
- **Representation** → More than one election—this is about voice, maps, votes, and defending democracy itself.  
- **Training** → From pulpits to campuses to neighborhoods, we sharpen skills and multiply actions until they echo statewide.  

## Join LIVE FREE CA for The Underground: Statewide Organizing Huddle

**Every third Thursday · 5-7 PM PT · Zoom (Statewide)**  
Register once → [livefreeusa.org/events](https://www.livefreeusa.org/events)

Join **LIVE FREE CA** for **The Underground** — our statewide huddle where we turn moments into movements.

This is where communities across California come together to meet the moment, build power, and move for repair, representation, and justice. The Underground is where faith leaders, organizers, and neighbors align around what’s happening now and how we act together.

Our rhythm is simple and powerful: **Ground → Educate → Act.**  
**Ground** in truth, reflection, and the stories that root us in community.  
**Educate** through training and awareness—tools, definitions, and analysis that connect lived experience to systems change.  
**Act** together in real time—taking collective steps that show what organized people can do.

Everything we do centers three pillars:  
**Repair. Representation. Power.**

**Repair** means care, safety, and economic dignity in our communities.  
**Representation** means voice, visibility, and civic participation.  
**Power** means organizing people, resources, and ideas to transform systems at their root.

**Bring two people. Take two actions.**

events.title: K(now) Y(our) R(ights) Business Outreach

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Join us for a business canvassing shift! Small businesses are a key pillar of our immigrant communities. We need your help to ensure that their employees are armed with the knowledge and resources to respond appropriately if ICE comes to their business. No prior experience is required; we will begin with a 30-minute training session.

Working in pairs, block by block, we will meet with owners, managers, and employees at their business establishments. We use multilingual, legally vetted materials to ensure they know how to protect themselves now, what to do if ICE comes, what to do in case of detentions, and where to find additional resources. Foreign language skills (especially Spanish) are helpful, but not required.

Canvassers should expect to visit a wide variety of businesses; "business casual" attire is preferred. Wear comfortable shoes and expect to carry a tote bag weighing a few pounds.

This action is rooted in principles of cooperation, empathy, and collective action.  Effective community care involves building networks of mutual support and empowering ourselves (community members!!) to meet our collective needs.

events.description:
Work with others to stand up for democracy and resist fascism. Our times call for concerted, communal, and local action. Come to our monthly meeting to connect and get involved!

Indivisible is a national movement of thousands of group leaders and more than a million members taking regular, iterative, and increasingly complex actions to resist the GOPs agenda, elect local champions, and fight for progressive policies.

Lancaster Together is one of several local chapters. Each chapter has its own flavor and we all work together on bigger projects. You can join any or all of them -- whatever works best for you. Our chapter meeting is in East Hempfield and many members live in Lancaster City, Lancaster Township, and parts south and west, although we welcome anyone from any part of the county.

We organize protests and rallies, hold our elected officials to account, speak up and support those who can't, and most of all, work together with other Indivisible chapters and mission-aligned local and national partners to increase our impact. All of our activity is meant to spread awareness and make change happen.

Most of our day-to-day work takes place OUTSIDE of our monthly meeting. You can start a new project right away, or join an existing effort. But the meeting is the best way to meet everyone and see what your role can be. We use it to update, connect, onboard, discuss, and decide. We also promise it will last only ONE hour.

##Here are five things to know about our grassroots organization:

- **We Are Indivisible** We are stronger in unity. We emphasize partnerships and collaboration to stand in solidarity with those most affected by right-wing policies, while also seeking to build awareness about and change those policies.

- **Strong Leaders, Strong Groups, Strong Movement** Indivisible is decentralized, fostering leadership at the local level. Our volunteers can lead and take independent action, while coordinating with national campaigns for maximum impact.

- **Inside/Outside Strategy** We engage with existing political structures while simultaneously applying pressure from the outside. This dual approach involves working within systems like Congress while mobilizing grassroots pressure on elected officials to advance progressive goals.

- **A Virtuous Cycle of Advocacy and Elections** We believe in electing progressive candidates and progressive policies. We hold our elected officials to account and work to elect progressive candidates who can resist tyranny and promote democracy.

- **A Real Democracy** The organization is driven by a vision of a democracy that serves everyone. We aim to defeat right-wing political agendas and build an inclusive democracy that reflects the needs and values of all people.

- **Nonviolence** A core principle behind all Indivisible activity is a commitment to nonviolence.

*If these principles align with your values, please join us!*

events.title: No Kings Westfield Weekly Standout
events.description:
## Our Mission 

No Kings Westfield: Defending democracy through nonviolent action, uniting community to reject authoritarianism, and affirming that power belongs to the people.

## Invitation and Affirmation

All who believe in our mission are welcome to join us and by doing so
affirm that violence and intimidation are never a solution – not on a nation-to
nation level and not on a person-to person level – and all of us agree to
conduct ourselves accordingly.

## Every Week!

We vigil every Tuesday in Park Square until someone takes the oath of Presidential office who does not seek to be a king!


### Our Commitment
No Kings Westfield is committed to peaceful, lawful resistance. We defend democracy through the power of organized community action, not confrontation.

### Core Principles
  - Non-violent resistance is strategically effective

  - De-escalation protects our movement, our community, and our message

  - Peaceful persistence builds the broad coalition needed for lasting change

### At Events

  - Remain calm and composed, even when provoked

  - Do not engage with counter-protesters or hecklers

  - If tensions arise, step back and find an organizer

  - Our strength comes from disciplined unity, not individual reactions

  - Remember: we're modeling the democracy we seek to protect

### Why This Matters

Research shows non-violent movements are twice as likely to succeed as violent ones. Every act of discipline strengthens our cause and our community.

### If Confronted

"We're here peacefully exercising our constitutional rights to defend democracy. Thank you for your concern."

  Questions or concerns? Contact an organizer immediately.

### We stand out in Westfield:

To show our neighbors they are not alone

To show our neighbors we will not be silent in the face of authoritarianism

To build community and resiliency with existing organizations

All are welcome. Please refrain from profanity on signs.



[Parking](https://www.cityofwestfield.org/DocumentCenter/View/1575/AMENDED-Parking-Lot-Locations?bidId=)

Contact us: contact@nokingswestfield.com

events.title: Roadside Rallies Against Fascism
events.description:
Join us for another Roadside Rally Against Fascism down in Bellmawr at the corner of Black Horse Pike and E Browning Road.

UPDATE: Recently, our rally has been unfairly targeted by local police. One person was arrested for disorderly conduct while lawfully recording a traffic stop, and several citations have been issued for trumped-up infractions such as: excessive honking while operating a vehicle; jaywalking; disregarding stop signs; and trespassing.

Please record any police activity you witness and notify us ASAP (especially regarding Officer Sarin, who is deeply frightened by traffic control boxes and nice old ladies). Allow the rally leaders and safety marshals to take point on interacting with the police. Say as little as possible to the police if they speak to you, and only comply with their orders to the minimal extent as required by law. Remember that New Jersey is not a "stop and identify" state, and you are only required to provide your ID if you are being detained on reasonable suspicion of a crime (i.e. whatever crime the officers decide to invent). Here is a link to some useful info from the ACLU about your rights when interacting with the police:  https://www.aclu.org/know-your-rights/stopped-by-police

Please bring your signs, flags, street antics, and any other ways you can think of to joyfully disturb the peace. But please avoid any messaging that is outright hateful, violent, or discriminatory. Do your best to keep the messaging on target -- Bellmawr PD is a problem, but our real enemy is tyranny as a whole. Eyes on the prize.

There is a good amount of traffic and plenty of sidewalk, and there is parking available on nearby residential streets (make sure not to obstruct the nearby police and fire departments on Lewis Ave). We would love to welcome as many folks as possible to come make some noise with us!

This is a nonviolent demonstration, so please attend with safety and de-escalation in mind. There may be a few counterprotestors, but we can never be 100% sure. Do your best to minimize engagement with hecklers, and don't be too shy to smile and wave at our supporters!

And try to stay out of the street, the cops get triggered by that, too.

See you out there!

events.title: LA Compost's Annual Pumpkin Smash: San Gabriel Valley (1 of 4 Locations!)
events.description:
Don’t Let Your Pumpkin Haunt the Landfill! 🎃🧟‍♂️

Did you know that each year, around **1.3 billion pounds** of pumpkins in the U.S. end up in landfills after Halloween? Without oxygen to help them break down properly, they release methane, a potent greenhouse gas that harms our environment.

Instead of tossing it in the trash, give your pumpkin a second life as compost! Join us at CultivaLA Farm on November 6th from 9 AM to 12 PM for our Annual Pumpkin Smash. Smash, toss, or chop your pumpkin to pieces and feed our compost piles. You’ll cut down on landfill waste and give your pumpkin the chance to return to the Earth!

### What to Expect
-  **Bring Your Own Pumpkin (BYOP)**: Don't have one? You're still welcome to observe or share a pumpkin with another participant. 

-  **Learn & Explore**: Meet our team, tour the farm, and discover how hundreds of pounds of food scraps are transformed into nutrient-rich compost every week. 

-  **Get Involved**: Stick around to volunteer or explore the Compost Hub. No experience necessary!

### Important Information
- **Waiver Required**: All Pumpkin Smash participants must sign a waiver before taking part. Access the e-Waiver here: www.lacompost.org/waiver

- **Age Requirements**: While all ages are welcome to observe, minors under 16 must be accompanied by a parent or guardian.

- **Can't Make it on November 6?** We're hosting Pumpkin Smashes at three other locations! Check out the full schedule and FAQ at: www.lacompost.org/pumpkinsmash

events.title: Weekly 22nd Street Bridge Bannering Over Hwy 94 | Wednesdays
events.description:
We provide large physical messaging in the real world to connect with and activate voters to demonstrate that resistance is possible. Bring a sign for cars on the bridge or just wave to the cars passing below. You can also bring a flag, chair, bubbles, music, or anything else you want in order to have a good time!

Rules and Protocols

1. We avoid doing anything that could either harm ourselves or anyone else. This includes stepping into traffic, holding a sign where it could fall onto cars below, climbing fencing, etc.

2. We must not block pedestrian and bike traffic, so please keep the middle of the overpass and/or sidewalk clear to allow them to pass.

3. We supply the messages, you supply the waves. However, you are welcome to also display your own poster boards. Just avoid any messaging that would be rated above a PG-13.

4. We don’t litter. If we find litter, we pick it up and throw it away.

5. We don’t use stickers or anything that leaves a permanent mark on the overpass. However, chalk is okay and even encouraged.

6. If someone from the ‘opposition’ comes up to talk with us, do not engage with them. Best to just ignore them. One member will be designated to handle them and video record any aggressive interaction so that you can go right on waving.

7. We take lots of pictures and videos during our action for circulation on social media. If you prefer not to be included, please let us know and/or consider wearing a mask.

8. Should law enforcement pay us a visit, only the designated point person from the group should address them.

9. Ignore the middle fingers and negativity coming from some of the cars below. For every one of those confused folks, you are providing hope to another 100 people!

10. The Visibility Brigade is a non-violent, informal volunteer group in which we all participate with an understanding that our own actions are our personal responsibility and we accept our own personal liability. You participate with this understanding.

Feel free to reach out to VisibilityBrigadeSanDiego@gmail.com with any questions.

events.title: Weekly (Fri) Mass Pike Overpass Standout in Westfield - Southampton Rd (Routes 10/202)
events.description:
## Our Mission 

No Kings Westfield: Defending democracy through nonviolent action, uniting community to reject authoritarianism, and affirming that power belongs to the people.

## Invitation and Affirmation

All who believe in our mission are welcome to join us and by doing so
affirm that violence and intimidation are never a solution – not on a nation-to
nation level and not on a person-to person level – and all of us agree to
conduct ourselves accordingly.

## Standout Tips

Please wear highly visible clothing if possible. 

Wow! What a great location for a standout! There's lots and lots of traffic passing by. Southampton Road (Routes 10/202) is heavily traveled northbound and southbound, and the Mass Pike eastbound and westbound is below. Lots of honks and thumbs up and waves...and a few folks flying middle fingers. We smile and wave at them all!

We've discovered that the magic happens when we smile and wave to people!

Come when you can, and leave when you must. You needn't be present for the entire event.

## How to Get There

The address "130 Southampton Road, Westfield" will get you just north of the overpass.

## Parking
We can't park in the Southampton Rd breakdown lane. There are vacant business properties north of the bridge, and we've been warned NOT to park there.

Please park on the north side (the westbound shoulder) of Sgt. Thomas Dion Way, off of Southampton Rd. just north of the Mass Pike.

## Etiquette!
We don't give the finger to people who give the finger to us, or who say unpleasant things. We smile and wave to them, too.

We may see a counter protester. If so, the best thing to do is just ignore them and spend our time and energy waving to motorists. Let's keep things 100% non-confrontational in words and body language.

## Other Stuff
Please take everything you brought away with you, and leave the site totally clean.

If rain is predicted, we'll cancel.

## A Few Requests
We've found that roof rake sections make wonderful flagpoles and banner poles. If you have a roof rake (or 10’-15’ light metal poles or conduit) to contribute, we'll be happy to take it off your hands!

And, if you have an extra 3' x 5' American flag you're not using, we'd love it if you'd pass it on to us!

Join us at the Mesa City Council meeting(s) to advocate for the nullification of ICE and Mesa PD's 287(g) agreement. 

**We want the City of Mesa to withdraw from its 287(g) agreement with the Immigration and Customs Enforcement Agency (ICE) and cease any and all cooperation between ICE and the Mesa PD. Learn more about the agreement here:** 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZfCriBTDrHw
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z9euNT9FjwY (Spanish)

If you are interested in attending the City Council Meeting(s) to support this effort, RSVP using Mobilize.

There were approx. 135 287(g) agreements when Biden left office. There are now 1000+ active agreements in the US and growing under the Trump administration.

events.title: Weekly 22nd Street Bridge Bannering Over Hwy 94 | Wednesday Mornings - Visibility Brigade
events.description:
We provide large physical messaging in the real world to connect with and activate voters to demonstrate that resistance is possible. Bring a sign for cars on the bridge or just wave to the cars passing below. You can also bring a flag, chair, bubbles, music, or anything else you want in order to have a good time!

Rules and Protocols

1. We avoid doing anything that could either harm ourselves or anyone else. This includes stepping into traffic, holding a sign where it could fall onto cars below, climbing fencing, etc.

2. We must not block pedestrian and bike traffic, so please keep the middle of the overpass and/or sidewalk clear to allow them to pass.

3. We supply the messages, you supply the waves. However, you are welcome to also display your own poster boards. Just avoid any messaging that would be rated above a PG-13.

4. We don’t litter. If we find litter, we pick it up and throw it away.

5. We don’t use stickers or anything that leaves a permanent mark on the overpass. However, chalk is okay and even encouraged.

6. If someone from the ‘opposition’ comes up to talk with us, do not engage with them. Best to just ignore them. One member will be designated to handle them and video record any aggressive interaction so that you can go right on waving.

7. We take lots of pictures and videos during our action for circulation on social media. If you prefer not to be included, please let us know and/or consider wearing a mask.

8. Should law enforcement pay us a visit, only the designated point person from the group should address them.

9. Ignore the middle fingers and negativity coming from some of the cars below. For every one of those confused folks, you are providing hope to another 100 people!

10. The Visibility Brigade is a non-violent, informal volunteer group in which we all participate with an understanding that our own actions are our personal responsibility and we accept our own personal liability. You participate with this understanding.

Feel free to reach out to VisibilityBrigadeSanDiego@gmail.com with any questions.

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Abolish ICE SLO County! Show Up and Speak up at the County Board Meeting

location.venue: SLO County Board Of Supervisors Chambers, Katcho Achadjian Government Center

events.description:
Action Alert: Speak up About ICE Commandeering County Property!

Please plan to attend the Board of Supervisors meeting on one or two Tuesdays a month at 9:00 AM at 1055 Monteret Street in SLO.

The board voted to prohibit ICE from using county-owned or controlled property as a staging area, processing location, or operations base for federal immigration enforcement. The resolution also stipulates that non-public areas of any County facility may not be used for immigration enforcement without a valid warrant, writ, or order signed by a judicial officer.

We encourage you to attend meetings in person or via zoom or to submit written comments to urge the county to enforce this resolution at the jail. Currently, ICE conducts raids in the public lobby and transfers individuals via non-public sally ports without judicial warrants. If enforced, this resolution could end these operations. The sheriff facilitates these raids and has even cordoned off an area in the lobby for ICE agents to use for their operations.

How to take action:

  - Attend a Meeting: 9:00 AM. And make submit a slip to make a comment for General Comment on a Non agenda item.
  - Submit Written Comments: Boardofsups@co.slo.ca.us
  - Review the Full Resolution: https://agenda.slocounty.ca.gov/iip/sanluisobispo/file/getfile/178340

events.title: PPT & T4APA! Communications Committee
events.description:
Building the narrative of Transit Justice in our community is a critical part of our work. The Communications Committee hosts monthly virtual working meetings to tell the story of PPT’s campaigns, successes, and struggles. During these meetings, attendees help produce content that communicates our work to the public— including writing blogs, editing videos, creating content for our social media channels, curating photography, and doing graphic design.

Since 2025, the Communications Committee has been a joint space for members of Pittsburghers for Public Transit and supporters of [Transit for All PA!](https://www.transitforallpa.org/), the statewide transit campaign that we lead. Supporters of both organizations are welcome at these meetings, and we may work on projects relevant to Allegheny County or elsewhere in Pennsylvania.

### You might be a good fit for the Communications Committee if...
- You love writing and/or social media content creation
- You have experience with photography, graphic design, or web design

## 2026 Training Series

In 2026, our Communications Committee will be conducting a Comms Training Series! Each meeting will focus on a different core skill for communications work within organizing and justice movements. 

Here is a look at our syllabus for the year. We will release RSVP links on a rolling basis, so stay tuned to sign up for future dates! 

**November: Letters to the Editor and Op-Eds**

Local news media is a proven strategy for creating narrative change. You don't need to be a journalist to pitch a story—in fact, you have a strategic messaging advantage, just by being a transit rider in your community. Join experts from strategic communications firm Resource Media for a workshop on how to write Letters to the Editor, and practice your pitch!

### Past Workshops in 2026 (including so you can see what we've already learned!*

**January: Narrative Change Theory: Communications + Organizing**

**February: Telling an Effective Transit Story**

**April: Social Media Strategy for the Movement**

**May: Documenting Direct Actions on Social Media**

**June: Preparing for Harrisburg 2026 Day of Action**

**July: Designing for the Movement**

**August: Canva Bootcamp**

**September: Telling your story in social media videos**

**October: Photographing and videoing the movement**
events.accessibility_notes:

ASL and Spanish interpretation is available on request, but must be booked in advance. Given availability constraints for our interpreters, we are most likely to successfully book with 2 weeks or more of lead time. If interpreters are not available, Closed Captioning will be available for virtual meetings. Please email clair@pittsburghforpublictransit.org when registering to request interpretation.

events.title: Abolish ICE!  SLO County
events.description:
Rally and vigil every Sunday between 10 am - 11:30 am at the corner of Hwy 1 and Kansas Avenue. Join us for a rally to protest ICE activity in our beloved community and to hold vigil for those in our community abducted by ICE. The sheriff chooses to allow ICE agents into the jail to abduct people despite CA laws that would allow him not to cooperate. Despite the Board’s vote to stop commandeering the jail to make warrantless arrests, it continues unabated. The SLOSO facilitates 3 to 4 ICE abductions of people released from the jail per week. They account for over half of all the kidnappings in the county. People are detained out the jail who are being cited and released pending arraignment. They are denied due process and are guilty of no crime. Kidnappings at the jail are no different than the kidnappings in our community.

It IS happening here! ICE is in our community multiple times a week abducting people from the SLO County jail. Imagine you are waiting for a loved one to be released from the SLO county jail.  But before you can be reunited with them, they are kidnapped by masked secret police from the jail right before your eyes. Everyone deserves the right to be released from the jail safely regardless of immigration status. 

People taken at the jail are being denied due process and legal representation. They are separated from their children, families and loved ones. Don't turn your back on what is happening in our community. Everyone who is released from the jail should be released regardless of where they were born.

Bring large signs and banners centering calls for abolishing ICE and keeping it out of SLO and everywhere. If featuring signs with names of people murdered by ICE, please list all the people murdered by ICE. And the countless people harmed and disappeared whose names we do not know. Please stay off the road and stay safe.

events.title: EDF Action 2026 Environmental Book Club
events.description:
Join us the second Saturday of each month for our environmental book club!  We will be discussing these books and documentaries in 2026: 

JAN: Here Comes the Sun
By Bill McKibben 
Available on Amazon Paperback and Audible audio book 

The book explores the rapid, cheap growth of solar and wind power and how it offers humanity a genuine, hopeful chance to overcome the climate crisis and build a better civilization, despite fossil fuel industry opposition.

FEB:  A Future We Can Love 
By Susan Bauer-Wu 
Available on Amazon paperback + free audio book with Audible membership

Inspired by a conversation between the Dalai Lama and Greta Thunberg spoke for the first time in January 2021, millions of people around the world took notice. This book captures the lessons that came from that interaction. 


MAR: The Fragile Earth
By David Remnick, Henry Finder 
Available at local library, Hoopla and Amazon Paperback or Audible audio book

A collection of essays that tell the story of climate change—its past, present, and future—taking readers from Greenland to the Great Plains, and into both laboratories and rain forests.

APR: The Genius of Earth Day
By Adam Rome
Available at local library, Hoopla, Amazon + free audiobook with Audible membership.

The story of the first Earth Day is inspiring: it had a power, a freshness, and a seriousness of purpose that are difficult to imagine today. Earth Day 1970 created an entire green generation. 

MAY 9th:  Amplify
By Adam Met 

SPECIAL GUEST:  ADAM MET, PhD, Activist, Musician and Author

JUN: Unsettled by Steven Koonin 
Available at the local library, on Hoopla and Amazon Paperback or Audible audio book

Koonin was the top science advisor to the Obama administration.  When it comes to climate change, the media, politicians, and other prominent voices have declared that “the science is settled.” In reality, the climate is changing, but the why and how aren’t as clear as you’ve probably been led to believe. Koonin takes listeners behind the headlines, dispels popular myths, and unveils little-known truths. 

JUL: Documentary:  Ice on Fire | Free on Youtube (1:37)
(https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AP2IE8Upehc) 
Narrated by Leonardo DiCaprio

"Ice on Fire" explores the many ways we reduce carbon inputs to the atmosphere and, more importantly, how to "draw" carbon down, bringing CO2 out of the atmosphere and thus paving the way for global temperatures to go down. Through visiting visionaries and scientists young and old, the film explores the deep hope that we can turn away from the brink.  

AUG: Running Out By Lucas Bessire
Available at the local library, on Hoopla and Amazon Paperback

The imminent depletion of the Ogallala and other aquifers around the world is a defining planetary crisis of our times. Running Out explores aquifer depletion and the deeper layers through which it gains meaning and force. Anthropologist Lucas Bessire journeyed back to Western Kansas, where five generations of his family lived as irrigation farmers and ranchers, to try to make sense of this vital resource and its loss.

SEPT: Half Earth 
By Edward O. Wilson 
Available at the local library, on Hoopla and Amazon Paperback + Audiobook

In order to stave off the mass extinction of species, including our own, we must move swiftly to preserve the biodiversity of our planet. In this "visionary blueprint for saving the planet" (Stephen Greenblatt), Half-Earth argues that the situation facing us is too large to be solved piecemeal and proposes a solution commensurate with the magnitude of the problem: dedicate fully half the surface of the Earth to nature. 

OCT: The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind (watch the movie or read the book)
Movie: Find it on Youtube or Netflix 
Book: Available at the local library, on Hoopla and Amazon Paperback + Audiobook

Born to a family of farmers, Malawian agricultural engineer William Kamkwamba made headlines in 2001 when he built a functioning windmill out of old bicycle parts and scraps. (At the time, he was just 14 years old.) The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind, based on Kamkwamba’s memoir of the same name, tells the amazing true story of how he built a wind turbine and saved his small farming village from famine.

NOV: The Talking Earth (young adult)
by Jean George 
Available at the local library, on Hoopla and Amazon Paperback + Audiobook

Billie is a member of the Seminole Tribe, in a quest to identify facts over legend, she goes out into the Everglades alone, to stay until she can believe. In the wilderness, she discovers that she must listen to the land and animals in order to survive. With an otter, a panther cub, and a turtle as companions and guides, she begins to understand that the world of her people can give her the answers she seeks.

DEC:  A look back at our list of books - what did we learn? What is most memorable from our reading? 

_________________________________________________________
BOOK CLUB 2025 (For reference only) 

January 11th: [Documentary] Living the Change: Inspiring Stories for a Sustainable Future (Free Full Documentary)

February 8th: [Book] No is Not Enough, by Naomi Klein (Available on amazon, Hoopla, local library)

March 8th: [Book] The Language of Climate Politics, by Genevieve Guenther (available on amazon, Hoopla and local library)

April 12th: [Book] Silent Spring - Rachel Carson Let’s revisit the book that started our book club AND the environmental movement!

May 10th: [Podcast] How to save a planet - listen to a few episodes and come to the meeting to share what you learned. (https://gimletmedia.com/shows/howtosaveaplanet/episodes#show-tab-picker) find it on spotify: https://open.spotify.com/show/1KzrasExlM5dgMYwgFHns6

June 14th: [Book] It’s not that Radical | climate action to transform our world - Mikaela Loach

July 12th: [Documentary]: Climate extremes (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U8pLrRkqbb0)

August 9th: [Book] Earth for All, by Sandrine Dixson Decleve (available on Amazon)

September 13th: [Book] What if We Get it Right, by Ayana Elizabeth Johnson (Available in book and audio on Amazon)

October 11th: [Podcast] Climate Rising (https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/a-preview-of-cop29-what-business-leaders-should/id1482781075?i=1000675873770)

November 8th: [Book] The Good Ancestor, by Roman Krznaric (available on Amazon and Hoopla audio)

December 13th: Year end wrap up - what did we learn? 2026 Book Club

events.description:
REV UP (“Register, Educate, Vote, Use your Power”) is a nonpartisan movement led by the American Association of People with Disabilities to build the power of the disability vote.

REV UP National Calls bring disability vote organizers from across the country together to learn, connect, and strategize. Each call includes timely updates—such as federal voting rights news, calls to action, and funding and engagement opportunities—followed by a focus on a core topic with guest speakers. The topic for this call will be updated closer to the call date.

After registering you will receive an email from the American Association of People with Disabilities zoom with a unique link. We will resend the link on the day of the call.

CART and ASL are provided. Please include your access needs when signing up so we can share your information with access providers. Registered attendees receive slides and the agenda before the call, and recordings and notes are shared afterward.

Learn more about REV UP: www.aapd.com/about-rev-up/
