events.title: Tucson Shutdown Committee, Sun., 9/13 and weekly thereafter
events.description:
Tucson Shutdown

Please join Shutdown Trump Committee meeting, by Zoom, weekly on Sundays. The Steering Committee meets from 7-730 pm each week, followed by the General Meeting, from 7:30-8:30 pm. All are welcome to observe the Steering Committee meeting, but only the Steering Committee members (active Working Committee heads and sponsoring organizational reps) participate and vote.  You will be given the zoom link after you sign up. This meeting is for anyone who wants to volunteer.

Trump has threatened to cancel the mid-term elections. This would be a crucial step in completing his authoritarian takeover. The only thing that has been shown to reliably stop such a takeover is large-scale, non-violent noncooperation. An historic coalition came together in St. Louis in late May to call for exactly such a shutdown–if he does try to cancel the election. MayDayStrong.org has 600 labor unions and community groups as members.  Seven representatives from Tucson organizations went to St. Louis, including Democracy Unites Us, Party for Socialism and Liberation, Tucson Democratic Socialists of American and the local African-heritage ministerial alliance. Nine cities representing 30% of the economy have already committed to disrupt their economies for two weeks in case he does try to cancel the elections, so called “Tier 1” cities. Some of us in Tucson seek to make us a “Tier 2” city, to support the national Shutdown by disrupting our local economy as much as possible, at or above the scale of January 30th, for as long as we can. 

Please join us as individuals or representing a group.

events.title: Rush-hour Resistance Rally @ ICE Field office on Central & Holly

address_lines: North Central Avenue & West Holly Street

events.description:
**Join us for our Thursday afternoon rally across from the ICE Field Office on Central & Holly in Central Phoenix!**

*Rush-hour Resistance Rallies happen every Monday–Friday during rush hour across the Phoenix metro area. Check out [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us) for the latest locations!*

Here are the particulars for this rally:

🕥 You are free to show up anytime, but we recommend arriving a few minutes early to introduce yourself. The morning rally starts at 7:30 and ends promptly at 8:30 AM. The afternoon rally starts at 4:30 and ends promptly at 6:00 PM.  

🅿️ Parking is a bit of a challenge. Some of us park on Holly St, directly across from the ICE Field Office. We haven’t had issues before, but parking enforcement is unpredictable. If concerned, take the light rail.  

🔥🧊 We gather on the WEST side of Central, just north of Holly. Please DO NOT protest on the east side. Immigrants have appointments in this building, and we don't want to prohibit them from what they are required to do.

🖌️ One of RhRR’s strengths is that people feel free to express themselves. Ideally, your signs would help articulate any of our three pillars:

* Defending democracy and the rule of law
* Encouraging voting
* Protecting neighbors and communities (e.g., immigrants, LGBTQIA+ people, workers, and veterans)

This approach keeps signs aligned with RhRR’s purpose, while preserving personal expression and emotional authenticity.

**For this location, try to make your messaging specific to immigration rights, human rights, and other anti-ICE slogans.**

🇺🇳 Flags, banners, and even inflatable costumes are welcome. Some blow lots of bubbles. While our mission is serious, humor and camaraderie matter.

😷 RhRRs are peaceful, public events. Most attendees don’t hide their faces, though some do; participate at your comfort level. Photos and videos are common on social media, but you can ask posters to remove accidental appearances.

Thanks in advance for joining us. See you on the streets! ✊

**More about RhRR and why we do what we do every day of the week:**

📣 Rush Hour Resistance Rally began with a clear idea: neighbors, gathering peacefully and regularly on busy nearby streets, could remind our communities that democracy is essential and that silence is unacceptable. Over the last year, RhRR expanded from a handful of participants to multiple locations across the Valley, reaching thousands of pedestrians and motorists each week. This momentum is significant, as is the duty it brings.

🗳️ As we approach the midterm elections, our united mission is to safeguard free and fair elections and promote civic participation, particularly in local and primary races where every vote carries weight. Our weekly rallies are more than outlets for frustration; they are consistent, visible commitments that normalize voting and democratic engagement as neighborly expectations.

🕊️ RhRR is a peaceful, nonconfrontational movement. Our goal is to reach the broader community, not to confront those seeking conflict. When tensions surface, we withdraw, stay composed, and look out for one another. This discipline keeps our rallies inviting and helps newcomers feel secure joining us.

🫂 Most of all, RhRR is about people caring for one another while standing up for the future of our democracy. Every person who shows up, every sign held, and every conversation sparked on a street corner is part of something larger and deeply hopeful.

More info at [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us).

events.description:
A casual, come-as-you-are gathering for freethinkers, skeptics, humanists, and anyone who enjoys good conversation over a drink or a meal. No agenda, no program — just an easy evening to meet people in your community who share a commitment to reason, compassion, and living ethically without reliance on the supernatural.
What to expect
Show up, grab a seat, and talk about whatever's on your mind — current events, books, life, the big questions and the small ones. Your host will be there to welcome you, introduce you around, and answer questions about the Arkansas Society of Freethinkers and the American Humanist Association if you have them.
First time? You're especially welcome.
A lot of people find Humanist Happy Hour an easier first step than a lecture or formal meeting. You don't need to identify as a humanist (or anything in particular) to come — just bring curiosity and an open mind.
About drinks
Alcohol is optional and never expected. The venue has non-alcoholic options and food, so come however you come.
Finding us
We meet on the third Monday of each month at 7 PM at the Flying Saucer in downtown Little Rock. Street parking is free but limited after 6 PM on President Clinton Ave. Additional street parking is free and usually available off President Clinton Ave, but may require walking a block or two. Paid lots and garages are also available in the area, including the library garage located in the same building as the Flying Saucer.
Hope to see you there.

events.title: PORTLAND - Workers Rally for Universal Healthcare
events.description:
The purpose of this event is so that Unions stand shoulder to shoulder in solidarity and in power, to demand Universal Healthcare in Oregon. In particular, we demand that our legislature complete the bill and pass it to the voters for 2028.

**Please wear you union colors to this event!**

Here is a link to the most recent Workers Rally flyer which changes as we add endorsements! Please print and share widely!
https://canva.link/8eobhbi7n3ibq2w

## What This Means for Union Members

- **Health Care for all** – Everyone in, no one out
- **Quality Care** – PEBB + quality coverage (the kind insurance our lawmakers get)
- **Fair, predictable costs** – Insurance costs go down dramatically for most workers
- **Premiums only** – UHPGB projected cost estimates are premiums only; they don't include copays or deductibles
- **Save our Schools** – $500–800 million/year in projected savings for K-12 education
- **Save our public services** – Hundreds of millions/year in projected savings for government programs
- **Easier Contract Negotiations** – The rising cost of healthcare no longer competes with demands for higher compensation
- **Coverage untied from employment** – A job loss or early retirement before Medicare no longer means scrambling for individual coverage (25 million workers in the US only stay in their current job for health insurance)
- **Better coverage in our rural communities** – Normalized rates will be a lifeline for rural clinics and hospitals
- **So much more** – Like lower workers' comp and auto insurance rates, since medical costs are no longer priced into those premiums

events.title: Good Trouble Anti-Racism Workshop Series Session 4: The Iceberg Is Right Here

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Session 4: The Iceberg Is Right Here
Connecting history to our community today, how the past continues to shape the present right where we live.

The essence of the Good Trouble Anti-Racism Workshop Series 
(hereafter referred to as GTAR Workshop Series) is encapsulated in a quote from Congressman John Lewis: "Not the civil rights we inherited-but the civil rights we are building." 

GTAR Workshop Series is created and led by Sondra Light-Holt - a Black woman, a community health provider and advocate, a lifelong resident of Sandusky Ohio, and an active member with the NAACP. She is a board member of Serving Our Seniors and brings 25 years of experience in the field of healthcare to this Series.

THE GTAR Workshop Series is anti-racism education through the lens of healthcare, allowing us to more fully understand one another across racial lines, thus strengthening and expanding our community. Racism is America's wound. This series provides information regarding the harms of racism in housing, healthcare, education, and the justice system. Each session equips participants with factual knowledge, historical context, and civic language to recognize and respond to systemic racism in their own lives. 

The Series intentionally encourages people of all races to open up, share their experiences, ask hard questions and be heard without judgment. We'll learn, expand and strengthen our community, and take action by working together to heal our wounds, thus mitigating future damage. Medical racism runs throughout this series as a core thread, because community health is inseparable from community justice. 

Solidarity is practiced in real time, not just discussed in theory. Attendees are encouraged to share experiences of being targeted by racism, or being encouraged to behave in a racist way. Additionally, discussion is open to talking about positive experiences of friendship or power-sharing partnerships across racial lines. This model allows participants to acknowledge what has occurred in the past and make choices about how to build their future. 

Each session contains 2 parts: the Education portion of each Workshop provides relevant information to absorb; the Training portion builds solidarity across races. 

Topics: 
Session 1-How We Got Here-The Blueprint of American Racism (8/13) 
Session 2-The Iceberg-Seeing What You Were Taught Not to See (9/10) 
Session 3-It's Personal-Lived Experience, Privilege & the Stories We Tell Ourselves (10/8) 
Session 4-The Iceberg Is Right Here-Our Community Today (11/12) 
Session 5-What Do We Do Now-The Call to Action (12/10)

6 Sunrise PDX members opted to challenge their citations, and they need your support as they oppose this egregious violation of their first amendment rights. 

**Join Sunrise PDX on January 6th outside Lake Oswego City Hall** as we publicly pressure LO Mayor Joe Buck and other elected officials to denounce ICE presence in Lake Oswego. We will rally outside of the courthouse before the trial to make it clear that ICE is not welcome in Lake Oswego, and our right to peacefully protest will not be infringed by government overreach.

**Other ways you can help us fight back:**

1. Donate to our **[GoFundMe](https://gofund.me/6266d6031)** to cover citation costs and legal fees

2. Call Mayor Joe Buck’s office at 503-635-0213 and urge him to protect our right to protest and honor Lake Oswego’s status as a Sanctuary City by refusing to allow ICE to stay there

3. Boycott the Residence Inn by Marriott, where ICE sleeps in Lake Oswego; tell your friends and family to do the same

4. Follow Sunrise PDX at **[@sunrisepdx](https://instagram.com/sunrisepdx)** to stay informed about other ways to protect our immigrant neighbors and push ICE out of the Portland Metro

We the People: Claim Our Collective Power

A Five-Part Virtual Civic Engagement Training Series

Communities already hold the power to shape the decisions that affect their lives. Join this interactive five-part virtual training series to learn how to use your voice in the public processes that shape our communities. Drawing from San Diego's movement history and traditions of collective action, you'll build practical civic engagement skills to influence public decisions, strengthen communities, and advance human rights.

In this series, you'll learn how to:

- Participate in federal and California state rulemaking processes.
- Deliver effective public comment at city and county meetings.
- Understand public budgets and advocate for community priorities.
- Practice civic engagement skills through real-world exercises.
- Build confidence using your voice to advocate, organize, and create lasting change.

Complete each module to earn a Certificate of Participation. Participants who complete all five modules will earn recognition as Human Rights Dignity Defender Specialists in recognition of their commitment to civic leadership, collective action, and advancing human rights.

Training Schedule
Each module is offered in both English and Spanish. Attend one module or complete all five to earn the Human Rights Dignity Defender Specialist recognition.

Inspirándose en la historia del movimiento social de San Diego y sus tradiciones de acción colectiva, desarrollarás habilidades prácticas de participación cívica para influir en las decisiones públicas, fortalecer las comunidades y promover los derechos humanos.

- Participar en los procesos de normas federales y estatales de California.
- Presentar comentarios públicos eficaces en las reuniones municipales y del condado.

events.description:
Election Defenders is a weekly organizing call to learn, plan and promote resistance to authoritarian interference in our democratic elections.

We act in service of democracy and in line with lawful, nonviolent civil resistance against authoritarians.

The meeting will be hosted on Zoom every Saturday at 11:00 AM CT and will bring interested parties together to build the skills and community needed to amplify resistance voices across the country.

Why It Matters

Free and fair elections are a basic pillar of healthy democracies, and our elections are under attack by the Trump regime.

Trump and his enablers are trying many tactics: disenfranchising legitimate voters, blocking mail delivery of ballots, calling for armed intimidation at polling locations, making false or unsubstantiated claims about voting fraud, etc.

Election Defenders will support activists who wish to use lawful, nonviolent civil resistance to protect our democracy.

When: 

Every Saturday at 11:00 AM CT (9am PT, 12pm ET)

Format: Weekly group call via Zoom

Duration: 60 minutes

Focus areas: 

Understanding the entire election process and its vulnerabilities, utilizing training and information opportunities, supporting and growing the resistance, coordinating election protection efforts.

Learn more about the Board here: https://www.hcao.org/uhpgb

They have set aside time in their monthly meetings to hear from YOU about what you need in a new system. Share your perspective with the Governance Board in the form of Public Comment.

TALK TO THE PEOPLE MAKING THE PLAN! 

You must register in advance to reserve your time for public comments by emailing uhpgb.info@dcbs.oregon.gov. Or, if attending a meeting in person, you may sign-up 15 minutes before the meeting begins.

The Board meets on the 3rd Thursday of the month, both remotely and in-person at 350 Winter St. NE, Salem OR 97301. Often meetings are in Basement Conference Room F: please check meeting information for room changes.

This new system will be simpler, more affordable, and more sustainable — cutting costs for families and businesses while building a healthier, more stable future for our state."

Health Care for All Oregon has seen in real time that public comments has changed the work of the Board, and the framework of the plan. Your input can make a difference in this work.

events.title: 14th Annual National Vigil for All Victims of Gun Violence
events.description:
Each year since 2013, the Newtown Action Alliance Foundation (NAAF), the charitable arm of the Newtown Action Alliance (NAA), and numerous partners in the gun violence prevention community have sponsored the National Vigil for All Victims of Gun Violence on or near the anniversary of the Sandy Hook shooting tragedy. These multidenominational events, held in Washington, D.C., at the National Cathedral and St. Mark’s Episcopal Church, bring together survivors of gun violence, victims’ family members, concerned citizens, faith leaders, lawmakers, leaders of gun violence prevention organizations, and activists from across the nation. 

The 14th Annual National Vigil for All Victims of Gun Violence will be held on Wednesday, December 9, 2026 from 7-9:00pm ET at St Marks Episcopal Church on Capitol Hill, Washington, D.C. 

December 14, 2026 is the 14-year mark of the Sandy Hook tragedy. By this December, more than 1.4 million Americans will be killed or injured by guns since the Sandy Hook shooting tragedy. We urge you to join the gun violence prevention community in our collective effort to continue to shine a light on the devastating epidemic of gun violence in our nation until these gun deaths and injuries are reduced. 

The victims, survivors and the families impacted by gun violence are often forgotten. We have lost our #FreedomToLive. Therefore, the Newtown Action Alliance Foundation and the Newtown Action Alliance, in partnership with 160+ organizations  will host the annual national vigil service of mourning and loving remembrance for all who have fallen victim to the ongoing epidemic of gun violence in America. 

Our goal is simple. The gun violence prevention movement will unite to support the families and communities impacted by gun violence, educate, continue to raise awareness, and keep this critical issue front and center throughout our nation. Together, we will renew our vow to #HonorWithAction to #EndGunViolence in America by restoring our #FreedomFromGunViolence.

events.title: Post Election Review
events.description:
Minnesota takes election security seriously. Before the Election, we have the Public Accuracy Test. During the election, election judges ensure that the processes in the polling places follow the law. After the election, we have the Post Election Review. 

**[Minnesota Statutes 206.89](https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/206.89)** states that after every state general election, Minnesota counties perform a post-election review of election results returned by the optical scan ballot counters used in the state.  The review is a hand count of the ballots for each eligible election (U.S. President, U.S. Senator, U.S. Representative, and Governor) in the selected precincts compared with the results from the voting system used in those precincts.

The post-election review is carried out by the County Canvassing Board, made up of the County Auditor (in St. Louis County, Nancy Nilsen), the Court Administrator of the District Court (Kim Vizena), the mayor/chair of the town board of the largest municipality in the County(Roger Reinert), and two County Commissioners (Patrick Boyle and Ken Musolf). 

Come witness this historic process. Our elections are precious. Maybe in prior years we could let this operate in the background. 2026 is different. 

Note: the starting time, 9 am is set, the ending time depends on how long it takes to review the selected precincts.

events.title: Proactive Behavior Screening for Stronger Student Success
events.description:
**Proactive Behavior Screening for Stronger Student Success**

Join Firelight Books for an informative presentation introducing the Nichols Behavior Checklist (NBC), an innovative universal behavior screening and intervention tool designed to help schools identify behavioral and emotional concerns early—before they become barriers to student success.

The NBC is an Internet-based, individualized screening instrument for students in 1–12 that is quick, user-friendly, cost effective, and highly informative. In approximately 10 minutes per student, the NBC provides individualized behavioral screening reports with practical recommendations to support intervention planning and behavior management.

This presentation will demonstrate how the NBC helps educators, intervention teams, counselors, administrators, and clinicians:

* Identify areas of behavioral and emotional concern
* Improve student behavior through early intervention
* Support positive school functioning and interpersonal relationships
* Strengthen data-driven decision making
* Monitor trends at the district, campus, classroom, or individual student level
* Provide meaningful documentation for intervention planning

Attendees will learn how the NBC can be used as both a proactive screening instrument and an effective intervention support tool to help improve student outcomes, classroom climate, and overall school success.

The Nichols Behavior Checklist provides schools with practical behavioral insight—turning data into positive action for students.
www.firelightbooks.com

events.title: Intro to Community Organizing: Growing to Win
events.description:
How do we win? How do we advance our goals for social change? We get organized! Community organizing is people power in action. It's about uniting around a shared goal to make a difference together. Anyone can be an organizer. You don’t need a degree or years of experience—just a passion for change and a willingness to listen and learn.

_Billionaires are already organized, and we can be too!_

In this training opportunity, facilitator Brian Eaton will lead participants in an exploration of Structure Based Organizing, a century-old technique for building power and creating durable solutions to issues that matter to a community.

Participants in this one-hour workshop will learn:

- How Structure Based Organizing works—its key principles and techniques

- How Structured Organizing Conversations act as the foundation of successful campaigns

- How Structure Based Organizing can enable us to build local power into a mass movement

**Note: Enrollment limited to 15 participants.**

events.title: Food Scraps Collection: NoHo Farmers' Market
events.description:
As a volunteer, you’ll be right in the action, collecting food scraps from market-goers—the first step in a crucial process that turns waste into nutrient-rich compost. These scraps, gathered at local markets, are then processed at nearby green parks or gardens. Throughout your shift, you'll be guided by an experienced LA Compost staff member, who will act as your Compost Manager, offering insights and helping you share the benefits of composting with the public. The best part is that during your volunteer shift, you can take some time to shop at the market. Join us and be part of the composting movement that's transforming LA—one food scrap at a time!

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:

As a volunteer, you’ll play a hands-on role in guiding market-goers through composting, ensuring their food scraps are clean of stickers, compostable, and ready to be turned into nutrient-rich compost. You’ll monitor for contamination, assist with tracking data, and serve as a friendly, welcoming host to our composting community. 

#### MORE INFO: 

* You'll be stationed at the LA Compost booth under a pop-up canopy within the farmers' market. There will also be seating available.
* You may be asked to assist with moving filled bins of material weighing 60+ pounds. We always offer team lifts; you will never be asked to lift bins if you prefer not to.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome!
* Bathrooms are available
* If you sign up, please show up! We rely on volunteers like you to achieve our mission.  
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT: 
VOLUNTEER WAIVER: Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. Access the e-waiver at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver

CODE OF CONDUCT: All volunteers are expected to adhere to our volunteer code of conduct. Please visit https://www.lacompost.org/codeofconduct to review.

events.title: New Member Orientation! (Fall Series)
events.description:
As a member-led youth movement, MOVE Texas Members are at the heart of our mission to transform democracy in Texas and beyond. **Born out of the student organizing movement in San Antonio in 2013,** MOVE Texas was founded by young people who saw a gap in civic engagement and decided to take action. What started as a small group of student leaders registering their peers to vote has since grown into a statewide movement of young people that trains, mobilizes, and empowers a new generation of progressive community organizers.

## Who are MOVE Texas Members?

MOVE Texas members are the backbone of the organization, reflecting the energy and diversity of young Texans leading the charge for a more just and equitable future for all Texans across race, class, and place.  As a youth movement, MOVE Texas members are under 35, and are either:


- **Students:** The original foundation of MOVE Texas, young leaders organizing on campuses across the state, running voter registration drives, educating their peers, and leading local issue-based campaigns.

- **Community Members:** Young Texans who are inspired by MOVE Texas’ mission and actively work to build power in their neighborhoods, from hosting events to advocating for direct local and statewide policy change.

## MOVE Texas members receive:

- Access to MOVE trainings, programs, and resources,

- Voting power for statewide and local campaigns,

- Exclusive invitations to MOVE statewide events,

- Connection to a network of peers organizing across the state,

- Exclusive members merch.


MOVE Texas membership is open to anyone who believes in the power of young people to lead and shape the future AND our present.

# The LGBTQ+ Summit During the New Jersey League of Municipalities is BACK this November!

Join us and the Garden State's new LGBTQ+ business association, the Unity Chamber of Commerce, at the Hard Rock Hotel & Casino in Atlantic City on Tuesday, Nov. 17, for the return of this special event.⁠

The LGBTQ+ Summit During the New Jersey League of Municipalities is powered by PSEG.
⁠
### Special Guests
#### Honorable Julien X. Neals
*United States District Judge, District of New Jersey*

Since 2021, Judge Neals has served as a US District Judge of the US District Court for the District of New Jersey. Before that, he served as County Counsel and Acting County Administrator for Hackensack, and the Business Administrator for the City of Newark. He is a staunch ally for LGBTQ+ equality.

#### Assemblywoman Luanne Peterpaul
*NJ Legislative District 11*

In 2023, Luanne Peterpaul became the first openly lesbian woman elected to serve in the New Jersey Legislature. While representing NJ's 11th Legislative District, she was the primary Assembly sponsor for a bill to expand access to HIV medication and a primary sponsor of the recently signed into law bill to shield reproductive and transgender healthcare.

#### Bernie Wagenblast
*Transportation Journalist and Voice Actor • Summit Emcee*

Bernie Wagenblast is a transportation journalist and voice actor. She's best known for being a voice millions hear daily on transit systems, including the NYC subway, the AirTrain at Newark Liberty International Airport and PATCO in South Jersey and Philadelphia. Since her transition in early 2023, she's become a highly visible advocate for trans folks. 

Attendees will receive a free lunch.

Every Saturday at 1:00 PM | Coolidge Corner

Join members of three Brookline pro-democracy groups — indivisible Activist Evenings, Brookline Pax, and Speak Out, Seniors! — for our weekly rally at Coolidge Corner.

We gather to raise our voices and our signs in defense of democracy, justice, and decency — and to stand united against the abuses of the Trump administration and the forces that threaten our rights and freedoms.

We stand for:

• Immigrant rights, human rights, and racial justice

• Free speech, the Constitution, and the rule of law

• Access to health and healthcare for all

• Protection of our planet and the future we leave to the next generation

We choose empathy over cruelty, peace over violence, and hope over fear.

Our rallies are peaceful, spirited, and uplifting — a chance to connect, recharge, and stand up for what matters. Bring your friends, your voice, and your sign (or borrow one of ours!).

events.title: ARC Book Club: 'The Warmth of Other Suns' by Isabel Wilkerson
events.description:
Welcome to ARC’s (Antiracist Conversations) 12-week Virtual Read-Around Book Club.

 We will read Isabel Wilkerson’s book, The Warmth of Other Suns, which tells the epic story of America's Great Migration.

Our book club uses a unique format called a “Virtual Read-Around.”
No reading ahead is required: we will meet every Tuesday from September 8 through December 15, 2026, to read and experience Isabel Wilkerson’s The Warmth of Other Suns live as a group.

The book club will be facilitated by Jan, Pat, and Ms. Evelyn.

Together on live video, we will open each session with greetings and an icebreaker, and then we will read the book out loud.

There will be no verbal discussion during our weekly live meetings.

Important Note: Space is limited to 20 participants.  Registering for all book club meetings at once is the best plan. 

If you register and determine that you are unable to attend, please cancel your Mobilize registration so we can open your spot to someone else.

Weekly Meeting Schedule
We will meet every Tuesday for 90 minutes from September 8 through December 15, 2026. Find your local time zone below:

Pacific Time (PT): 8:00 AM – 9:30 AM
Mountain Time (MT): 9:00 AM – 10:30 AM
Central Time (CT): 10:00 AM – 11:30 AM
Eastern Time (ET): 11:00 AM – 12:30 PM


Meeting Timeline Breakdown
Every session follows this exact 90-minute structure (listed in Central Time):

10:00 AM – 10:10 AM: Open Zoom room, greetings, icebreaker, and tech check.

10:10 AM – 11:25 AM: Read out loud together as a group for 75 minutes.

11:25 AM – 11:30 AM: Wrap up and log off.

Reading and Journal Steps
We will cover about 30 to 35 pages together each week. 
 Confirm your attendance for the series by September 2, 2026. 

We’ll email additional information after you’ve confirmed your participation. 

Catching Up: If we do not finish the designated pages during our live read-around, please finish those specific pages on your own before the next Tuesday session.


Write Notes: After completing the weekly block, spend 10 to 15 minutes writing in a private journal while your thoughts are completely fresh.


Final Gathering: We will meet on Tuesday, December 15, at our usual session time for a final virtual gathering to share ideas from our journals and have a full verbal discussion.

See you on Tuesday, September 8, 2026.

With much appreciation,
The ARC Team

events.title: Volunteer Phone Banking - Virtual
events.description:
Every vote matters, and we’re on a mission to make that a reality. That's why ACLU of Michigan volunteers will be calling voters whose ballots need to be cured to ensure their vote can be counted.
 
In Michigan, voters who vote via Absentee Ballot must sign their ballot envelope before their vote is counted. If there are any issues with the signature, the voter’s city or township clerk will notify the voter with instructions on how to fix, or “cure”, the signature issue. (Often, the voter forgot to sign the back of their Absentee Ballot.)
 
Studies have shown that voters are more likely to follow up on their clerk's notice if they receive a call from friendly volunteers, so join us to make sure that every vote counts!
 
No experience is required; we will provide the training. You will just need: 1) a computer or tablet, 2) a cell phone, and 3) a steady internet or Wi-Fi connection.

events.title: Orlando Food Show: March 6th, 2027
events.description:
The 2027 SEPC Food Show Produce Rescue will occur on March 6th at the Orlando World Center Marriott in Orlando, FL.

Volunteers will glean fresh fruits and vegetables from the SEPC Southern Exposure Food Show.  All produce will be donated to those who struggle with food insecurity in Florida.  

This large indoor event requires bending, lifting, packing boxes, and working with others!  We are looking for up to 100 volunteers to help!  We will have two shifts available. 

The morning shift will begin around 8:30 am, and the second shift will begin at 6 pm.  The more volunteers we have the quicker we will finish, and the fresh food will be off to those in need!

### Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

#### 1. What is the SEPC Food Show?

- This is an annual event hosted by the Southeast Produce Council (SEPC),  which is a large trade show connecting growers, distributors, retailers, and foodservice professionals to showcase new produce, technology, and trends in the fresh fruit and vegetable industry, featuring education, networking, and exhibits. 

SoSA is the food recovery recipient of the showcased food. Following the events, with the help of our volunteers, we pack everything up to be sent to various food storage and distribution agencies.  

#### 2. Who can attend? Are community service hours available?

- All are welcome—no prior experience needed! Perfect for families, small groups, or anyone looking to serve or receive community service hours. (Kids under 18 must be with an adult.) Please bring any community service paperwork to be signed at day of event.

#### 3. Can I take food if I would like to try it?

-  No. Contractually all food is sent to food banks and agencies that will distribute to people in need. If you know someone in need or are in need yourself, please let one of the SoSA Crew staff know that would like to take back. Food that is deemed "inedible" is available for volunteers to take as animal feed after all pounds are accounted for.

#### 4. What do I wear?

- Wear comfortable clothing that you can bend, lift and walk in. Closed-toed shoes are mandatory.

#### 5. Where does the food go?

- All the produce goes directly to local food banks and community partners feeding those in need.

#### 6. How can I stay in the loop?

- For event updates via email, sign up at: https://endhunger.org/get-involved/volunteer/

#### 7. Other FAQs :

- NO smoking, NO pets
Please note- Please bring your own water. There will be restrooms. 

📢 Questions? 
Contact:
Megan McEwen 
📞 (863)224-0403
📧 fl-glean@endhunger.org

events.title: Freedom Fridays: CELEBRATE THE AMERICAN PEOPLE!!!
events.description:
Join us on Friday, November 6th at NOON at the Williamsburg James City County Courthouse, located at 5201 Monticello Avenue, Williamsburg.

BRING YOUR CELEBRATORY SIGNS TO THIS FREEDOM FRIDAY!!!

The American people did it. We showed up to vote and fought for decency, kindness, fairness, and democracy - the America we want to be in this world!!! Bring a cold beverage, and a chair, if needed.

COMMUNITY NORMS: Please read before attending one of our events. One of our main objectives is to host PEACEFUL, RESPECTFUL and SAFE EVENTS. Remember, when attending a Williamsburg JCC Indivisible event, your actions represent our group, and you are expected to conform to the Community Norms. Safety is a top priority for our attendees. Please remain out of the median, per instructions from the police. Being in the median puts us at risk and potentially drivers as well. Do not block the right-of-way for others. If someone is on the sidewalk, please step back and let them pass. If an Urgent Situation arises, we will raise a straight arm with our Hand in a Fist to ask for Silence. PLEASE DO THE SAME TO QUIET THE CROWD. This way we can quickly relay an important message to all. We wish to remind everyone that we do not react to those drivers who make it clear they do not support us by aggravating them through screaming obscenities or making certain hand gestures. We do not want to enrage them and potentially make everyone, including other drivers, less safe. It is easier to wave at everyone and say, “Have a nice day.”
PLEASE DO NOT BLOW WHISTLES UNLESS ICE IS PRESENT. The purpose of the whistles is to alert the public to be vigilant. Otherwise, blowing them can falsely alert the crowd to a danger that does not exist! At our events, please do not hold signs or otherwise promote other events that Williamsburg JCC Indivisible is not hosting. You may be placing a potential legal liability onto our group that we are NOT willing to accept. Please do not engage in DISRUPTIVE BEHAVIOURS! If you are asked to stop engaging in activities which are disrupting an event to the point people are complaining to the hosts that they are experiencing physical or emotional trauma, it is expected that you will be respectful of others and follow our Community Norms and stop those behaviours. Loud noises, such as, but not limited to, COWBELLS, horns, etc., are usually deployed by counter-protesters to disrupt an event, not by attendees participating in an event. If you refuse to disengage from such thoughtless behaviours, do not ruin the event for everyone else - please be kind and leave! As with our previous events, the same rules apply. We will not engage with counter-protesters. If an issue arises, please notify one of the event organizers, who will be wearing Williamsburg JCC Indivisible T-shirt. We will not engage in any acts of violence or violation of any applicable laws or engage in civil disobedience. All actions will be peaceful. Everyone participating in this event will be required to behave lawfully to ensure the safety of event participants and will seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. We will obey the orders of authorized event marshals and law enforcement authorities. Event organizers will not be responsible for any injury or damage if any were to occur during this event. Each individual is responsible for the consequences of their actions and attends at their own risk. We will park in the Courthouse parking lot without blocking access lanes and will remove any trash that is left. We are committed to maintaining public health measures to practice safe protesting during these times. Please wear a mask and socially distance if that makes you more comfortable - weigh your own risk in attending. Follow all local safety guidelines at minimum, and any safety instructions from hosts that exceed local law.

location.venue: Donovan Hines Foundation of Exuberance Co

events.description:
2026 #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence

Beginning Wednesday, December 9, 2026 until the end of December, we will come together across the nation to host the #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence.

These local events will be anchored by the 14th Annual National Vigil for All Victims of Gun Violence on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C.—held near the 14-year mark of the Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting tragedy, when a 20-year-old gunman armed with an AR-15 hunted and murdered 20 first graders and six educators.

Across the country, vigils (as simple as lighting candles) and gatherings will honor lives stolen by gun violence, uplift survivors, raise awareness, and demand urgent action from our leaders to finally end this epidemic. From schools and workplaces to houses of worship, neighborhoods, grocery stores, homes, nightclubs, streets, and even our democracy itself—gun violence impacts every aspect of American life.

The theme of this year’s campaign is #FreedomToLive—the simple, powerful idea that every person deserves to live free from the daily threat of gunfire. Together, survivors, families, advocates, and allies will raise our voices to ensure that FREEDOM means the right of every person to live, learn, work, worship, speak, vote, and gather without the daily fear of gun violence.

We stand in solidarity with over 1.4 million Americans who have been shot since Sandy Hook, with every community devastated by gun violence for decades. We will send a clear message to our local, state, and federal lawmakers, raise awareness, and help build the movement for common-sense solutions.

Let’s #HonorWithAction together. Let’s demand freedom from gun violence.

#### Literature & Ladle Society Sorting Soup’s (Book Club’s) Sunday: Burnout @9am & This is the Plan @4pm -ZOOM

#### _This fall, The Ladle & Literature Society—also known as the Sorting Soup Book Club—this weekend 9/20 has  two (2) Book Clubs.. 9am and 4pm.

_We’ll gather around books that take both the personal toll of organizing and the practical work of winning seriously.

#### Let us know you will be attending either the 9am by RSVPing here -> https://mobilize.us/s/30D6NR

#### Sunday @ 9 am ..Burnout: The Secret to Unlocking the Stress Cycle

*Burnout: The Secret to Unlocking the Stress Cycle* by Emily and Amelia Nagoski explores why stress lingers in our bodies long after the immediate crisis has passed, and how we can interrupt the cycle through rest, connection, movement, boundaries, and joy. Organizers are regularly asked to absorb urgency, outrage, grief, and other people’s needs; without ways to process that load, exhaustion becomes a predictable political outcome. 

This discussion is for anyone who wants to build a practice of care sturdy enough to support the long haul—because a movement cannot afford to treat its people as disposable.

It is an antidote to doomscrolling and magical thinking: organized people change what looks inevitable by showing up, making a plan, and bringing others with them. 

#### Join the 4pm CDT we have  *This Is the Plan: How to End America’s Meltdown & Save Democracy* by Ben Wikler, turns toward the collective work of democratic renewal. Drawing from his organizing and political experience in Wisconsin, Wikler lays out a practical argument for building durable power, expanding participation, and addressing the systems that undermine democracy—not simply focusing on a single candidate or election. \\ NOTE NOV 1ST 4PM THIS IS THE PLAN IS CANCELED THIS WEEK ONLY …

events.title: Honesty Coalition 2026 LGBTQ+ Youth & Parents Listening Session
events.description:
This session is for students and their parents. We'll have two rooms in the Zoom—so parents and students can speak freely with their peers!

The Belonging for Every Student Listening Campaign is a statewide effort to better understand how recent anti-LGBTQ+ laws are shaping the experiences of students, educators, and families across Ohio.

Over the past few years, laws like House Bill 8 have required all 611 school districts in Ohio to adopt new policies. While these policies are public record, what remains unclear is how they are being put into practice and how they are impacting real people in school communities.

This autumn, we are listening. We want to know: How are districts implementing these policies? Are schools going beyond what the law requires? How are LGBTQ+ students and families being affected? What changes are educators experiencing in their classrooms, materials, and ability to support students?

By gathering stories, insights, and data from across the state, this campaign will help build a clearer picture of what’s happening on the ground. These findings will directly inform advocacy strategies for the 2026–2027 school year, ensuring that efforts to support safe, inclusive, and equitable schools are rooted in the lived experiences of Ohio communities.

Please share with young Ohioans who have something to say about the experiences of LQBTQ+ students in our schools in the 2026-2027 school year.

events.title: The People's Tea
events.description:
## **Special Announcement** 

On Wednesday, November 4th, we'll hold a special session to hear stories from folks on the ground, make sense of what this election tells us about our landscape, and name what comes next. 

Because **our work doesn't end on Election Day**: we'll share the concrete ways we'll keep organizing to keep each other safe and protect our democracy in the months and years ahead.

We'll have Spanish translation available for this call. 

**Anuncio Especial**
El miércoles 4 de noviembre, realizaremos una sesión especial para escuchar historias de la gente en el terreno, entender lo que esta elección nos dice sobre nuestro panorama, y definir lo que viene después.

Porque nuestro trabajo no termina el Día de las Elecciones: compartiremos las maneras concretas en que seguiremos organizándonos para protegernos mutuamente y defender nuestra democracia en los meses y años por venir.

Habrá interpretación en español disponible durante esta llamada.

### More information: 
**The People's Tea** is a biweekly power hour where we’ll discuss what’s going on, what it means, and what we can do. 

At the People’s Tea, we will slow down, process the news, and make sense of what’s happening. We’re building a space where we can stay informed without losing our humanity (and sanity), and move from feeling overwhelmed and isolated toward understanding, connection, and collective action. 

We will meet every other **Wednesday at 8 PM Eastern / 7 PM Central / 6 PM Mountain / 5 PM Pacific.** There’s only one requirement to join. This will be a judgment-free space where we will show compassion and curiosity. We simply expect you to be respectful and non-judgmental. There are no expectations to have all the answers, know the “right” things, or even know where to begin. 

**Come learn, listen, and connect.**

events.title: Florida NOW Anti-Racism Book Club Discussion: Abolition. Feminism. Now.
events.description:
Join the Florida NOW Anti-Racism Book Club for a discussion of Abolition. Feminism. Now. by Angela Y. Davis, Gina Dent, Erica R. Meiners, and Beth E. Richie.

n this groundbreaking book, four leading abolitionist feminist thinkers and organizers explore the history and present-day practice of abolition, drawing connections between struggles against prisons, policing, racism, gender-based violence, and economic injustice. The authors examine abolition not simply as an effort to dismantle systems of punishment, but as a project of building the social, political, and economic conditions that allow communities to thrive.

The book brings together decades of feminist organizing, scholarship, and movement-building to ask what it means to imagine a world beyond punishment, and how we begin creating that world now.

Join us for a conversation about the book’s central ideas, the movements and histories it explores, and what abolitionist feminism can teach us about building a more just and liberatory future.

Monday, December 21st, at 6:30 PM on Zoom

All are welcome, whether you’ve finished the book, are still reading, or are joining the conversation to learn more.

events.title: 2026 #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence
events.description:
2026 #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence

Beginning Wednesday, December 9, 2026 until the end of December, we will come together across the nation to host the #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence.

These local events will be anchored by the 14th Annual National Vigil for All Victims of Gun Violence on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C.—held near the 14-year mark of the Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting tragedy, when a 20-year-old gunman armed with an AR-15 hunted and murdered 20 first graders and six educators.

Across the country, vigils (as simple as lighting candles) and gatherings will honor lives stolen by gun violence, uplift survivors, raise awareness, and demand urgent action from our leaders to finally end this epidemic. From schools and workplaces to houses of worship, neighborhoods, grocery stores, homes, nightclubs, streets, and even our democracy itself—gun violence impacts every aspect of American life.

The theme of this year’s campaign is #FreedomToLive—the simple, powerful idea that every person deserves to live free from the daily threat of gunfire. Together, survivors, families, advocates, and allies will raise our voices to ensure that FREEDOM means the right of every person to live, learn, work, worship, speak, vote, and gather without the daily fear of gun violence.

We stand in solidarity with over 1.4 million Americans who have been shot since Sandy Hook, with every community devastated by gun violence for decades. We will send a clear message to our local, state, and federal lawmakers, raise awareness, and help build the movement for common-sense solutions.

Let’s #HonorWithAction together. Let’s demand freedom from gun violence.

Bring signs and your friends. Sign Messages Recommended: End Gun Violence, March For Our Lives, Stand With Victims, Stop Domestic Abuse

events.title: Untested, Unsafe, Unacceptable – Write to Your Members of Congress NOW!

Dear friends,  
I am one of the millions of Americans who rely on mail in voting. But now, Our Votes Are in Danger! the government is trying to rush through a dangerous, untested USPS rule that could disenfranchise millions of voters who rely on mail in voting. Our Votes Are in Danger!

Here’s what’s happening: 
•	USPS built a brand new ballot screening system in just 3 months (normally takes over a year)
•	It was given less than 1 week of testing
•	A “zero failure” policy means: one barcode error = thousands of ballots rejected
•	The Trump administration has appealed to the Supreme Court to allow this rule to take effect before the midterm elections

📢 "Untested, Unsafe, Unacceptable" – That's Our Message
We are saying NO to:
❌ UNTESTED – A system built in 3 months with less than 1 week of testing
❌ UNSAFE – One barcode error could reject thousands of ballots
❌ UNACCEPTABLE – Our votes are NOT your experiment
We need to make our voices heard – NOW.

Step 1: Find your members of Congress

https://www.house.gov/representatives/find-your-representative

The new USPS ballot system is:
❌ UNTESTED – A system built in 3 months with less than 1 week of testing
❌ UNSAFE – One barcode error could reject thousands of ballots
❌ UNACCEPTABLE – Our votes are NOT your experiment

Over 250 current and former members of Congress have already urged the Supreme Court to block this executive order.Please join them.  
I ask you to:  
1.	Support Senator Blumenthal’s investigation

3.	Call on USPS to pause and independently test this system

Please act now. Our votes depend on it.

Sincerely,  
[Your Full Name]  
[Your Address]

events.title: The Pioneer Project
events.description:
The Pioneer Project is a two-part program where participants will be trained in the fundamentals of legislative advocacy and then supported as they practice what they learned in a real-world policy campaign. The program begins with 8 remote trainings over the course of 4 weeks (skipping over the week of Thanksgiving) that will equip our trainees with the skills to design a policy, propose it to their lawmakers, and pull the right levers to get it passed into law. After completing the trainings, participants can choose to join us in our mission of jumpstarting a nationwide transition to clean energy by launching a policy campaign of their own. 

Our curriculum covers the process of legislative advocacy from start to finish, and is based on the lived experience of youth and environmental advocates over the years. Legislative advocacy is a skill that allows everyday people to weigh into and lead political decisions in their community. Right now, politicians mainly hear from corporations and paid lobbyists when making their decisions and creating policy. Legislative advocacy opens the door for anyone to enter that conversation and make political change. 

The second and most exciting phase of the program is our clean energy policy campaigns, led by past participants in the states where a clean energy transition is needed the most. After completing all the trainings, participants can choose to launch their own statewide policy campaign or join an ongoing campaign using our clean energy policy framework. Throughout these campaigns, participants will apply everything they've learned from the trainings in real life, strengthening their knowledge with experience. Policy campaign teams will be provided with continuous support from Pioneer Energy through coaching, templates, and other resources. 

Everyone and anyone is welcome to join the Pioneer Project, but we believe this program will be especially helpful to grassroots groups looking to add another tactic to their toolbox, young activists learning how to build their own power, and people interested in a future in public policy.

PROGRAM DETAILS: The training phase spans 4 weeks, skipping over the week of Thanksgiving. Trainings are Monday and Wednesday at 6 PM est, and run for an hour or less. Finally, these trainings are free, remote, and open to all!

TRAINING TOPICS
November 16th: Welcome to Pioneer Energy
November 18th: Engineering a Policy
November 30th: Preparing for the Project
December 2nd: Researching your Legislature
December 7th: Lobby Meetings
December 9th: Bill Drafting and Sponsorship
December 14th: Supporting the Bill
December 16th: Advocacy and the Home Stretch

events.title: Intro to Community Organizing: Growing to Win (MV)
events.description:
How do we win? How do we advance our goals for social change? We get organized! Community organizing is people power in action. It's about uniting around a shared goal to make a difference together. Anyone can be an organizer. You don’t need a degree or years of experience—just a passion for change and a willingness to listen and learn.

_Billionaires are already organized, and we can be too!_

In this training opportunity, facilitator Brian Eaton will lead participants in an exploration of Structure Based Organizing, a century-old technique for building power and creating durable solutions to issues that matter to a community.

Participants in this one-hour workshop will learn:

- How Structure Based Organizing works—its key principles and techniques

- How Structured Organizing Conversations act as the foundation of successful campaigns

- How Structure Based Organizing can enable us to build local power into a mass movement

**Note: Enrollment limited to 8 participants.**

events.title: The First Five Years: Nashville Early Childhood Convening

location.venue: American Baptist College- Lewis & Scruggs Hall

events.description:
## Birth to five isn’t a phase. It’s the blueprint.

The first five years shape everything that follows. Our children deserve a community that treats them that way.

Join us — parents, providers, educators, leaders — as we start building a coalition for Davidson County’s youngest residents.

This isn’t a meeting about our kids. It’s a room built by the people raising them. That coalition carries the work forward: setting its own priorities, doing its own research, and advocating for the investment this community’s youngest residents deserve.

### What This Convening Does

- **Builds the line from kitchen table to policy table**, which helps residents connect lived economic pressure to local systems and public investment while understanding how to plug in after the election

- **Sets community-defined priorities** around family affordability, carried forward into TEA's economic justice work with community voice at the forefront

- **Activate and equip residents and trusted messengers with toolkits to GOTV** because while we know that voting alone won't fix the problem, we acknowledge that it is a power-building tool in our toolbox

## The gaps are real. So is our power to close them. Let's put our feet on the street and our boots on the ground.

events.title: Carrollton AREA Democrats - Nico Nights with Neighbors

location.venue: Nico's Cocina - Event Room (to right of restaurant)

events.description:
WELCOME to our once a month (third Wednesday) meeting of the Carrollton AREA Democrats Club.  Our focus is to get to know our Neighbors - to meet like-minded folks for fellowship, education, solidarity and purpose.  Learn how WE can shape our plans as we seek to SAVE OUR COUNTRY AND DEMOCRACY!  

Our November 18th meeting is a continuation of our mission to understand and get to know our neighbors better as we take a timely look at our "Mosaic of Carrollton" - people living in our community and how we can be Allies to Each Other. 

This month we have invited Madison Noelle McNair (she/her) to present "Disability & Democracy: Inclusion As A Core Value."  We will be discussing accessibility, inclusion, accommodations, activism, disability history, and how disability is intersectional with all causes.

Presenter's Bio:
Madison is 29, she was born & raised in the Dallas area, she has been disabled her entire life and is passionate about accessibility. She began her journey by volunteering starting at 5 years old, and started more dedicated advocacy at 18 years old. She has been honored to work with many non-profit and advocacy groups across Dallas including Sunrise Movement Dallas and Sunrise Movement Tarrant, Dallas For Change, La Colectiva NTX, El Movimiento, Viva Colectiva, Vecinos Unidos DFW, New Disabled South, Dallas Area Transit Alliance, and she feels extremely lucky to have worked for many more in addition to these. Madison is currently a part of the Class of 2026 and Cohort 7 of the LBJ Women’s Campaign School at UT Austin, on the Patient-Family Advisory Council (PFAC) at Parkland, and the Paratransit & Accessibility Advisory Group (PAAG) with DART.

Instagram: @monoqueenmadi 

We are looking forward to presenting additional educational topics at future meetings for all of us to learn about, understand, and appreciate our commonality. 

As always - we will give time to any candidates that are stopping by to introduce themselves and speak for a few minutes at the end of our meetings.

PLEASE NOTE - for those who can arrive early - about 5pm - you may participate in #CRAFTIVISM. If you arrive at 5PM or later - we will be creating "At Risk" packets to be distributed in our community for those who may be targeted by ICE. In addition - we have created "Whistle kits" for Allies.

THE MEETING WILL BEGIN A LITTLE BEFORE 7PM.

We are a Grass Roots Group dedicated to preserving our American way of Life that honors the Individual with Diversity, Equality and Dignity. Learn about ways you can participate in ACTIVISM.  Learn how you may participate in our HIVES (Precinct) project.  We are Creating FUN Caring Communities - and Winning Elections!  And we are building on our momentum from 2025 thanks to your growing enthusiasm! 

Let us help you find ways that you may use your skills, talents and strengths to participate in our fight to take back our country thru activism, demonstrations, precinct building, voter registration and much more.  

Our Goal is to be a source of Information to all Carrollton AREA Democrats so they may make informed and wise decisions at the voting booth. 

We now have a Web Site: https://www.carrolltondemocrats.com/. This will provide our Carrollton Democrats the resources they need whether they live in Denton or Dallas County.  

JOIN US every 3rd Wednesday of the Month:
Nico Nights with the Neighbors - Nico's Cocina (6:30 to 8:30). 

3065 N. Josey Lane, Carrollton, TX 75007

We meet in the EVENT ROOM to the right of the restaurant. 

Please sign up on Mobilize so we may prepare enough materials for everyone. 

If you wish to be placed on our email list, (only 3-4 a month) please SIGN UP on CarrolltonDemocrats.com.  And we'll be able to introduce you to your neighbors in your precinct.   

Again - we are happy you have found us - look forward to meeting you!

events.description:
#### Literature & Ladle Society Sorting Soup’s (Book Club’s) Sunday: Burnout @9am & This is the Plan @4pm -ZOOM

#### _This fall, The Ladle & Literature Society—also known as the Sorting Soup Book Club—this weekend 9/20 has  two (2) Book Clubs.. 9am and 4pm.

_We’ll gather around books that take both the personal toll of organizing and the practical work of winning seriously.

#### Let us know you will be attending either the 9am by RSVPing here -> https://mobilize.us/s/30D6NR

#### Sunday @ 9 am ..Burnout: The Secret to Unlocking the Stress Cycle

*Burnout: The Secret to Unlocking the Stress Cycle* by Emily and Amelia Nagoski explores why stress lingers in our bodies long after the immediate crisis has passed, and how we can interrupt the cycle through rest, connection, movement, boundaries, and joy. Organizers are regularly asked to absorb urgency, outrage, grief, and other people’s needs; without ways to process that load, exhaustion becomes a predictable political outcome. 

This discussion is for anyone who wants to build a practice of care sturdy enough to support the long haul—because a movement cannot afford to treat its people as disposable.

It is an antidote to doomscrolling and magical thinking: organized people change what looks inevitable by showing up, making a plan, and bringing others with them. 

#### Join the 4pm CDT we have  *This Is the Plan: How to End America’s Meltdown & Save Democracy* by Ben Wikler, turns toward the collective work of democratic renewal. Drawing from his organizing and political experience in Wisconsin, Wikler lays out a practical argument for building durable power, expanding participation, and addressing the systems that undermine democracy—not simply focusing on a single candidate or election. \\ NOTE NOV 1ST 4PM THIS IS THE PLAN IS CANCELED THIS WEEK ONLY … 

#### Join by Zoom .. The Literature & Ladle Society Sorting Soup’s (Book Club’s) Sunday sessions: Burnout - ZOOM at 9:00 a.m. & This is the Plan @4pm CST, -> https://bit.ly/NWSOFA-Zoom

events.description:
In November we'll welcome Megan Peterson and Erin Maye Quade the Executive Director and Senior Advisor, respectively, of [Gender Justice](https://www.genderjustice.us/) to present on "Gender and Authoritarianism" at our monthly meeting. 

Building off the enthusiasm for our "soup and cake" with the Debate Watch Party, November's meeting will kick off with a potluck STARTING AT 5:00 with the actual meeting beginning at 6:00.

Authoritarians regularly use gender as a wedge issue to create fear, divide people, and reinforce traditional hierarchies and patriarchy. The Trump regime is following this playbook on many fronts: trans youth participation in sports, Hegseth's attacks on diversity in the military, the SAVE Act to disenfranchise women voters, blocking health care for trans youth, and on and on. Gender Justice's presentation will outline these issues in a potent and coherent way and better equip us to protect the rights of ALL people to live fully and freely with respect to gender. 

Megan and Erin will present by Zoom, allowing us to share the event with Indivisible groups throughout CD8. This is something of an experiment. 

We will still meet in person in Duluth for the potluck at 5:00 PM, discussion and planning on how gender advocacy might fit into our 2027 planning. 

Please spread the word.

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Since November 2020, the League of Women Voters of Michigan and their Pro-Democracy Partners have worked to be the public’s eyes and ears at Michigan’s county canvass of votes cast during an election. Each year they work together to ensure that trained volunteers observe County Board of Canvassers (BOC) meetings, across the state of Michigan, watching the process by which local results are reviewed and certified.

This consistent, nonpartisan observation promotes transparency and accountability, helps identify potential issues that could put timely certification at risk, and reassures Board of Canvassers members and election staff that the public is engaged in their work. Should observation uncover anything beyond the canvassers’ ministerial, nondiscretionary duties, LWVMI can elevate the issue to the Secretary of State’s office or an election attorney.

### Your Role As An Observer:
- Our BOC Observer are an important aspect of our volunteer election work! 
- Our observers not only serve to build trust in the community as well as between local government and the League, but they also help to ensure our elections are running as the laws intended. 
- Reporting from our observers helps us understand the health of our democratic systems, where issues are happening, and where things are running smoothly.  
- These insights are important to all of us working to support our democracy, and ultimately support our communities in ensuring their voices are heard! 

We hope you will join us, volunteer, and bring a friend to be a part of this election work!

PS: Shifts are subject to change, as county clerks work to finalize the details of the county canvass. If your shift is cancelled, you will be contacted by a representative from the League of Women Voters.

events.title: PR Committee Meeting - Democratic Party of Outagamie Co.
events.description:
Join the Democratic Party of Outagamie County’s Public Relations Committee to help us use tech to build the messages, visuals, outreach, and community connections that move local Democrats forward. We are an all-local, all-volunteer team within our county party, working to elect dems and further progressive values right here at home.

Volunteers with specialized skills often lead projects in their areas of expertise, but there’s room for learning and collaboration, too. You don’t need to know every tool already, we’re looking for people who are comfortable using technology, willing to learn, and ready to take ownership of tasks.

Whether you are a web developer, designer, photographer, chronically online, spreadsheet organizer, metrics-minded planner, email design wizard or simply someone who wants to pitch in when you can, there is a place for you on the PRC. Most volunteer roles are designed for a manageable 2–3 hours per week, and monthly project-based assignments are available for people who cannot take on an ongoing role.

At this meeting, we’ll:

- Welcome new and returning volunteers and make space for quick introductions
- Share updates on social media, email, events, and current PR projects
- Review open assignments and volunteer needs
- Match people with roles based on their interests, skills, and availability
- Discuss ways to support DPOC events, candidates, Outagamie Action Teams, and local community partners
- Gather ideas for future content, campaigns, and projects

We are currently especially looking for volunteers interested in:

- Social media static & Carousel content design, videos, and engagement
- Copywriting, editing, proofreading
- Graphic design, Canva templates, print materials, and email design
- Photography, short-form video, and video editing
- Website updates and event information
- Project coordination, deadline tracking, and intake support
- Press releases, talking points, media relations, and rapid-response writing
- Event promotion, flyer distribution, and volunteer coordination

No prior committee experience is required, just be comfortable working between your phone and laptop, learning new software as needed, and communicating digitally to a modern audience. We can provide tools, templates, direction, and a supportive team, bring your skills, curiosity, and ideas. If you are not ready for a standing role, you can also join our Project Volunteer pool and opt into one-off assignments that fit your schedule.

The PR Committee is where we turn good work into clear, local, people-centered communication. Help us make sure Outagamie County voters know what Democrats are doing, where they can get involved, and why every election matters.

One night. One film. The founder of Moms First, in the room, in Denver.

Only valid tickets purchased through Eventbrite will be admitted to this event.

We need to talk about something bigger than the next dance floor. The culture wars have divided us — this is how we come back together.

MFT is proud to partner with Moms First to bring their film No Country for Mothers to Apollo Hall, Denver — with founder Reshma Saujani joining us live.

No Country for Mothers explores the culture wars surrounding American motherhood and why both the "girl boss" and "trad wife" labels ultimately distract us from the real issue: the lack of support for American families. Following activist Reshma Saujani, the film charts a growing national movement to reunite moms across divisions and win the kind of historic support families actually need.

Since its June 2026 NYC premiere, the film has reached 1,000+ community screenings nationwide and holds the record for the most producers ever credited on one feature. On November 9, it's Denver's turn, with a live, intimate Q&A led by the film's Executive Producer and Moms First Founder & CEO, Reshma, in person.

Moms First is fighting for the policy change mothers deserve — paid leave, real childcare, structural support. We've spent years building the other half of that fight: the community, joy, and permission to come first that prove what happens when moms feel seen, resourced, and supported — we take on the world.

The night:

- Cocktail hour, charcuterie & cash bar
- Full screening of No Country for Mothers
- Live Q&A with Reshma Saujani
- Apollo Hall, Denver — Monday, November 9, doors 5pm
- $45 (+ fees) per ticket · 10% of proceeds go directly to Moms First
- Dress code: glam, elevated cocktail — wear something that makes you feel powerful. Can't swing it? No sweat, just bring the vibe.

Endless gratitude to Apollo Hall for donating their beautiful space and believing in this mission as much as we do — this night wouldn't be possible without them.

This isn't for a side. It's for every mother who's tired of being asked to pick one.

events.description:
HELP US RAISE AWARENESS!

In order to raise awareness and stand vigil, our group holds signs at places throughout Salem, where our neighbors were abducted by ICE. 

• Please register to RSVP and get address.

• Every Friday, rain or shine.

• Signs are handed out and locations are assigned at a meeting spot to be disclosed.

• Teams of two then set out for one hour of sign holding.

• Bring a friend or we’ll assign you a partner.

• After the hour is up, meet back at the original meeting spot to turn in signs and check in.

Our purpose is not only to raise awareness of our neighbors being taken from us, but to hold sacred space and honor those who have been abducted and for their families who are dealing with the trauma of their loss.

• We hold these signs for each and every person languishing in detention centers across the US.

• We hold these signs in defiance of the fascism and the hate.

• We hold these signs to use our white privilege, for those of us who have it, and be the best allies we can be.

More about why we do this:

ICE activity in Salem has resulted in many of our neighbors being abducted over the past 18 months. The exact number is difficult to obtain, as ICE does not share information, but the local Rapid Response Team and PIRC (Portland Immigration Rights Coalition) data supports the number as being over 100 since Trump took office.

• Across the state, ICE has abducted over 2,500 individuals, 700 in August of this year. • Across the nation, ICE is ramping up numbers; also in August, 51,000 people were taken. • Most of which have no criminal record.

• Abductees are being warehoused in over 200 privately owned detention centers in the US, where they are held for months, or years, in deplorable conditions.

• There are documented cases of rape, abuse, malnutrition, bad water and food, restricted access to medical care and lawyers.

• GEO Group and Core Civic; the corporations who own most of the detention centers, earn $150 - $175 per person per day.

• Both corporations earned over 2 billion dollars in total revenue in 2025, with net profits exceeding $200 million.

• Half of the total revenue comes from ICE contracts.

Want to help us raise awareness?

events.title: Wind Changers Women's Gathering
events.description:
Wind Changers Women’s Gathering 2026:  2 night camp out. 

The “Wind Changers” represents a shift—a movement toward healing, restoration, connection, and renewed purpose. The Wind Changers Women’s Gathering is an intentional and sacred space created to bring women together for collective prayer, healing, meaningful connection, and empowerment.

In a world that can often feel isolating and overwhelming, this gathering provides a sanctuary where women from all walks of life can come together to build one another up, lift each other’s spirits, support one another, find motivation, and inspire each other.

The gathering is intentionally structured to help women move from isolation to community, creating an environment where women feel seen, heard, supported, and valued. Through shared experiences and meaningful connection, women are reminded that they do not have to walk through life alone.

The Gathering Will Provide:
Collective Prayer & Reflection: Creating a grounded and spiritually supportive environment where women can pause, reflect, reconnect, and renew their spirits.

Talking Circles: Providing safe and welcoming spaces for women to share their stories, express their experiences, release burdens, and receive mutual support without judgment.
Empowerment & Motivation: Creating impactful moments that inspire women to recognize their strength, build one another up, pursue their purpose with confidence, and encourage one another beyond the gathering.

Community Connection: Creating opportunities for fellowship, relationship-building, and meaningful connection so that no woman leaves feeling alone. The goal is for every participant to leave knowing she has a community around her.

We believe that when women have safe spaces to heal, connect, and grow, the impact extends far beyond the gathering itself. Women return to their families, communities, and neighborhoods renewed, strengthened, and empowered to become pillars of strength, hope, and positive change. 

At its heart, Wind Changers is about creating a shift within women that creates a ripple of change throughout families and communities. When women are supported, restored, connected, and empowered, they are better equipped to carry that strength, hope, healing, and purpose into the communities they call home.

Together, we can create a space where women feel seen, heard, supported, valued, and empowered—and where healing and connection become the beginning of lasting change.

events.title: Sexual and Domestic Violence Awareness Workshop
events.description:
Sexual Violence and Domestic Violence Workshops are designed to help you build resilience, develop skills to keep you and your loved ones safe, and create bonds with those who have been through the same experiences as well as educating and informing the public for prevention. Survivors deserve active, accessible and affordable advocacy, support and the right to heal on their own terms.

This group is ran by peers and volunteers with a few experts coming to speak to us at certain times also. We started this group because we know we have a serious lack of education surrounding this and even sex education itself and in rural areas, we lack these resources and education even more. In a world where there is so much violence put on our children and ourselves as women, we must find and create spaces where we feel safe, comfortable, heard and overall have the support we all need.

Every last Tuesday of the month 5-6pm. The majority of our workshops will be at the Peebles Library in their meeting room. Depending on weather, we may have locations outdoors, at a park or hiking location for the woods or even the private 3rd space we created where our community aid garden is. Our lead, Taryn, will be there to greet you and get us started at each of these groups and workshops.
We are allies and accomplices here.

5-6pm Sexual and Domestic Violence Educational Workshops
6-7pm Women's Support Group

There are no age restrictions only to make this accessible. We don't want to make younger children or your children who may need this group to feel like they can't be apart of it just because of their age. If they have experienced hardship or need a safe space just like we do, we will not be turning them away. We do understand that this could potentially keep conversations from being too deep but if enough girls or younger women would like to attend, we can start a support group for our youth.

Our sexual and domestic violence workshops are to bring awareness to ourselves and our youth to help prevent further violence against children and women. Both of these groups will be for survivors as well as the general public, those who want to learn more to help with prevention and education around sexual violence and assault.

What to Expect:
Bonding, Venting and Relating
Mutual Support
Trauma-Informing to Foster Healing
Education on Women’s Health
Sexual Violence Awareness + Education Workshops
Skill Building
Sharing Resources
Safety and Confidentiality

Specific Workshop Examples:
What is Sexual Violence, What is and Can be Considered Sexual Violence, Consent 101, What is Grooming, What are Warning Signs, Women’s Health and Anatomy, Self-Defense and more. In hopes we keep our children and community safe.

There are no age restrictions. Everyone is welcome. We all need to learn these things to help with prevention. We want these workshops and the support group to be as accessible as we possibly can, that includes rides and childcare. If you have children, you can bring them to the first group or workshop you attend if you need to. A kid’s club will begin once we find more volunteers to help us make this successful as well and we will have them during these times. Once we find enough volunteers and go through background checks, we will talk more about this at the our group meetings or workshops and spread the word more.
