events.title: Women’s Support Group
events.description:
Women's group is a support group to gather women who may have been through the same experiences, would like to share stories, resources and bond with others on a monthly basis. This group is ran by peers and volunteers with a few experts coming to speak to us at certain times also. We started this group because we personally know how it feels to be alone with no one to relate to or to talk to. In a world where there is so much violence put on our children and ourselves as women, we must find and create spaces where we feel safe, comfortable, heard and overall have the support we all need.

Every last Tuesday of the month 6-7pm. Most of our support groups and workshops will be at the Peebles Library in their meeting room. Depending on weather, we may have locations outdoors, at a park or hiking location or even the private 3rd space we created where our community aid garden is. Our lead, Taryn, will be there to greet you and get us started at each of these groups and workshops.
We are allies and accomplices here.

6-7pm Women's Support Group
5-6pm Sexual and Domestic Violence Educational Workshops

Survivors deserve active, accessible and affordable advocacy, support and the right to heal on their own terms. This group and the workshops are designed to help you build resilience, develop skills to keep you and your loved ones safe, and create bonds with those who have been through the same experiences as well as educating and informing the public for prevention.

There are no age restrictions only to make this accessible. We don't want to make younger children or your children who may need this group to feel like they can't be apart of it just because of their age. If they have experienced hardship or need a safe space just like we do, we will not be turning them away. We do understand that this could potentially keep conversations from being too deep but if enough girls or younger women would like to attend, we can start a support group for our youth.

Our sexual and domestic violence workshops are to bring awareness to ourselves and our youth to help prevent further violence against children and women. Both of these groups will be for survivors as well as the general public, those who want to learn more to help with prevention and education around Sexual Violence and Assault. For more information on these workshops, you can find that on the event pages of the Sexual Violence Awareness Workshops and on our community aid page too.

We want this group to be as accessible as we possibly can, that includes rides and childcare. If you have children, you can bring them to the first group or workshop you attend if you need to. A kid’s club will begin once we find more volunteers to help us make this successful as well and we will have them during these times. Once we find enough volunteers and go through background checks, we will talk more about this at the our group meetings or workshops and spread the word more. We’re working towards bringing our villages back. We can't have a village without villagers.

Coffee and snacks will be available too. We hope you join us. We all need someone or something. We’re here for you. No shame, no judgement, no exceptions.❤️‍🩹

We want to add to ensure it's known, when we say women, we are always including trans women as well as non-binary folks who may also need a support system. As soon as we find a better term to use for only women and non-binary folks, the name of this support group will change. We apologize to anyone who may feel left out or uncomfortable to the term Women's Support Group.

events.description:
**Join us for a virtual conversation between Food & Water Watch Founder & Executive Director Wenonah Hauter and Zephyr Teachout, author of _Anti-Monopoly: A Citizen’s Guide_.**

_Anti-Monopoly_ is being called a “movement-defining” book that dives deep into the battle between the forces of oligarchy and the rise of the anti-monopoly movement. Zephyr explains how anti-monopoly sentiment cuts across traditional political lines, gives real teeth to economic populism, and offers actionable ways to use people power to solve this problem together. 

Zephyr Teachout is an award-winning author, constitutional law professor, and nationally renowned democracy and anti-corruption activist. _The New York Times_ called her “the godmother of the current moment of dissatisfaction with establishment politics,” and she has inspired anti-monopoly legislation in states across the country. Her additional writings include the books _Corruption in America_ and _Break ’Em Up_ and articles featured in _The New York Times_, _The New York Review of Books_, _Foreign Affairs_, and _The Nation_. Zephyr serves as Board Chair for Food & Water Action and sits on the board of Food & Water Watch, helping guide strategies on clean water, safe food, and climate advocacy.

events.title: Save Democracy, Not the SAVE Act – Write to Your Members of Congress NOW!
events.description:
This a local Indivisible event!

Dear friends,

I am one of the millions of Americans who believes that voting is a fundamental right—not a privilege reserved for those who happen to have the right paperwork. But right now, Congress is trying to pass the SAVE America Act, a bill that would make it harder for eligible citizens to register and vote.

Our Votes Are in Danger!

Here's what's happening:

•	The SAVE America Act passed the House 218–213 on February 11, 2026

•	It requires documentary proof of citizenship—in person—to register to vote and photo ID to cast a ballot

•	Over 21 million eligible American citizens do not have proof of their citizenship readily available

•	It is an unfunded mandate that would cost states hundreds of millions of dollars with zero federal funding

•	The Senate has repeatedly failed to pass it, and even Republican leaders admit the votes aren't there

•	President Trump is now demanding that the Senate abolish the filibuster to force it through

📢 "Save Democracy, Not the SAVE Act" – That's Our Message

📝 Your Action: Write to Your Members of Congress

Step 1: Find Your Members of Congress

•	Find your U.S. Representative:
https://www.house.gov/representatives/find-your-representative

•	Find your U.S. Senators:
https://www.senate.gov/senators/senators-contact.htm

Step 2: Use This Template (Copy and Paste)

Subject: Save Democracy, Not the SAVE Act – Write to Your Members of Congress NOW!

Dear [Senator/Representative Last Name],

I am a constituent from [City, State], and I urge you to vote NO on the SAVE America Act (H.R. 7296 / S. 1383).
The SAVE America Act is a solution in search of a problem. It is essentially a backdoor poll tax, forcing 140 million Americans without a passport to pay fees for documents they do not have.

I ask you to:

1.	Vote NO on the SAVE America Act – in any form, whether standalone, attached to the NDAA, or included in reconciliation
2.	Support dedicated federal funding for election administration if any new requirements are imposed
3.	Oppose efforts to abolish the filibuster to force this bill through
President Trump has made clear the goal is to keep Republicans in power. As he stated, the bill is about ensuring his party maintains control of Congress. Our democracy is not a partisan tool.

Please act now. Our votes depend on it.
Sincerely,
[Your Full Name]
[Your Address]
[Your City, State, ZIP]

Step 3: Send It!

•	Use your members' official website contact forms (fastest)

•	Or email/call their offices directly

•	Call the Capitol Switchboard at (202) 224-3121 and ask to be connected

events.title: Progressive Democrats of Oklahoma — Monthly Meeting
events.description:
## Join Progressive Democrats of Oklahoma — In Person or Online!

**Looking for a way to connect with fellow progressives, get involved in your community, and help shape a better future for Oklahoma? We'd love to meet you!**

Join Progressive Democrats of Oklahoma (PDOk), the Oklahoma chapter of Progressive Democrats of America, for our monthly meeting! We gather in person at New Covenant Christian Church in Oklahoma City and online via Zoom.

Our monthly meetings are an opportunity to connect with like-minded Oklahomans, learn about issues and elections affecting our communities, share ideas, and explore meaningful ways to make a difference.

**Whether you're a longtime progressive, newly interested in political organizing, or simply curious about what we do, there's a place for you at the table.** No previous involvement or experience is necessary!

### Turning Progressive Values Into Action

We believe meaningful change starts with people coming together. Across Oklahoma, our members work to strengthen communities and advance progressive priorities through:

- Voter registration and voter education
- Get Out the Vote (GOTV) initiatives
- Supporting local, state, and national campaigns
- Phone banking and grassroots organizing
- Building connections and strengthening communities
- Collaborating with other organizations and community partners

There's no single way to get involved. Whether you're ready to take action, looking to meet others who share your values, or just want to learn more, we welcome your participation.

### Stay Connected!

**Want the Zoom link or more information?** Join our GroupMe community at **tinyurl.com/PDOkla** to connect with members, ask questions, and stay informed about upcoming meetings and opportunities.

We hope to see you at our next meeting!

---

**A note about our meeting location:** Progressive Democrats of Oklahoma is an independent political organization and is not affiliated with New Covenant Christian Church or any religious institution. Our meetings are secular and open to people of all religious beliefs and backgrounds, including those with no religious affiliation. New Covenant Christian Church generously provides meeting space and is an open and affirming congregation that welcomes all people into its building.

events.title: Facilitating The Learning Environment

Facilitating the Learning Environment:

Participants will be able to design equitable physical learning spaces that support engagement and access; co-create norms, routines, and procedures that foster trust, safety, and belonging; and implement behavior responses that promote student growth, accountability, and skill development.

events.title: Engaging Every Learner
events.description:
Engaging Every Learner: 

Participants will be able to explain how diversity, equity, inclusion, and social-emotional learning shape instruction and engagement; apply current research that expands Jacob Kounin’s group-management principles; plan lessons and strategies that engage every learner; and reflect on their group-management strengths and growth areas to identify improvements.

events.title: Principles of Instruction
events.description:
Principles of Instruction: 

Participants will be able to explain the social context of learning and its instructional implications; analyze knowledge development within the Zone of Proximal Development; apply cognitive and metacognitive strategies that foster independent learning; and design high-quality lessons that expand access, engagement, and opportunities for all students to demonstrate mastery.

events.title: Feedback for Deeper Learning
events.description:
Feedback for Deeper Learning: 

Participants will be able to distinguish effective feedback from other classroom communication; gather student feedback to inform instruction, elevate student voice, and promote agency; provide timely, actionable feedback aligned with individual needs and learning goals; and use purposeful questioning and discussion to deepen learning and foster meaningful feedback exchanges.

events.title: Maximizing Learning Time:
events.description:
Maximizing Learning Time:

Participants will be able to identify the time constraints including allocated time, engaged time, and academic learning time; understand the relationship between required learning time and actual time spent learning; account for lost learning time; and learn strategies for maximizing learner engagement.

events.description:
2026 #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence

Beginning Wednesday, December 9, 2026 until the end of December, we will come together across the nation to host the #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence.

These local events will be anchored by the 14th Annual National Vigil for All Victims of Gun Violence on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C.—held near the 14-year mark of the Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting tragedy, when a 20-year-old gunman armed with an AR-15 hunted and murdered 20 first graders and six educators.

Across the country, vigils (as simple as lighting candles) and gatherings will honor lives stolen by gun violence, uplift survivors, raise awareness, and demand urgent action from our leaders to finally end this epidemic. From schools and workplaces to houses of worship, neighborhoods, grocery stores, homes, nightclubs, streets, and even our democracy itself—gun violence impacts every aspect of American life.

The theme of this year’s campaign is #FreedomToLive—the simple, powerful idea that every person deserves to live free from the daily threat of gunfire. Together, survivors, families, advocates, and allies will raise our voices to ensure that FREEDOM means the right of every person to live, learn, work, worship, speak, vote, and gather without the daily fear of gun violence.

We stand in solidarity with over 1.4 million Americans who have been shot since Sandy Hook, with every community devastated by gun violence for decades. We will send a clear message to our local, state, and federal lawmakers, raise awareness, and help build the movement for common-sense solutions.

Let’s #HonorWithAction together. Let’s demand freedom from gun violence.

events.title: WEBINAR: Reproductive Justice for Transgender, Gender Non-Conforming and Intersex People!
events.description:
Throughout 2025, Equality California Institute conducted message testing to identify tools and framing to empower TGI (Transgender, Gender Non-Conforming, and Intersex) people seeking reproductive justice and sexual health care. Join us for a webinar to walk through the process and findings from this inquiry.

This work was conducted with funding from the California Department of Public Health and in partnership with Goodwin Simon Strategic Research, TransLatin@ Coalition, Unique Woman's Coalition, Invisible Men, and Gender Justice LA.

events.title: March for Our Democracy: The Fight Isn't Over
events.description:
We are taking to the streets, because we know this fight isn’t over. Voters decided, and now we need to make it count.

Americans across the country voted for candidates who presented a vision of bold change, accountability, and never shied away from demanding a future that works for us, not authoritarian wannabes and their billionaire buddies. 

We’ve heard it. Now, we're going to make sure it happens.

What: March for Democracy
When: Saturday, November 7, 2026
Time: 12 PM
Location: Times Square

A core principle behind all Hands Off NYC events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Interfaith Prayer Meeting for Peace is a collaboration of people of faith from various organizations. We grieve this administration’s assault on human dignity and life at home and abroad. We grieve ruthless corporate war profiteering. So we meet monthly in the shadow of the largest weapons manufacturer on the globe, and across the street from the largest luxury mall in the nation, to pray and bear witness that a better world is possible.

NOTE: Time of event is approximate and will be finalized by email!

As people of faith and conscience committed to peaceful, legal, prayerful presence, we agree to the following:

We agree to respect “that of God in every person” and refrain from hostile language and insults.

We agree to leave room for repentance in those with whom we disagree and to oppose violence, not people.

We agree to trust the Divine to bring about peace, shalom and wholeness in our world.

We agree to follow all legal instructions from law enforcement.

We agree to quickly cooperate with peacekeeper and Meeting facilitator directions that are for our safety.

As an interfaith gathering, we agree to exercise freedom of expression and respect the freedom of expression of others. If you have a prayer, reading, song, or other activity, it will represent your faith and conscience with integrity. If someone else’s sharing does not align with your faith and conscience, you are free to abstain from participating during that moment.

events.title: Kits of Care: Pack with Purpose! 🧡
events.description:
🧡 Kits of Care: Pack with Purpose!

You’ve been donating. Now let’s get packing! 🙌

Over the past two months, we’ve been collecting supplies for three types of kits to share with community members served by Partners for Our Communities (POC):

🍪 Christmas Cookie Jars filled with baking ingredients and a recipe for a homemade holiday treat.
💜 Period Kits with menstrual care essentials.
🎒 Unhoused Kits with personal care items for neighbors experiencing homelessness.

Donations are coming along beautifully, and now it’s time to bring everyone together for our first assembly event!

📅 Saturday, November 14 | 1–3 PM
📍 Countryside Church Unitarian Universalist (CCUU), Palatine

We’re looking for 50+ volunteers to help put together 150 Christmas Cookie Jars, 150 Period Kits, and 75 Unhoused Kits. That’s 375 kits packed with care in one afternoon!

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 This is a kid-friendly event! Bring your family or a friend. Kids and adults can decorate cards with cheerful messages, fill jars, and pack supplies. No experience needed. We’ll show you what to do! This is a great opportunity for teens to get volunteer hours!

🎁 There’s still time to donate! Check out the list of items we still need: [Kits of Care Flyers - 11/1/26](http://tinyurl.com/KitsOfCare1101)

Whether you’ve donated supplies or are joining us for the first time, we’d love to have you there. Come meet your neighbors, learn about Partners for Our Communities and the services they provide, and help care for others! 🧡

We will have a second packing day on Sat, Jan 23rd. Look for the Sign up in December.

Sponsored by Indivisible Barrington, Countryside Church Unitarian Universalist (CCUU), and Partners for Our Communities (POC).

Come join the Bellaire/Braeswood Democrats and the West University Area Democrats at the November 9, 2026 meeting with Jeremy Wallace of the Houston Chronicle.  Jeremy will analyze what just happened on November 3rd and what to expect will happen going forward because of the results.

Jeremy Wallace has covered politics and campaigns for more than 20 years. Before joining the Hearst Texas newspapers in 2017, he covered government and politics for the Tampa Bay Times, The Miami Herald and the Sarasota Herald-Tribune. Previously he covered Congress for the Boston Globe and Detroit Free-Press. Originally from San Antonio, he attended the University of North Texas and earned his bachelor’s degree from the University of Missouri.

Jeremy also authors the Texas Take with Jeremy Wallace newsletter, where he shares insights from inside the Capitol.  Work on the Texas Take has him frequently on CNN, PBS, BBC America, MSNBC and statewide NPR stations.

Location: West University Community Center at 6104 Auden St. 77005

location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Great Scott Farms is graciously extending a field to harvest fresh produce for families in need. This is a great way to way to give back, enjoy the outdoors, and share in meaningful community service.

All are welcome! The more hands we have to help- the more produce we can recover! Produce is available for anyone in need. 

We are beginning many gleans at 11am due to private gleans that are scheduled on the same day. The private groups will only be gleaning for an hour so there should be plenty of produce left over to rescue. 

If you would like to be a receiving agency please reach out to the leading coordinator or Megan at (863) 224-0403. 

🌱 What to Bring:

✅ Closed-toe shoes (required)

✅ Comfortable clothing that can get messy

✅ Hat, sunscreen, and gloves (optional but helpful)

✅ A reusable water bottle to stay hydrated

📢 RSVP or Questions? 
Contact:
Megan McEwen
📞 (863) 224-0403
📧 fl-glean@endhunger.org

### Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

#### 1. What is gleaning?

- Gleaning is collecting leftover crops from farms that would otherwise go to waste. These fresh fruits and vegetables are then donated to food banks and hunger relief groups.

#### 2. Who can attend?

- All are welcome—no prior experience needed! Perfect for families, small groups, or anyone looking to serve. (Kids must be with an adult.)

#### 3. Are tools provided?
- Yes! We’ll supply any tools and bags you’ll need to glean.

#### 4. What if it rains?

- We’ll monitor the weather and let you know if anything changes. Safety first!

#### 5. Where does the food go?

- All the produce goes directly to local food banks and community partners feeding those in need. If you are an organization in need - reach out to the event coordinator to become a recipient. 

#### 6. How can I stay in the loop?

- For event updates, visit: https://www.mobilize.us/endhunger/

#### 7. Other FAQs :

- NO smoking, NO pets

events.title: Alcona County Canvass Observation

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Since November 2020, the League of Women Voters of Michigan and their Pro-Democracy Partners have worked to be the public’s eyes and ears at Michigan’s county canvass of votes cast during an election. Each year they work together to ensure that trained volunteers observe County Board of Canvassers (BOC) meetings, across the state of Michigan, watching the process by which local results are reviewed and certified.

This consistent, nonpartisan observation promotes transparency and accountability, helps identify potential issues that could put timely certification at risk, and reassures Board of Canvassers members and election staff that the public is engaged in their work. Should observation uncover anything beyond the canvassers’ ministerial, nondiscretionary duties, LWVMI can elevate the issue to the Secretary of State’s office or an election attorney.

### Your Role As An Observer:
- Our BOC Observer are an important aspect of our volunteer election work! 
- Our observers not only serve to build trust in the community as well as between local government and the League, but they also help to ensure our elections are running as the laws intended. 
- Reporting from our observers helps us understand the health of our democratic systems, where issues are happening, and where things are running smoothly.  
- These insights are important to all of us working to support our democracy, and ultimately support our communities in ensuring their voices are heard! 

We hope you will join us, volunteer, and bring a friend to be a part of this election work!

PS: Shifts are subject to change, as county clerks work to finalize the details of the county canvass. If your shift is cancelled, you will be contacted by a representative from the League of Women Voters.

events.title: Brookline Rally for Democracy, December 2026
events.description:
Brookline Rally for Democracy

Every Saturday at 1:00 PM | Coolidge Corner

Join members of three Brookline pro-democracy groups — indivisible Activist Evenings, Brookline Pax, and Speak Out, Seniors! — for our weekly rally at Coolidge Corner.

We gather to raise our voices and our signs in defense of democracy, justice, and decency — and to stand united against the abuses of the Trump administration and the forces that threaten our rights and freedoms.

We stand for:

• Immigrant rights, human rights, and racial justice

• Free speech, the Constitution, and the rule of law

• Access to health and healthcare for all

• Protection of our planet and the future we leave to the next generation

We choose empathy over cruelty, peace over violence, and hope over fear.

Our rallies are peaceful, spirited, and uplifting — a chance to connect, recharge, and stand up for what matters. Bring your friends, your voice, and your sign (or borrow one of ours!).

All are welcome!  The rally is multi-generational and family-friendly; those using walkers or other mobility devices may use them to sit to participate.

In the event of inclement weather, we’ll each use our best judgment about whether to attend. We hope you’ll do the same! 

Please join us, one rally at a time.  We’ll continue for as long as it takes.
events.accessibility_notes: All are welcome, including participants with walkers, wheelchairs, scooters, and other mobility devices.

events.title: Kanawha County IEP Circle
events.description:
IEP Circles WV is a parent-led community where families of exceptional learners come together to find support, build knowledge, and create change. If you're navigating an IEP, 504 Plan, evaluations, school communication, or accessing services, these gatherings are designed to help you feel informed, connected, and supported.

Each meeting brings caregivers together with experienced advocates, education attorneys, and community partners who provide practical guidance, answer questions, and facilitate meaningful discussions. You'll have opportunities to share experiences, learn from other families, discover helpful resources, and build lasting relationships with people who understand the challenges you face.

Beyond individual support, IEP Circles helps families understand the larger issues affecting special education. We'll explore how school funding, staffing shortages, IDEA funding, and state and federal policy decisions impact the services available to students. By connecting personal experiences to these broader challenges, families can better understand why obstacles exist and how they can work alongside educators and other parents to improve public education.

For those interested in taking the next step, IEP Circles also offers opportunities to develop advocacy skills through workshops on legislative advocacy, storytelling, public speaking, community organizing, and civic engagement. Whether you simply want support or hope to help shape the future of special education in West Virginia, you'll find a welcoming community where your experiences are valued and your voice matters.

Together, we can strengthen support for our children, build stronger communities, and advocate for a public education system that works for every student.

events.title: Keweenaw County Canvass Observation

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Since November 2020, the League of Women Voters of Michigan and their Pro-Democracy Partners have worked to be the public’s eyes and ears at Michigan’s county canvass of votes cast during an election. Each year they work together to ensure that trained volunteers observe County Board of Canvassers (BOC) meetings, across the state of Michigan, watching the process by which local results are reviewed and certified.

This consistent, nonpartisan observation promotes transparency and accountability, helps identify potential issues that could put timely certification at risk, and reassures Board of Canvassers members and election staff that the public is engaged in their work. Should observation uncover anything beyond the canvassers’ ministerial, nondiscretionary duties, LWVMI can elevate the issue to the Secretary of State’s office or an election attorney.

### Your Role As An Observer:
- Our BOC Observer are an important aspect of our volunteer election work! 
- Our observers not only serve to build trust in the community as well as between local government and the League, but they also help to ensure our elections are running as the laws intended. 
- Reporting from our observers helps us understand the health of our democratic systems, where issues are happening, and where things are running smoothly.  
- These insights are important to all of us working to support our democracy, and ultimately support our communities in ensuring their voices are heard! 

We hope you will join us, volunteer, and bring a friend to be a part of this election work!

**Shifts are subject to change, as county clerks work to finalize the details of the county canvass. If your shift is cancelled, you will be contacted by a representative from the League of Women Voters.**

events.title: Banned Book Club - To Kill A Mockingbird by Harper Lee
events.description:
For the remainder of October and throughout November we will be exploring How To Kill A Mockingbird by Harper Lee. I feel it is important to advise that this book may have triggers for some people. If you feel you might not be in an emotional space to handle the topics mentioned, or that this title just isn't for you, please feel free to skip parts or the book in full and stay tuned for December's title.

Content Trigger Warnings for To Kill A Mockingbird by Harper Lee include the following subjects:

• Abuse
• Murder
• N-word
• Racism
• Rape (mentioned)

Join us each month for a new book from our ever growing banned or challenged book list. Where we choose a new title each month and combine reading out loud in a group setting, reading alone, and discussing how the books might correspond to the world around us.

This month we will finish To Kill A Mockingbird by Harper Lee.

Please make sure to add any suggestions to the Google spreadsheet shared in the Zoom chat before the third week of the month to have a chance at it being selected for the next month. The event name will be updated once the title is selected.

The meetings are 90 minutes long and broke down into 3 parts. The first half hour is spent discussing the section that was designed or our anticipations on what the book might be like. The middle section we read out loud, and the last half hour is spent going over what we read and assigning the next section.

So far we have read the following titles and discussed how they correlate with our present day. 

• The Diary of a Yong Girl - Anne Frank 
• 1984 - George Orwell 
• Animal Farm - George Orwell 
• Fahrenheit 451 – Ray Bradbury 
• Looking Backward – Edward Bellamy 
• The Age of Reason - Thomas Paine 
• Howl and Other Poems - Allen Ginsberg
• Civil Disobedience - Henry David Thoreau

All are welcome and even if you haven’t picked up the book feel free to join us for the discussion and reading.

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Florida NOW Film Screening: Reimagining Safety
events.description:
Join us as we close out the series with a screening of Reimagining Safety, a documentary filmed in the aftermath of the 2020 murder of George Floyd and the worldwide protests that followed. The film brings together 10 experts, including abolitionists, social workers, scholars, a former LAPD detective, and a former district attorney, to examine how policing and incarceration shape our ideas about safety.

The film revisits the 2020 protests and the growing calls to defund and abolish the police, while exploring the history and ongoing impact of police violence, racism, mass incarceration, mental health crises, housing insecurity, and the criminalization of poverty. It also highlights restorative justice, violence prevention, community responders, and other approaches that seek to build safety through care, accountability, and community rather than punishment and isolation.

Stay after the screening for our final community reflection and conversation in this series.

events.title: 24th Annual ReLeafing Day at Glen Leven Farm!
events.description:
Join the Nashville Tree Foundation for the 24th Annual ReLeafing Day!

Held each year on the Saturday before Thanksgiving, ReLeafing Day is our signature community tree-planting event. Following the devastating 1998 tornadoes, our founders launched this initiative as a major restoration effort - raising $1,000,000 in six months and planting over 6,000 trees across the city. Today, that legacy continues as we focus on planting new trees in Nashville every November.

This year, we invite you to dig deep and plant trees at the beautiful Glen Leven Farm on Saturday, November 21st. We are proud to be supported by Root Nashville, helping drive the citywide goal of planting 500,000 trees by 2050, and funded by the Cumberland River Compact.

Whether you are an experienced tree planter or a first-time volunteer, this is the perfect way to connect with nature, meet fellow tree lovers, and actively grow our urban forest!

What to Expect: 
We will start the morning with a brief introduction and an overview of the day's goals. Our team will provide a step-by-step tree planting demonstration and review essential safety guidelines so you feel completely confident. Then, we'll plant our trees!

events.title: A District That Works for Children, Youth, and Families
events.description:
**What would it take to build a District that truly works for all children, youth, and families?**

That’s what we will be asking at our end-of-year summit on **Thursday, December 3, from 6:30-8:00 pm.** At DC Action, we’re bringing together the DC Out-of-School Time Coalition, Under 3 DC, and the Youth Economic Justice Coalition to lead a bold conversation with the mayor-elect and elected leaders from across the District, and we want you to join us. 

This is a critical moment for the District, with a new mayor for the first time in a dozen years, major turnover on the council, and continued uncertainty about the economy. The budget and policy decisions made over the coming months, and the plans carried out in the next few years, will impact the District for generations to come. 

It’s vital that the needs of Black and brown children, youth, and families be at the center of these discussions. That’s why this event will be led by young people, parents, and direct service providers from the three coalitions, who will share their experiences and what they want to see from our elected leaders, from making child care more affordable, to expanding out-of-school time programs, and committing to ending youth homelessness.


**Doors open at 5:30pm.**

The School Board of Lee County sets the policies and rules that govern the administration of the District. The Board operates according to Florida law and Florida Department of Education regulations, and it sets policy when members meet in official session.

That makes School Board meetings an important place for our community to be present and engaged.

Whether you are a parent, educator, student, or community member, we invite you to join FSPS-Lee to:

events.title: Lee County School Board Workshop
events.description:
Join FSPS-Lee at the Lee County School Board Workshop

Join Families for Strong Public Schools – Lee Chapter as we attend the Lee County School Board Workshop to stay informed and engaged in the conversations shaping our public schools.

What is a School Board Workshop?

A workshop is different from a regular School Board meeting. Regular meetings are where the Board takes formal action and votes on agenda items. Workshops are primarily working sessions where Board members receive information, ask questions, discuss issues in greater detail, and explore potential policies or decisions before they may come back for formal action.

That makes workshops an important part of the public decision-making process.

By the time an issue reaches a final vote, Board members may have already spent significant time discussing it during workshops. Attending or tuning in gives families and community members an opportunity to understand what is being considered earlier in the process—not just when it is time for a vote.

Why Tune In or Attend?

📚 Get informed early about issues and proposals that could affect Lee County public schools.

👀 See the process in action and hear the questions, concerns, and priorities Board members raise as they consider an issue.

📝 Be better prepared to advocate when an issue moves forward for future discussion or action.

🤝 Stay connected with FSPS-Lee and other community members working to support strong public schools.

You don't need to be an education policy expert to participate. You can simply attend, listen, learn, and become more familiar with how decisions affecting our schools are made.

Strong community engagement doesn't begin when the Board takes a vote. It begins by paying attention throughout the process.

Our schools. Our community. Our voice. 💙

Join FSPS-Lee at the workshop or tune in and stay informed about what's happening in Lee County public schools.

events.title: Lee County Public Schools Coalition Launch
events.description:
Lee County Public Schools Coalition Launch
Saturday, November 14, 2026
1:30 PM – 4:00 PM
Fort Myers Regional Library — Meeting Rooms (Separate Building)
Fort Myers, Florida

Families for Strong Public Schools Lee invites local organizations, community leaders, parent groups, educators, advocacy organizations, and other partners to join us for a collaborative gathering focused on one shared goal:
Strengthening public schools in Lee County.

This will be an opportunity for groups from across our community to come together, build relationships, share priorities, and strategize about how we can more effectively support students, educators, families, and strong public education.

We know there are many organizations throughout Lee County already doing important work. Rather than working in separate silos, we want to create opportunities to connect our efforts, share information, identify common goals, and build a stronger coalition for our public schools.

What to Expect

Join us for light refreshments and an informal but productive conversation about:
The biggest challenges currently facing Lee County public schools
Opportunities for collaboration between community organizations
Supporting and amplifying educators, parents, students, and school
communities
Improving public awareness and engagement around education issues
Coordinating advocacy and community outreach
Identifying shared priorities and opportunities for collective action
Creating stronger communication between organizations working to support public education

This is not about every organization agreeing on every issue. It is about finding the areas where we do agree and determining how we can work together to make a greater impact.

Who Should Attend?

We welcome representatives from parent and family organizations, education advocacy groups, teacher and employee organizations, civic and community organizations, neighborhood and grassroots groups, student organizations, nonprofits, faith and community partners, and other organizations whose work intersects with our children.

events.title: Urgent Opposition to Livestreaming Nidal Hasan’s Execution – Write to Your Members of Congress NOW!
events.description:
This a local Indivisible event!

Dear Representative [Last Name],

I am writing as your constituent to express my profound objection to the Pentagon’s announced plan to livestream the execution by firing squad of Nidal Hasan, scheduled for December 3, 2026. This would be the first military execution in more than 60 years and the first public execution in the United States in nearly a century. I strongly urge you to publicly oppose this decision and to exercise congressional oversight to prevent the Department of Defense from turning a solemn act of military justice into a public spectacle.

I want to be clear: my objection is not rooted in sympathy for Hasan or in any doubt about the gravity of his crimes. He murdered 13 unarmed soldiers and wounded more than 30 others at Fort Hood in 2009, and he has never claimed innocence. The families of the victims and the survivors deserve justice and closure. But justice and spectacle are not the same thing, and the decision to livestream this execution is a profound mistake that will harm our nation’s moral standing, endanger our security, and undermine the very principles we claim to uphold.

The livestream would violate fundamental human rights standards.

The United Nations human rights office has warned that livestreaming an execution would amount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition on torture under international law. A UN spokesperson described the prospect of a government executing someone “in front of live cameras” as “abhorrent”. Amnesty International has condemned the plan as “reprehensible,” noting that international human rights bodies have long found public executions incompatible with the prohibition on cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment. The United States should not join the ranks of nations that carry out public executions; according to Amnesty International, only Iran and Afghanistan are known to have done so in 2025. This is not who we are—or who we should aspire to be.

The livestream would make us less safe, not more.

Senator Jack Reed, Ranking Member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, has warned that livestreaming the execution “only gives the shooter what he wants: more attention and more control” and that it is “a gift to anti-American terrorist recruiters”. Congressman Jason Crow, a former Army Ranger, has similarly stated that a public execution “only gives our adversaries fodder for anti-American propaganda that makes us less safe”. Hasan has said he acted to stop soldiers from deploying to Afghanistan; broadcasting his death to a global audience would hand extremists a powerful recruitment tool and validate their narrative that America is at war with Islam. The last thing our national security needs is a propaganda victory for those who wish us harm.

The livestream would degrade our military and our legal system.

Army Regulation 190-55 governs who may witness military executions and does not provide for unrestricted public attendance. There is no regulation or precedent for a military execution to be livestreamed, and experts have noted that public executions are typically held in authoritarian countries to instill fear and demonstrate government power. Republican Senator Thom Tillis has said that public executions are what “oppressive dictatorships do” and called the plan “beyond disgusting”. Democratic Senator Chris Murphy accused the Secretary of Defense of “mimicking ISIS”. When lawmakers from both parties use the same language to describe an American policy that they use for our enemies, something has gone deeply wrong.

The livestream would traumatize victims and survivors.

Alonzo Lunsford, a former Army sergeant who was shot seven times during the attack and who plans to attend the execution in person, has said he does not agree with making the event publicly available without censorship. The families of the fallen and the survivors deserve to mourn and to seek closure in a manner that respects their dignity, not to have their trauma broadcast to the world as entertainment. As Senator John Curtis has warned, a civilization “erodes when it cultivates an appetite for executions as a form of entertainment”.

What I am asking of you. I respectfully urge you to take the following actions:

1.	Publicly denounce the Pentagon’s plan to livestream Hasan’s execution and call on Secretary Hegseth to reverse the decision. Bipartisan voices—including Senators Reed, Tillis, Murkowski, and Curtis, and Representatives Crow and Smith—have already spoken out. Your voice would add needed weight.
2.	Exercise congressional oversight. The House and Senate Armed Services Committees should demand transparency regarding the legal authority for this livestream, the financial arrangements (including any potential monetization), and the consultation process that led to this decision. A letter from former national security officials has already raised serious questions about whether the execution could be used for “commercial gain or partisan political propaganda”. Congress must investigate.
3.	Support legislative or regulatory action to ensure that no future military execution is livestreamed or otherwise made available to the public for entertainment or political purposes. The default should be the solemn, limited-witness procedure prescribed by Army Regulation 190-55.

The death penalty itself is a matter of serious moral and legal debate, and I respect that Americans of good faith disagree on it. But whatever one’s position on capital punishment, livestreaming an execution is beyond the pale. It is cruel, it is dangerous, and it is beneath the dignity of the United States. Hasan’s crimes were horrific, but responding with a public spectacle does not honor his victims—it exploits them. It does not strengthen the rule of law—it makes a mockery of it. And it does not make us safer—it makes us a recruiting poster for our enemies.

I urge you to act swiftly and forcefully. Please let me know what steps you plan to take.

Respectfully,

[Your Name]
[Your Address]
[City, State, ZIP]
[Email Address]
[Phone Number]

events.title: Public Hearing: Tell IDEM Not to Rubber-Stamp Amazon Jasper County Data Center's Dirty Diesel Permit
events.description:
The Indiana Department of Environmental Management (IDEM) has published a draft air permit for Amazon’s Project Orion AI data center, a sprawling 13-building complex under development in Wheatfield that would allow about 384 polluting backup diesel generators — millions of gallons of fuel — near homes and right next to the Schahfer coal and gas plants and the Kankakee River watershed, which will be impacted by tens of millions of gallons of discharge and intake daily from the cumulative impact of these facilities. 

Amazon's own filings show the data center would release thousands of tons of smog-forming air pollution and carbon monoxide each year without strict controls, impacting Jasper County residents, farm families, and downwind neighbors. 

Jasper County deserves clean air now! Join the virtual public hearing on November 10th to tell IDEM to protect our communities and airways from Amazon’s dirty diesel generators permit. 

*The hearing begins at 6:00 PM CT and will conclude as soon as public comments are done, or no later than 9:00 PM CT.

Please sign and share our petition to send a quick comment on the permit: www.jtnwi.org/no-dirty-diesel-amazon.

And use our toolkit to develop your comments and learn more about the permit: www.jtnwi.org/amazon-hearing-toolkit.

events.title: After the Midterms -- Now What? with Professor Sam Wang
events.description:
We now know the outcomes of the 2026 midterm elections, and after we've whooped and hollered and danced ourselves into oblivion, it's time to regroup. How should we move forward in our efforts to engage voters, protect the vulnerable, and expand democracy? Happily, there's no one better to strategize with than Professor Sam Wang. Many of us were impressed with Dr. Wang when he ran for US Congress in NJ's 12th district, and we are thrilled to have the opportunity to hear from him again. He'll address key takeaways from the election, how to think about the impacts both short- and long-term, and what this means for our local activism. Please join us for this lively and thought-provoking discussion!

**About Sam Wang**

Sam Wang is a professor of neuroscience at Princeton University and a pioneer in the fight for our democracy and against gerrymandering. He has authored books on how the brain functions, and he worked on science and education policy in the US Senate. In 2026, he ran for the US Congress in New Jersey's 12th Congressional District, and while he didn't win in the primary election, for many of us, he won our highest regard. 

Sam is now continuing the campaign in the form of Third Mountain Action, an organization to save and rebuild democracy and science.

events.title: Signs of Solidarity: Teaching local businesses about ICE

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Canvass local businesses in Lavergne/Smyrna and share practical information about what businesses can do if ICE comes to their workplace—including steps to help protect the rights and safety of employees and customers. Everyone is encouraged to volunteer to help, and we especially need Spanish-speakers.

The Trump administration is sending ICE deep into communities to spread fear among immigrants. Many families—including citizens—are now afraid to go to work, shop, or go about daily life. 

We want to show immigrants they are welcome and essential to our communities. We go to local businesses and ask them to post signs supporting immigrant neighbors and rejecting ICE intimidation, and help them create private employee-only spaces that ICE cannot legally enter without a signed judicial warrant.

Results from previous canvasses: Over 300 businesses canvassed, 
over 40 volunteers, over 200 signs, and "know your rights" pamphlets accepted.

Never canvassed before? We got you! You do not go alone. We pair newcomers with experienced folks. 

We will email training material that needs to be reviewed prior the event via Mobilize after you RSVP. Please register by Thursday, 11/5 so we can group volunteers into teams.

In response to these recent events, we are offering a dedicated online support space for local community activists. This will be a safe space to process any grief & loss that’s coming up, as well as a space to learn about vicarious trauma and compassion fatigue.

events.description:
For our November monthly meeting, Duluth Indivisible has asked Megan Peterson and Erin Maye Quade, the Executive Director and Senior Advisor, respectively, of [Gender Justice](https://www.genderjustice.us/) to present on "Gender and Authoritarianism". Because we are meeting in person and they are presenting on Zoom, we've decided to offer the Zoom version throughout MN08. Hence this Zoom version of the event. People who register will get the Zoom link a few hours before the event. 

Authoritarians regularly use gender as a wedge issue to create fear, divide people, and reinforce traditional hierarchies and patriarchy. The Trump regime is following this playbook on many fronts: trans youth participation in sports, Hegseth's attacks on diversity in the military, the SAVE Act to disenfranchise women voters, blocking health care for trans youth, and on and on. Gender Justice's presentation will outline these issues in a potent and coherent way and better equip us to protect the rights of ALL people to live fully and freely with respect to gender. 

We will still meet in person in Duluth for a potluck at 5:00 PM, with the presentation at 6:00, followed by discussion and planning on how gender advocacy might fit into our 2027 planning. To sign up for the **in-person session**, please do so through this Mobilize link: [Gender and Authoritarianism: In Person](https://www.mobilize.us/duluthindivisible/event/1040294/)

Please spread the word.

events.title: Sunrise Orlando @ Public Comment: Orange County Board of Commissioners Meeting
events.description:
### Speak with Sunrise Orlando during Public Comment @ Orange County Board of County Commissioners Meeting! 🌅

Join us for the Orange County Board of County Commissioners' weekly Public Comment to learn and discuss the decisions being made in our county, connect with the community, and advocate for a more affordable, walkable, and sustainable Orlando.

**What is Public Comment?**

Public Comment refers to the period scheduled during the beginning of the morning session of the Board of County Commissioners’ meeting. It is time set aside at each BCC meeting for members of the public to speak on general topics of interest or concern within the BCC’s authority.

**What does Public Comment with Sunrise Orlando look like?**

When participating in public comment with us, you can expect to:

- Meet up with Sunrise Orlando members and community supporters.
- Attend the public meeting together in the morning.

- Participate in public comment if appropriate and available.

- Learn how local decisions affect our communities and how we can take action.

You don't need to be a Sunrise Orlando member or a policy expert to join us! Whether it's your first public meeting or you're one of our regulars, we'll be there to help you with talking points, information, and encouragement!

events.title: Lifeline DC 2027: Walk For Lives
events.description:
On Saturday, September 11, 2027, we walk together in Washington, D.C.

Walk for Lives D.C. is the closing day of Lifeline DC, three days in the nation’s capital following Hill Day and the Synthetic Drug Summit. It brings the families, survivors, and advocates who walked in their own cities and towns in May to the National Mall, side by side, in one place.

We walk for the sons and daughters, brothers and sisters, parents and friends we have lost to fentanyl. We walk for the families still in the fight, and for the young people we can still protect. Every step says the same thing to the country: these lives mattered, and this crisis demands a response.

We walk on a date this nation already holds for remembrance. We carry that spirit with us, honoring every life that should still be here.

What to expect

A morning program with family speakers and a moment of silence
A gentle, accessible walk of about one mile, open to all ages and abilities
A Community Resource Village with treatment, recovery, and public health organizations
Time to connect with families who understand

Bring a sign. Carry the name or photo of someone you love, or a message you want Washington to see.

Schedule [CONFIRM]

8:30 AM: Check-in opens
9:00 AM: Opening program
10:30 AM: Walk steps off
11:00 AM to 12:30 PM: Community Resource Village

Location [CONFIRM]
Floral Library Gardens, Tidal Basin, National Mall, Washington, D.C.
Nearest Metro: Smithsonian (Blue, Orange, Silver lines)

Walk for Lives D.C. is free and open to everyone. Please register so we can plan for you, and share this event with someone who should be walking beside you.

Can’t be in D.C.? Walk for Lives returns to cities and towns across America on Saturday, May 15, 2027.

About United Against Fentanyl
United Against Fentanyl is a nonpartisan, nonprofit organization that interrupts the use of illicit fentanyl through innovative, bold, and effective initiatives.

Questions? info@unitedagainstfentanyl.org

events.title: Tending Environmental Grief: Part Two
events.description:
We are living in an era of significant environmental change and loss. In recognizing that these times are challenging to live in, adapt to, and cope with, it’s essential that we come together as a community to process our experiences. Join Sky Island Alliance and [Maria Renée](https://www.maria-renee.com/) on Thursday, Dec. 10, at 9:30 a.m. for a dedicated time to understand the terrain of environmental grief, work through emotions, celebrate this beautiful region, and practice building resilience together. This free webinar is the second in a series of opportunities to contribute your creative responses to a changing region, whether they come from grief, hope, or anything in between. Participants will have a chance to share their reflections and experiences in response to a series of prompts this fall.

_See [Tending Environmental Grief: Part One](https://skyislandalliance.org/2026/10/tending-to-environmental-grief/) >>>_

events.title: Banned Book Club - December's Title TBD
events.description:
Join us each month for a new book from our ever growing banned or challenged book list. Where we choose a new title each month and combine reading out loud in a group setting, reading alone, and discussing how the books might correspond to the world around us.

Please make sure to add any suggestions to the Google spreadsheet shared in the Zoom chat before the third week of the month to have a chance at it being selected for the next month. The event name will be updated once the title is selected.

The meetings are 90 minutes long and broke down into 3 parts. The first half hour is spent discussing the section that was designed or our anticipations on what the book might be like. The middle section we read out loud, and the last half hour is spent going over what we read and assigning the next section.

So far we have read the following titles and discussed how they correlate with our present day. 

• The Diary of a Yong Girl - Anne Frank 
• 1984 - George Orwell 
• Animal Farm - George Orwell 
• Fahrenheit 451 – Ray Bradbury 
• Looking Backward – Edward Bellamy 
• The Age of Reason - Thomas Paine 
• Howl and Other Poems - Allen Ginsberg
• Civil Disobedience - Henry David Thoreau
• To Kill A Mocking Bird - Harper Lee

All are welcome and even if you haven’t picked up the book feel free to join us for the discussion and reading.

events.title: Beacon Shine the Light Great Neck:  ICE OUT
events.description:
Join The Beacon for Thursday Shine the Light, as we bring our voices to the street every Thursday from 12:00-12:30 PM.  (NOTE NEW EARLIER TIME!)

Each week, we make our voices heard wherever we are. As beacons, we shine light by making a sign and bringing it outside. Don't have a sign? Don't worry! You can borrow one of ours.

Together, we are building visible resistance and organized compassion, meeting our neighbors, and joining together in acts of solidarity. We find joy in resistance through community, music, comedy and street theater.

Across the country, communities are organizing to disentangle local law enforcement from federal immigration enforcement. Here in Nassau County, families continue to live in terror of separation, detainment, detention and deportation.

We stand weekly in opposition to this unprecedented assault on the rights, safety, and economic security of people in this country. For 30 minutes every Thursday, we say ICE OUT OF OUR COMMUNITIES! ICE OUT FOR GOOD! and we stand in favor of compassionate democracy and against cruelty, fear and despair.

People that come together in solidarity and say NO to ICE are a critical bulwark against mass deportations and the erosion of civil rights. There is much that we can do locally. And there is much that our elected officials can do — if we demand courage and leadership. Join us!

There are Beacon groups all over the USA. Our local Great Neck group meets every Thursday from 6:00-6:30 pm. We are joined by the Singing Resistance Great Neck to sing songs of solidarity and resistance, old and new.

For more information on The Beacon, visit www.beaconfordemocracy.org

A core principle behind all ICE Out For Good events is a commitment to nonviolent action and no civil disobedience. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values, and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events. All events should be held in public spaces or on public property.

events.title: Vote Yes on the War Powers Resolution
events.description:
✊Vote Yes on the War Powers Resolution

Dear friends,

I am one of the millions of Americans who believes that only Congress has the power to declare war—and that no President, Democrat or Republican, should be able to drag our country into a costly, unauthorized conflict without a vote. Right now, Congress has a historic opportunity to reassert its constitutional authority and end an unauthorized war. But we need to make sure our representatives finish the job.

🚨 Our Constitution Is in Danger!

Here's what's happening:

•	On February 28, 2026, the Trump administration launched Operation Epic Fury, a major military campaign against Iran—without congressional authorization

•	The war has cost billions of taxpayer dollars, driven gas prices up 69% in some states, and put our brave servicemembers in harm's way 

•	The House has passed a War Powers Resolution three times—but it has never reached the President's desk 

•	The Senate passed a companion resolution 50–48 on June 24, 2026—the first time both chambers passed a war powers resolution since 1973
 
•	But the White House is ignoring it, claiming the War Powers Act is "not constitutional" and "not binding" 

•	Congress has still not held public hearings or voted on a formal Authorization for Use of Military Force (AUMF)

Our Constitution is not optional. Our votes are not a suggestion. Congress must act.

📢 "Vote Yes on the War Powers Resolution" – That's Our Message

We are saying YES to:

•	✅ YES to the Constitution – Article I gives Congress, not the President, the sole power to declare war 

•	✅ YES to accountability – The American people deserve a vote before our troops are sent into harm's way

•	✅ YES to ending an unauthorized war – The War Powers Resolution of 1973 requires the President to withdraw forces within 60 days unless Congress authorizes the action

•	✅ YES to diplomacy – The administration launched this war while negotiations with Iran were actively ongoing 

•	✅ YES to our troops – They deserve clear objectives, an exit strategy, and the full support of a Congress that has debated and authorized their mission

Our Constitution is not a suggestion. Our votes are not optional. Congress must act NOW.

The American people deserve a vote. Our troops deserve a strategy. Our Constitution demands accountability.

Please act now. Our democracy depends on it.

events.title: Public Hearing: Tell IDEM Not to Rubber-Stamp Google Michigan City Data Center's Dirty Diesel Permit
events.description:
The Indiana Department of Environmental Management (IDEM) has published a draft modification to Google's Building 2 air permit for its facility under construction at 402 Royal Road in Michigan City.

The permit would add 66 more large diesel backup generators, on top of the 66 already permitted for Building 1. If finalized, the campus could run 132 critical diesel engines, ~725,000 gallons of on-site diesel, and even bigger engines than Building 1, with ZERO modern pollution controls in this draft. 

Krueger Middle School and Paladin - Head Start are each about a third of a mile from the site's property line, and residences are nearby. The site is a contaminated brownfield under active IDEM oversight. Michigan City residents have shown up to speak out against Building 1, packed Council chambers, and demanded accountability for the past year, while local permits for Building 2 may still be pending. This state permit will determine whether Indiana allows a second diesel power plant next to our schools and homes without basic safeguards.

Michigan City deserves clean air! Join the virtual public hearing on November 17th to tell IDEM to protect our communities and airways from Amazon’s dirty diesel generator permit.

Sign and share our petition to send a quick comment on the permit at www.jtnwi.org/no-dirty-diesel-google.

*The hearing begins at 6:00 PM CT and will conclude as soon as public comments are done, or no later than 9:00 PM CT.

### Speak with Sunrise Orlando during Public Comment @ the LYNX Board of Directors Meeting! 🌅

Join us at the LYNX Board of Directors Meeting to learn about and discuss decisions that will shape our public transportation and to advocate for a more affordable, walkable, and sustainable Orlando.

**What is Public Comment?**

Public Comment refers to the time scheduled at the beginning of a meeting for public input. At each LYNX Board of Directors meeting, time is set aside for members of the public to speak on general topics of interest or concern listed on the meeting agenda. Members can provide in-person, virtual (Zoom), or written comments before the board.

**What does Public Comment with Sunrise Orlando look like?**

When participating in public comment with us, you can expect to:

- Meet up with Sunrise Orlando members and community supporters.

- Attend the public meeting together in the morning.

- Participate in public comment if appropriate and available.

- Learn how local decisions affect our communities and how we can take action.

You don't need to be a Sunrise Orlando member or a policy expert to join us! Whether it's your first public meeting or you're one of our regulars, we'll be there to help you with talking points, information, and encouragement!

Through game experiences it's possible to not only normalize a different world, but learn how to behave in that world and make meaningful choices. We learn that different is not neccessarily scary--sometimes it's cosy as well as exciting! 

Through games we want people to embrace a country that shares power, and supports the well-being of all its citizens.

In this online class Katherine will help you to learn how to make effective interactive stories, and perhaps even make your own game!

events.title: March for an AI Treaty: Washington, DC
events.description:
On November 18, world leaders gather in Shenzhen, China for the APEC summit. Trump plans to meet Xi Jinping there.

So on November 14, we march from the Capitol to the White House, demanding Trump and Xi make a deal to stop the AI arms race.

The CEOs of OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind have [signed a statement](https://www.safe.ai/statement-on-ai-risk) warning that AI poses a risk of human extinction. Each says it can't slow down while the others race, and while China races. Only a deal between the US and China can break that deadlock.

We're not asking either country to stop alone. We're asking both to stop together, with verification.

The same day, we march in San Francisco and New York. All cities: [aitreatymarch.org](https://aitreatymarch.org)

📅 SATURDAY, NOV 14 || 11 AM → 1 PM ET

11:00 🗣️ Rally at Pennsylvania Ave & 3rd St NW, at the foot of the Capitol
11:40 🚶 March up Pennsylvania Ave to the White House
12:20 📢 Final rally at Lafayette Square

The route is about 1.3 miles. The final route is still being confirmed, and we'll update this page.

Bring a sign, and bring your friends!

This is a peaceful, nonviolent march. Please follow marshals' instructions. AI company employees are welcome.

Co-hosted with the DC AI Safety Collective.

events.title: Office Hours + Check-In: Cutting Off the Data Pipeline to ICE
events.description:
At our recent webinar, we learned how thousands of local law enforcement agencies share 911 caller data, victim and witness information, and other records with LexisNexis, a private data broker that sells access to federal agencies including ICE. This often happens without local officials or residents realizing it, even in sanctuary communities.

**We've started reaching out to our local officials and requesting public records. Now it’s time to compare notes.** Join this De-ICE Action Network check-in to share where your local effort stands, troubleshoot obstacles, and learn from organizers taking on the same fight in other communities. 

Whether you’ve filed a public records request, met with a city council member, hit a wall with your police department, or are still figuring out where to start, we want to hear from you.

**What to expect:**
• Discussion of progress, roadblocks and lessons learned
• Help working through the action toolkit
• Q&A and troubleshooting with Shawn Segal of FinePrint
• Opportunities to connect with others working on this issue

**Who should attend:** Anyone who attended or watched the recording of our earlier webinar, plus organizers, advocates, local officials and staff ready to take action. 

New to the issue? You’re welcome too! Email us at events@de-iceaction.org and we'll send you everything you need to get started.

**Registration required.** This is an interactive session, so we encourage you to join live. If you have questions but can't make it, email tips@de-iceaction.org.

events.description:
At our Compost Hubs, food scraps collected from the community are transformed into nutrient-rich compost, and we need your help to make it happen! As a Compost Hub Support Volunteer, you’ll gain hands-on experience working alongside our knowledgeable Compost Managers. Get ready to leave feeling accomplished, a little sweaty, and brimming with new compost knowledge. 

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:
Roll up your sleeves and dive into a variety of engaging activities; whether it’s managing a three-bin system, tending to a compost pile, sifting finished compost, or exploring a mix of everything. There’s something for everyone, from beginners to seasoned pros! Plus, our Compost Hubs are situated in LA County’s most cherished green spaces: community gardens, urban farms, and beautiful parks. Join passionate community composters, learn to turn food scraps into rich compost, and connect with the local food system. 

#### MORE INFO: 
* You will be working outdoors! Shade levels vary by site.
* Activity level can be adjusted to your comfort and abilities—just communicate with your Compost Manager.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome!
* If you sign up, we ask that you show up! We rely on volunteers, like you, to achieve our mission.  
* This site has public restrooms. 
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.
* Access to water, but please bring a filled water bottle. 

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under the age of 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT: 
VOLUNTEER WAIVER: Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. Access the e-waiver at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver

events.title: Online to Offline: Digital Organizing 101
events.description:
## Every strong movement starts with real human connection. In this connected world, that happens both online and offline.

Digital organizing uses digital tools to meet and engage people online, and then move them into in-person action. It doesn’t replace the real world relationship-building we must do to build movements that win change. It just provides another path to get there.

In this training we walk through how to use digital tools with the same discipline we bring to in-person conversations — to build real relationships, move people to act, and grow your base. 

### Our brand new Digital Organizing 101 training will cover:

- The foundational principles of digital organizing

- Using platforms like Whatsapp, Reddit, Facebook and Instagram to identify and engage supporters

- Real-world case studies to apply digital organizing principles

- The formula to craft personal and persuasive messaging 

- Digital systems and hygiene

This space will build a community of organizers with the skills to leverage the online world and make change offline. See you there!

_This training is co-lead by Public School Strong and the Alliance to Reclaim Our Schools._

events.title: Our Future OUR Vote NC

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
This November, it’s going to take all of us to protect free and fair elections, so that WE, the people of North Carolina, get to decide our future. We’ve already seen how people in power in our state and in the White House are trying to silence Black and brown voters, students, working people, and anyone who disagrees with them. Our democracy is under attack but we’re not backing down! 

On election day, and on a few other key dates in November, we’re coming together to exercise and defend our vote and to show those in power that we are watching:

- Tuesday, November 10th: Last day for voters with absentee or provisional ballots to “cure” their ballots and make sure they are counted. We’ll come together in our counties that evening to celebrate historic voter turnout, thank the election officials who are working hard to make our democracy run, and to send a clear message: count every vote. 

- Monday, November 16th: Join us in the evening for a mass call with partners across the state to hear updates about what happened in the elections and during county certification, and what's next in the movement to protect our vote. We'll also get ready to make our voices heard when the NC General Assembly reconvenes in November.

- Tuesday, November 24th: Deadline for the NC State Board of Elections to certify all the NC election results. We’ll hold a peaceful rally between the NC General Assembly and the State Board of Elections on Halifax Mall, in Raleigh, ready to defend our vote. 

Sign up here to let us know you’re in, and we’ll follow up with more details!

Volunteers will meet near 351 Divisadero St and then work on the medians for the 300 block and 400 block. SF Public Works will provide lane closure and tools. Please sign up so we can prepare enough tools.

We typically start removing green waste at 10:45 AM. Please stay until the end so we can complete all the tasks.

### Agenda
- Safety talk 
- Planting demo 
- Gardening, planting, weeding, pruning, cleaning
- Leave the green waste on the street 
- Rake green waste into large piles 
- Load green waste into the trucks starting around 10:45 AM. 

### What to Bring/Wear
- Bring a reusable water bottle 
- Wear sunscreen and closed toe shoes
- Dress in layers

### Community Partners
- SF Public Works
- District 5 Supervisor Bilal Mahmood
- Divisadero Merchants Association
- North of Panhandle Neighborhood Association (NOPNA)
- Alamo Square Neighborhood Association
- Divisadero neighbors

-5pm-5:45pm Working on dissecting the universal health plan into digestible, educational pieces for the public. Includes writing material and turning it into a 5th grade reading level

-5:45pm-6:30pm Writing scripts for social media. Brave souls will make social media video content out of them. I'll show you how to not make that such a scary experience

events.title: Salmonberry Trail Planting Party - Help us Beautify Wheeler!
events.description:
Join the Planting Team in Wheeler!

The Salmonberry Trail is almost ready to open, and we need your help with the finishing touches! Come join our team of volunteers as we plant native and drought-tolerant plants along Wheeler’s new trail segment.

This is the first coastal section of the 82-mile Salmonberry Trail Rails and Trails project—a wonderful opportunity to create a welcoming, beautiful trail for residents, visitors, and wildlife.

🌿 What will we be doing?

Plants have been selected and locations planned. The planting process is straightforward, and everyone can help!

Unpot each plant and check its roots.

Score the roots if needed to encourage healthy growth.

Dig a hole where needed (some holes will be prepared in advance SO EVERY physical capability can help!).

Place the plant in its designated location.

Backfill with soil and add mulch to help retain moisture and support healthy growth.

Water each plant in to give it a good start and help settle the soil around its roots.

No special gardening experience is necessary—just bring your enthusiasm, a willingness to get your hands dirty, and a desire to make a difference!

🌼 Why come?

Together, we can:

Create native habitat for birds, bees, and butterflies, providing food, shelter, and support for local pollinators and wildlife.

Add natural beauty and greenery to the trail.

Help make the Salmonberry Trail a welcoming destination for our community and visitors.

Every plant we put in the ground is an investment in Wheeler’s future!

Can you spare a few hours on November 21? Bring a friend, meet your neighbors, and help us grow something wonderful!

🧤 Bring: Gardening gloves, sturdy shoes, and a water bottle. Planting tools and supplies will be provided as available.

Let’s plant the future of the Salmonberry Trail—one plant at a time! 🌱

If you are coming from the Portland Metro area, let us know if you need to carpool with someone and will help arrange a ride!

[Please read the volunteer waiver](https://salmonberrytrail.org/volunteer-waiver)

events.description:
Meet on the overpass of 3rd and Howard.

We provide physical messaging in the real world to connect with and activate voters. Bring your own signs too. Prepare to wave and generally have a good time.

Rules and Protocols

We avoid doing anything that could either harm ourselves or anyone else. This includes stepping into traffic, holding a sign where it could fall onto cars below, climbing fencing, etc.
We must not block pedestrian and bike traffic, so please keep clear to allow them to pass.
We supply the messages, you supply the waves. However, you are welcome to also display your own poster boards. Just avoid any messaging that would be rated above a PG-13.
We don’t litter. If we find litter, we pick it up and throw it away.
We are NOT allowed to attach the signs to the fencing on the overpass. We don’t use stickers or anything that leaves a permanent mark on the overpass. However, chalk is okay and even encouraged.
If someone from the ‘opposition’ comes up to talk with us, do not engage with them. Best to just ignore them. One member will be designated to handle them and video record any aggressive interaction so that you can go right on waving.
We take lots of pictures and videos during our action for circulation on social media. If you prefer not to be included, please let us know and/or consider wearing a mask.
Should law enforcement pay us a visit, only the designated point person from the group should address them.
Ignore the middle fingers and negativity coming from some of the cars below. For every one of those confused folks, you are providing hope to another 100 people!
The Visibility Brigade is a non-violent, informal volunteer group in which we all participate with an understanding that our own actions are our personal responsibility and we accept our own personal liability. You participate with this understanding.
