events.title: Warren Wilson: Without Shade, Without Rest
events.description:
Join us November 20, at 6pm in Kittredge Theater for a screening of the film Without Shade, Without Rest. There will be light refreshments provided and a discussion of farm and food worker rights following the film.

WeCount! is a non-profit, human rights organization that represents immigrant workers and families in South Florida, including plant nursery workers. WeCount!’s advocacy on extreme heat is the subject of the new documentary, Without Shade, Without Rest by Six Eye Films and Working Films. This documentary tells the story of two organizations, WeCount! and the Coalition of Immokalee Workers, and our efforts to win heat protections for Florida’s outdoor workers. In the face of intense industry lobbying and aggressive state preemption, the fight in Florida continues. Their work has helped put extreme heat in the national conversation and inspired advocacy for workplace heat standards across the country. 

While “Without Shade, Without Rest” is primarily focused on Florida, we believe this film can be a helpful tool for workers, advocates, organizations, and community members across the country and world, who are similarly grappling with the growing and existential threat of climate change and extreme heat. We hope the film helps shine a light on an urgent labor and human rights issue and contributes to meaningful dialogue and connections across our movements. In Asheville, a new campaign Planting Justice (Sembrando Justicia) is being launched by WeCount! and local partners in support of workers in the house plant industry who work locally with little labor protections. The food we eat and the plants we enjoy are nothing without the workers who plant and nurture them.

events.title: Salmonberry Trail Special Art Installation- Opening Reception!
events.description:
The Salmonberry Trail is hosting an art show in collaboration with the local non-profit, One Room Studios. We will also be featuring local "On the Trail" Artists to further the Salmonberry Trail's mission to connect local businesses to the greater community!

Jeff Beers will be featuring his collection "Paper and Raincoat" on the first floor of the Salmonberry Trail Office. On the second floor, we will be featuring local trail artists Alison Graves from Buxton Hill Farms, and Richard Knight of Richard Knight Studios in Timber.

### Gallery Hours (Thurs Nov 12 through Sat Nov 21):

- Opening Reception is Thursday, November 12 from 5-8PM
- Thursday and Friday from 5-8PM
- Saturday from 12-8PM


#### About the Artists:

##### Jeff Beers:
"“Paper & Raincoat” are the two main ingredients of a new series that unfolds like a myth cycle of life and death. Beers painstakingly made it out of scraps of thin sheets of paper that he’s aged for 30 years, and surplus raincoat material from Columbia Sportswear. (Beers got the latter from the local nonprofit SCRAP Creative Reuse.) After 16 months of meticulous work, these two simple ingredients have found cosmic depths in this series of 8 pieces."

##### Alison Graves:

"Set in the foothills of the Coast Range, Buxton Hills Farm is an 80-acre historic homestead and small woodland. The naturally abundant land, originally the homeland of the Atfalatl and Kalapuya people, remains home to deer and elk, owls and hawks, newts and frogs, bobcats and coyotes. Since the early 1900s the farm has been home to the Genzers, Raffertys, Wilsons, Mitchells and now the Graves family. Along the way the families have grown strawberries, prunes, hazelnuts, dairy cows and Christmas trees.

Since 2015 we have cultivated the small woodland for recreation and wildlife, with an emphasis on sharing the land with friends and family to learn about forestry and farming while having fun. We partner with organizations that share our interests to celebrate the seasons and learn together about the plants and animals that call this place home."


##### Richard Knight:

"Richard Knight Gallery is a craft store you should certainly visit, as you're sure to find something that will catch your attention. I offer a variety of wooden boxes, metal rose's(copper, steel and brass), beaded necklaces, pearls, and jade. I make use of a variety of sturdy materials in my crafts, but some things remain consistent in all my designs – a keen eye for detail and impeccable design, for starters."

Description

This is an opportunity for new members to meet current members and learn about volunteer opportunities, upcoming events, and more.  This is also a great time to bring your friends and neighbors into the fight for Democracy. Polls show that Democrats and Republicans agree on a lot of the issues that are closest to our hearts: belief in the right to fair housing, gas, and food costs, and the need to ensure we can all afford good healthcare when we need it. No one wants the wars, and no one knows why they need a mega data center in the field behind their house.
Politicians have had their fun with us, stirring up senseless division. But now it is more important than ever to hold their feet to the fire until we get the government we all want, one that listens and responds to those who fund it. And no one wants their government funded by a handful of corporations and billionaires. We have seen how quickly our rights and freedoms erode under that sort of tyranny. Let's come together en masse and plan for our future, as citizens of this one country. Not to make it anything, "AGAIN", because there have always been troubles. But to make it like new, where every spice in this melting pot brings its own flavor, creating something truly spectacular.

The election is over, but as important as it was, it was only our MidTerm. Let's come together and discuss what is next. Of course, we will follow the national Indivisible guidelines, but locally, what do we face over the next two years?

California Working Families Party went into this election with our biggest slate of candidates in history, endorsing more than 220 candidates up and down the ballot, from school boards and city councils to Congress and statewide office.

After months of organizing, knocking doors, making calls, and taking on billionaires and corporate special interests, we're bringing our WFP community together to unpack the results.

What happened? What surprised us? What did we win? What did we learn? And what the hell comes next?

Join California WFP leaders, organizers, and members from across the state for an honest, unfiltered conversation about the 2026 election results. We'll break down the biggest races, celebrate victories, discuss setbacks, and reflect on what this election means for the future of working-class politics in California.

Whether you're feeling fired up, frustrated, hopeful, or just trying to make sense of it all, this conversation is for you.

events.description:
# Get on the Bus, Get Organized! 🚌✊

With the midterms behind us, it’s time to lock in to win dedicated transit funding in 2027! Every conversation with a fellow rider or transit operator is a chance to build connections, grow our movement, and organize. If we want to restore and expand transit service across the Commonwealth, we need all hands on deck!

Join **Pittsburghers for Public Transit (PPT)’s Organizing Committee** for a monthly canvassing series to connect with our communities, talk about the issues impacting transit riders, and build people power for the transit system we deserve.

**Our first mission?** Making public transit a top priority for Pennsylvania’s governor!

**Never canvassed before? No problem!** Whether you’re a first-timer or a seasoned organizer, there’s a place for you. Come meet fellow transit advocates, talk with your community, and help build the grassroots power we need to win.

**Let’s get organized! Ride with us and fight for better transit for everyone!**


**Are you a confident canvasser willing to lead a small group of canvassers on the bus?** Volunteer to be a Canvass Lead - support a small group of canvassers by making sure folks don’t get lost and board the correct buses, and have the chance to debrief after their ride. Think this might be you, but need more information? Awesome! You can select either option as you register for your canvassing session. 


## What to expect

- **Training and practice** will take place at the beginning of each event.
- **Small groups** of canvassers will be led by an experienced Canvass Lead to various bus stops in the downtown area.
- **Bus rides and bus stops** are where canvassing will take place. Canvassers will ride the bus for about 30 minutes outbound, then return back downtown.
- **Social hour** afterwards will serve as the space to debrief, compare notes and connect with one another.

### Accessibility

While PPT will work to create a comfortable environment for participants, there may be barriers to participation. We cannot guarantee the accessibility of bus stops or the bus. Buses may be loud and crowded. We cannot obtain ASL for these events.

events.title: Yes to Wind! Responsible Wind Energy & Wildlife in Texas
events.description:
### Save the Date! 

This year will mark 10 years of offshore wind energy powering U.S. homes and businesses! The nation’s first offshore wind project began operating off Block Island, Rhode Island, in 2016. Since then, America has tripled its offshore wind energy capacity. By next year, offshore wind will power 2.6 million American households.

Now is an opportunity for Texas to build on that progress. 

To mark this milestone, the National Wildlife Federation and our partner, Audubon Texas, are hosting an event celebrating responsible wind energy in Austin on Tuesday, December 15th. 

Responsibly developed wind energy—both onshore and offshore—can help meet growing electricity demand, create jobs, and support a cleaner energy future while protecting wildlife and natural habitats.

Join us in celebrating Texas's continued leadership in wind energy, a successful decade of U.S. offshore wind, and supporting its responsible development in the Gulf!

**Learn why we say YES to Wind!**

events.title: Protest Against Mesa City Council & NTT Mesa PH10 Data Center Campus!
events.description:
### 🚨Protest NTT Mesa PH10 Data Center & the MCC! 🚨

Mesa Valley Indivisible officially teamed up with our sister group, [Indivisible Mesa](https://www.indivisiblemesa.org)—who has been leading the charge against Mesa’s 287(g) agreement and predatory data centers, like the planned 2.2 million sq ft [NTT Mesa PH10 Data Center](https://www.mesavalleyindivisible.org/no-mesa-ntt-global-ph10-data-center)—to make our voices heard at City Hall.

As public turnout surged, city officials escalated their efforts to quiet community opposition: 

- **On June 8th**, A local activist was physically removed from a council meeting simply for silently holding a small sign. 

- At the next Mesa City Council meeting **on July 17th**, after the indoor sign bans forced us outside, police arrested a peaceful protester for using a megaphone despite the fact that she complied with their demands. She was charged with bogus charges and forced to spend a night in jail...FOR USING A MEGAPHONE. The charges were dropped at her 9/28/2026 court date. k 

- **On August 7th** when Indivisible Mesa recently pressed the City Council coordinator for answers, the city shifted its story yet again! They claimed the councilmembers will not be voting on the data center at all and that NTT can proceed administratively, but only after grassroots pressure began mounting.


## 📢 Calls to Action:

**Whether or not you can attend, please do the following three things:**

1. [Submit a comment here](https://us.openforms.com/Form/44ff3314-58bb-418a-a122-46fe7725feef)! Feel free to choose one of the concerns listed below if you do not want to write your own comment. 

2. [Email the Mesa City Council members by](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1llwS0FcrAfxBdC1DwOL0hayMQ9SWK1WJkHFZlxXYdQ4/edit?usp=sharing). Contact info, directions, and scripts/templates provided!

3. [Call the Mesa City Council members](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1qedOvsbfPZ9mG1N6BKkc7QvL3XeamSdmvA_oVY7bu8w/edit?usp=sharing)** and use the script provided or your own! 


## 🚨 Important: 

- We do not care whether or not the data center is on the agenda. MVI and other local activists know it is VITAL we voice our disgust every single council meeting in order to make sure they actually listen to their constituents! 


### 🔑 Key Concerns Driving the Protest:

- Massive Handouts, Tiny Returns: Similarly sized data centers receive over $100 million a year in tax subsidies. That is revenue stolen directly from our local community services and neighborhood improvements.

- Virtually No Job Creation: Despite taking up huge amounts of space, this massive facility will only create 40 to 60 permanent jobs paying $60,000 or less. Compared to advanced manufacturing or bioscience, data centers provide practically zero high-quality jobs per acre.

- We Pay Their Bills: The infrastructure improvements and utility upgrades required for this project will likely be passed on to everyday customers, not the multibillion-dollar company.

- Driving Up Local Costs: Developments like this artificially inflate land costs, making it harder for our local farmers, small businesses, and families looking for affordable housing to survive.

- A 2.2 million-square-foot facility requires an astronomical amount of energy and water to keep its servers cool. In our delicate desert environment, this level of resource consumption is completely unsustainable and directly threatens the capacity of our local utilities.

- This project threatens the safety and peace of our residential areas. The constant, 24/7 roar of massive cooling fans creates severe noise pollution, while the sprawling, windowless buildings will industrialize our local landscape and destroy our community's character.


## 🪧 Sign Ideas:

- We won't be silent!
- No more Mesa Data Centers!
- NO one wants Data Centers!
- Hate data centers = bipartisan 


### 📷 Pictures & Videos
- Make sure to always tag **Mesa Valley Indivisible** on our group [Facebook page](https://www.facebook.com/share/g/1CFYV1DSaT/), [Instagram page](https://www.instagram.com/mesavalleyindivisible/), [BlueSky](https://bsky.app/profile/mesavalleyindivisi.bsky.social), and [TikTok](https://www.tiktok.com/@mesa.valley.indiv)
- Please also include #MesaValleyIndivisible 
- Add all photos & videos to our [Google drive!](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1S1uAHfKVI5PbUsu8MrkPVs-kuDCPDEqS?usp=sharing)

address_lines: East Southern Avenue & South Signal Butte Road

events.description:
## 🛫 ICE & AROCC: Stop ICE operations at Mesa Gateway Airport!

For eight months, [Mesa Valley Indivisible](https://www.mesavalleyindivisible.org/) members and a coalition of groups around the country have been working relentlessly to end Avelo Airlines’ involvement in the unlawful and inhumane deportation of primarily non‑violent immigrants via Mesa Gateway Airport. As a result, Avelo Airlines ended their contract with ICE in January 2026! 

Although Avelo Airlines has left our Mesa Gateway Airport, ICE deportation missions still happen every day and the Arizona Removal Operations Coordination Center (AROCC) continues to operate.

When local lawmakers recently conducted a surprise visit to the Arizona Removal Operations Coordination Center here at Mesa Gateway, they were sickened by what they found. Despite being a transit hub meant for 12-hour stays, people were being held for weeks, packed like sardines on bare concrete floors with no beds or showers. While the administration continues to claim these are short-term facilities, the reality has proven to be gut-wrenching medical neglect and overcrowding.

    
--------------------------------------

## 🔑 Key Concerns Driving the Protest:

- We have compiled public records, congressional oversight letters, and local reporting into one place. 
- Please read our complete [Mesa Valley Indivisible AROCC and ICE Air Deportations Fact Sheet](https://www.mesavalleyindivisible.org/ice-deportationsarocc) to understand the full scope of our key concerns and see how you can take action.

--------------------------------------

- To ensure you receive all necessary information for the upcoming event, please make sure you have officially registered via Mobilize.

  - Keep an eye out for emails from Mesa Valley Indivisible and check your spam/junk folder if you do not see them!

--------------------------------------------

##  ✨Protest Information:

- MVI's goal is to always to pack all 4 corners of the intersection. Please look for the empty spots and fill them!
- Make sure to stand side by side and not behind one another so every driver & the media can see how many attendees are present!
- Please share with friends, family, neighbors, EVERYONE!

events.title: Love as Action: Quaker Witness to Authoritarianism, Oppression, & War

address_lines: East College Avenue & South Allen Street

events.description:
# Love as Action: Quaker Witness to Authoritarianism, Oppression, & War

### Quakers have long stood in opposition to cruelty and inequality. In this time of rising authoritarianism and fascism, we are called to show this love in action again. 

Please join State College Friends Meeting and the American Friends Service Committee to bear witness and show resistance to the authoritarian actions of our country. 

On Saturdays, October 31 & November 14, 2026, at 1:00 p.m., we will gather at the Allen Street Gates for one hour of silent public worship.

Quaker worship is a communal time in reverent silence to listen inwardly for insight and guidance. Anyone who feels deeply led may share a brief message for the spiritual nurture of the group. Signs are welcome that, consistent with our values, highlight harms of authoritarianism or share love and support for communities who are suffering.

Together, we affirm: We will protect people and communities. We will resist authoritarian government. We will build a free, equal and just future. Shared witness reflects core Quaker principles: peace, equality, integrity, and community. And taking action publicly is a visible commitment to justice and compassion, in solidarity with communities facing harm and dehumanization. By standing together in silence, we affirm that every person has worth, that fear and violence must give way to love and fairness, and that our communities thrive when all are welcomed.

Our hope is that our presence will give hope to all who see us – to show that we can choose resistance - and remind everyone of our moral obligations to one another.

Join us! We gather monthly in communities across the country, showing love in action as a public witness of our Quaker values in times of rising injustice. To find our more about Love as Action nationally visit www.afsc.org/love-action

events.title: No Country for Mothers: A Maryland Community Screening & Conversation
events.description:
**Mothers have long been expected to figure it out. Childcare. Work. Leave. School schedules. Aging parents. Healthcare. The endless logistics of keeping a family going.**

During National Family Caregivers Month, join journalist, author, and advocate Christine Michel Carter for a free Maryland screening of Moms First’s documentary *No Country for Mothers*, followed by a public conversation about what it actually takes to raise and care for a family in Maryland today.

So much of what makes caregiving difficult gets treated as part of the deal. Childcare falls through, leave runs out, a child gets sick, an aging parent needs help, and work keeps moving as if none of it happened. Families adjust. Mothers rearrange. Somehow, somebody makes it work.

But “making it work” can hide how much women are being asked to absorb.

*No Country for Mothers* looks at the systems behind those experiences, but it also asks why mothers have spent so much time fighting over one another’s choices.

Working mom or stay-at-home mom. Career or family. Tradwife or girlboss. Mothers are constantly asked to pick a side and defend how they are doing motherhood, while many are dealing with the same underlying problems: childcare they can’t afford or find, inadequate leave, workplaces that were not designed around caregiving, financial pressure, and too little support.

This night is not about deciding who is mothering the “right” way.

And you do not have to agree politically with every woman in the room.

Motherhood and caregiving cross those lines. Women can have different families, different careers, different politics, and different ideas about how they want to live while still recognizing something in one another’s experience.

After the film, we’ll bring that conversation home to Maryland.

Mothers and caregivers will share what is happening in their own lives alongside civic leaders, advocates, employers, community organizations, and public leaders. We’ll talk about what families have accepted as normal, where they are being asked to solve larger problems on their own, and where there may be common ground for making family life work better.

We’ll ask:

- What have we gotten too used to calling “normal”?
- What are mothers and caregivers absorbing that shouldn’t fall entirely on families?
- Where are families falling through the gaps?
- Where can people who may disagree politically still find common ground?
- What would meaningful progress look like for Maryland families?

And then comes the question that matters after the conversation ends:

**What do I want to do with what I heard?**

For one woman, that may mean asking her employer to reconsider a policy that doesn’t work in practice. Another may call an elected official, learn more about an issue affecting her family, share her story, join other mothers around something she cares about, or bring this same conversation into her own community.

For someone else, the first step may simply be sitting in a room with other women and realizing that something she has been struggling to manage quietly is happening in families all around her.

You do not need to arrive as an advocate.

Come because you’re tired of figuring everything out by yourself. Come because you want to say some of this out loud. Come because you want to hear what other women are carrying. Come because you may disagree about plenty of things and still wonder whether motherhood has to be this hard.

The goal is not to leave with every problem solved or everyone in agreement. It is to leave seeing your own experience more clearly, understanding how it connects to something larger, and knowing that your voice belongs in the conversations where decisions about families are made.

**We spend a lot of time asking mothers how they’re going to make it work. On this night, we’re asking what needs to work better for them.**

Free and open to the public. Registration required.

Join Families for Safe Streets as we commemorate World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims in Central Park at the Charles A. Dana Discovery Center.

This year our ceremony will include an ancient tradition from Japan, folded paper cranes. The practice of folding a thousand paper cranes was originally an endeavor undertaken to with for a long life for oneself of a loved one.

Over time, the tradition has evolved to be associated with wishing for recovery from illness or injury, for happiness and good luck or for world peace. Members of Families for Safe Streets will create a thousand origami cranes to honor loved ones killed or injured by traffic violence and the people killed or injured this past year. We look forward to seeing you to mark this solemn, meaningful day with us.

After the ceremony, Families for Safe Streets members will gather for a meal together.

events.title: Unlocking Housing: A Community Listening Session
events.description:
We're launching our Housing Unlocked campaign and we want to hear from you. This listening session is a time for people impacted by incarceration and/or housing insecurity to come together, share our stories, and build a new campaign for housing justice. 

Dream.Org's Housing Unlocked campaign works with impacted communities to increase dignified housing for people impacted by incarceration, and fight back against the criminalization of homelessness in Pennsylvania, New York, Arizona, and Wisconsin. Our firm belief is that the people closest to the problem are most equipped to solve them. 

We want to work with you to build a world where people can access keys, not cages. Expanding access to quality housing is not only the humane thing to do, it is the common-sense solution to reduce recidivism, save taxpayer dollars, and keep communities safe.

People who have been incarcerated are up to 13 times more likely to experience homelessness, while unhoused people are often jailed simply for sleeping or standing outside. Housing insecurity is both a cause and effect of incarceration: the two operate in a vicious cycle, affecting tens of thousands of Americans every year. But it doesn't have to be that way.

Your voice is needed. It's time to unlock our blocks.

### Tenant Summit: Know Your Rights. Demand Accountability. Build Community Power.

**Everyone deserves a safe, stable, and affordable place to call home. But too many tenants are facing rising rents, unfair housing practices, the threat of eviction, and landlords who are not being held accountable. It's time to change that.**

Join us for a community-driven **Tenant Summit** focused on empowering renters with the knowledge, resources, and collective power needed to protect their homes and fight for stronger tenant protections.

This summit will bring together renters, housing advocates, community organizers, and legal experts for honest conversations about the challenges tenants face and the solutions our communities deserve.

Together, we'll explore:

- Know Your Rights: Understand tenant protections, lease agreements, eviction processes, and your rights under Arizona law.
- Landlord Accountability:Learn how to document unsafe living conditions, address unfair treatment, and advocate for responsible property management.
- Housing Stability and Affordability: Discuss rising housing costs, displacement, and the policies needed to keep families in their homes.
- The Power of Tenant Organizing: Discover how renters can organize within their apartment complexes and neighborhoods to demand better living conditions and lasting change.
- From Conversation to Action: Connect with advocates, access community resources, and identify opportunities to shape housing policies that put people before profits.

This summit isn't just about understanding the challenges we're facing. It's about building the power to change them.

Whether you're a longtime renter, facing housing challenges for the first time, or passionate about housing justice, your voice belongs in this conversation.

Because housing is more than four walls and a roof. It's the foundation for our families, our health, our dignity, and our future.

Your home. Your rights. Our collective power. Join us and help build an Arizona where tenants are protected, landlords are accountable, and every family has the opportunity to thrive.

events.title: 2026 #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence
events.description:
2026 #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence

Beginning Wednesday, December 9, 2026 until the end of December, we will come together across the nation to host the #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence.

These local events will be anchored by the 14th Annual National Vigil for All Victims of Gun Violence on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C.—held near the 14-year mark of the Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting tragedy, when a 20-year-old gunman armed with an AR-15 hunted and murdered 20 first graders and six educators.

Across the country, vigils (as simple as lighting candles) and gatherings will honor lives stolen by gun violence, uplift survivors, raise awareness, and demand urgent action from our leaders to finally end this epidemic. From schools and workplaces to houses of worship, neighborhoods, grocery stores, homes, nightclubs, streets, and even our democracy itself—gun violence impacts every aspect of American life.

The theme of this year’s campaign is #FreedomToLive—the simple, powerful idea that every person deserves to live free from the daily threat of gunfire. Together, survivors, families, advocates, and allies will raise our voices to ensure that FREEDOM means the right of every person to live, learn, work, worship, speak, vote, and gather without the daily fear of gun violence.

events.title: Visibility Brigade Kane Bridge Event North Aurora, 11/6
events.description:

New here? Welcome to Visibility Brigade Kane (VBK)! We're a local grassroots crew in Kane County, Illinois, standing up for democracy and pushing back against fascism, nationalism, and authoritarianism. Our signature move? Gathering on bridges over rush-hour traffic with giant-letter messages, waving flags, and giving drivers a peaceful, joyful, impossible-to-miss reminder that they're not alone. If you can only come occasionally, you're welcome too — bring a friend and be ready to wave at strangers! We also get together for trivia nights, watch parties, and social nights at local breweries — because building community is part of the work. Follow along for upcoming gatherings and ways to get involved. We'd love to see you on a bridge — or across a trivia table.

MAKE SOME NOISE. MAKE A DIFFERENCE.

The election is over. The work is not. We voted — now we keep showing up.

Rush hour. A packed bridge. A bold message thousands of MOTORISTS can't miss. Expect powerful messages, nonstop supportive honking, great people, and the kind of energy that reminds us we are far from alone.

Never done this before? Perfect. We'll get you set up and make sure you feel right at home.

We start at 4:00 PM and wrap between 6:15 and 6:30 PM. Come for all of it or whatever time you can give.

Itinerary:
4:00–4:30 PM install & set up signs, banners, flags
4:30-6:15 PM dance party (we wave flags, shake pom poms, bang cowbells, swing pool noodles — anything to make drivers look up at our message!)
6:15-6:30 PM take down & pack up

Weather:
Rain? We're still on. Fascism doesn't take a break for the weather — neither do we! Severe storms (hail, lightning, etc.) are a different story.

Parking:
West side of the North Aurora Police Department. (Please don't park on the bridge itself.)

What to Bring:
water or another drink
fun props (pom poms, cowbell, pool noodles, etc.)
comfortable clothes you can move & sweat in
a smile + a helpful attitude

What Not to Bring:
protest signs (unless letters are 2+ feet tall — otherwise drivers can't see them). The Bridge Message is our focus — help us keep it strong.

Rules of the Road (and Bridge!):
1) If MAGA folks approach, record — don't engage.
2) If police come: no worries, we're legally allowed to protest (we've checked).
3) Stay to the sides so cyclists, runners, and walkers can pass easily.
4) Motorist engagement: stay positive — even with the haters.

Visibility Brigade Kane installs bold, provocative messages in highly visible public spaces — against fascism, nationalism, and authoritarianism, and for democracy. Our goal is to reach beyond the politically engaged, spark curiosity, and inspire people to seek the truth for themselves. Join us. Be part of the movement. Be safe, be helpful, and HAVE FUN!

events.title: Rally at the Supreme Court: Protect Connecticut's Assault Weapons Ban

location.venue: Supreme Court of the United States

events.description:
Our Children's Lives Are on the Line. Show Up and Make Your Voice Heard!

Nearly 14 years after 20 children and six educators were hunted and murdered at Sandy Hook Elementary School by a 20-year-old gunman with an AR15 and high capacity magazines, the U.S. Supreme Court will hear oral arguments in cases challenging assault weapons bans in Connecticut and Cook County, Illinois.

These laws were enacted to protect our families and communities from weapons of war that are designed to efficiently and brutally kill as many people in the shortest time possible. Now, their constitutionality is before the nation's highest court, and the consequences could extend far beyond Connecticut and Illinois.

We cannot afford to be silent!

On December 2 at 9:30 AM ET, gun violence survivors, families, advocates, and concerned Americans will gather outside the Supreme Court to stand together for our children's freedom to live without the fear of gun violence.

We have seen the devastation these weapons cause in Sandy Hook, Parkland, Uvalde, Highland Park, Orlando, Las Vegas, Buffalo and communities across the country. We know what is at stake.

The Second Amendment should not mean that Americans must surrender their freedom to feel safe in classrooms, houses of worship, grocery stores, and public spaces.

Join us outside the Supreme Court on December 2 at 9:30 AM ET. Stand with survivors and communities impacted by shootings. Stand with families. Stand for the freedom to live.

Bring your signs, your friends, and your determination. Let's make sure the voices of those whose lives have been forever changed by gun violence are heard.

RSVP today and help us spread the word!

Organized by national gun control/gun violence prevention/gun safety groups. 

#ProtectKidsNotGuns #BanAssaultWeapons #BanWeaponsOfWar #FreedomFromGunViolence #HonorWithAction #EndGunViolence

events.title: Southern Made Post Election Debrief
events.description:
Join Southern Made WFP for a post-election debrief as we unpack the 2026 midterm elections, celebrate our shared work, and talk about what comes next for working people across the South.

From Georgia to Tennessee, North Carolina to Florida, and across the region, organizers, candidates, volunteers, and everyday people have knocked doors, made calls, built relationships, and fought for a South where working families can thrive.

Now it's time to come together, take stock, and chart our path forward.

events.title: Defend the Pacific Islands Heritage Marine National Monument from Industrial Fishing
events.description:
The Trump Administration is attempting to illegally rollback protections for the Pacific Islands Heritage Marine National Monument (PIHMNM) – threatening to open up **408,000 square miles of protected ocean to harmful industrial fishing.**

In April 2025, President Trump issued a proclamation seeking to allow commercial fishing in the waters 50 to 200 nautical miles around Jarvis Island, Johnston Atoll, and Wake Island. When the National Marine Fisheries Service attempted to immediately allow commercial fishing without going through the legally required rulemaking process, a federal court struck down that action.

Now, these protections are under threat again. In March 2026, a federal fishing council voted to reopen these protected waters to commercial fishing, and the National Marine Fisheries Service may be moving forward to take action. Any attempt to open these waters must comply with procedural requirements under federal law, including providing robust and meaningful opportunities for public participation. 

The Pacific Islands Heritage Marine National Monument protects **one of the last wild and healthy ocean ecosystems on Earth.** These islands, atolls, reefs, and waters hold profound cultural significance for Indigenous Pacific Islanders with ancestral, historical, and cultural ties to the region and are part of a cross-cultural Indigenous Pacific voyaging legacy. 

The monument is also a refuge for extraordinary marine life, including whales, sharks, rays, sea turtles, millions of seabirds, ancient coral systems, and deep-sea species found nowhere else on Earth.

**Industrial fishing puts this irreplaceable ecosystem at risk.** Large-scale fishing operations can catch and entangle endangered and threatened wildlife, including whales, dolphins, sea turtles, sharks, and seabirds, while removing fish and top predators that are essential to healthy ocean food webs and harming fragile corals.

For nearly two decades, the Pacific Islands Heritage Marine National Monument has represented a bipartisan conservation commitment. More than one million people, including cultural practitioners, scientists, and organizations across the Pacific and around the world, have stood up for the protection of this extraordinary place.

**Take action today to demand that existing protections remain in place.**

**Tell the Trump Administration and the National Marine Fisheries Service: Keep industrial fishing out of the Pacific Islands Heritage Marine National Monument and maintain existing protections.** Any action affecting these culturally and ecologically irreplaceable waters must follow requirements under federal law, honor Indigenous voices, use the best available science, and provide meaningful opportunities for public participation.

November 6, 2026

The Majorie Barrick Museum of Art Auditorium
4505 S. Maryland Pkwy, Las Vegas, NV 89154

Thirty years ago, Gail Ritchey, a young woman from a conservative Christian community in rural Ohio, gave birth alone and left her newborn in the woods. Now a devoted mother of three, her quiet suburban life shatters when DNA evidence links her to the infamous cold case of “Geauga’s Child.” Arrested for murder and vilified in the media, authorities dismiss her claim that the baby was stillborn. Facing a possible life sentence, Gail and her family must confront religious stigma, community judgment, and long-buried shame in the fight for her freedom.

Directed by Jessica Earnshaw (JACINTA), BABY DOE looks beyond the headlines to reveal the human complexity of Gail’s case, exploring how women’s health, justice, and powerful outside forces shape stories like hers. Watch the trailer here.

A guided discussion led by If/When/How: BSL Chapter will accompany the film screening. As well as tabling of local organizations for reproductive and women's rights.

events.title: General Member Meeting - What's Next?
events.description:
We've set early voting records this midterms, and we expect to see record turnout on November 3rd but we're not in the home stretch!  Between now and January 3rd, we are keeping a watchful eye. 

At Sunday's meeting, we'll be in a celebratory mood but also preparing for the work ahead! 

What happens on January 3rd? This is the day that the 120th Congress is planned to be seated, but only if the Speaker of the House abides by the roll of members-elect listed by the Office of the Clerk. 

Voters on both sides of the aisle are profoundly dissatisfied with the status quo of the Democratic Party. The candidates that won were candidates that were not afraid to tack left and take progressive stands. The candidates handpicked by Schumer and Jeffries did not win in this election. That tells us that Americans are ready for a sea change and we must be prepared to meet that moment. 

At Sunday's meeting, Mary Panzetta, from We Get Out the Resistance, will talk about what happens between now and January 3rd (we're not out of the woods yet-- those votes still need to be certified and the new Congress needs to be seated), the to do list for the new Democrat-controlled Senate and House, and the to do list for the rest of us to make sure this opportunity is not squandered.

location.venue: First United Church of Oak Park

events.description:
2026 #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence

Beginning Wednesday, December 9, 2026 until the end of December, we will come together across the nation to host the #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence.

These local events will be anchored by the 14th Annual National Vigil for All Victims of Gun Violence on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C.—held near the 14-year mark of the Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting tragedy, when a 20-year-old gunman armed with an AR-15 hunted and murdered 20 first graders and six educators.

Across the country, vigils (as simple as lighting candles) and gatherings will honor lives stolen by gun violence, uplift survivors, raise awareness, and demand urgent action from our leaders to finally end this epidemic. From schools and workplaces to houses of worship, neighborhoods, grocery stores, homes, nightclubs, streets, and even our democracy itself—gun violence impacts every aspect of American life.

The theme of this year’s campaign is #FreedomToLive—the simple, powerful idea that every person deserves to live free from the daily threat of gunfire. Together, survivors, families, advocates, and allies will raise our voices to ensure that FREEDOM means the right of every person to live, learn, work, worship, speak, vote, and gather without the daily fear of gun violence.

We stand in solidarity with over 1.4 million Americans who have been shot since Sandy Hook, with every community devastated by gun violence for decades. We will send a clear message to our local, state, and federal lawmakers, raise awareness, and help build the movement for common-sense solutions.

Let’s #HonorWithAction together. Let’s demand freedom from gun violence.

events.title: No One Has to Do It All: A Workshop on Finding Your Place in Renewing Democracy
events.description:
*NO ONE HAS TO DO IT ALL*
Finding Your Place in Renewing Democracy

Most of us know someone who says, “I’m so overwhelmed, I can’t do anything.” Sometimes that someone is us.

This workshop is the antidote. Movements don’t run on a few people doing everything. They run on many people each doing their part. When you see the whole ecosystem, the pressure comes off, and starting gets a lot easier.

We’ll use Deepa Iyer’s Social Change Ecosystem Map to explore ten roles people play in creating change—in our case, renewing democracy. Weavers build connections. Storytellers share what’s happening in our community. Caregivers keep people going. Disruptors shake things loose. There are six more. The map starts with what moves you, not with a list of tasks someone else needs done.

See the Map: https://www.socialchangemap.com/

What you’ll do:

*Learn the ten roles and spot the people in Woodbury who already play them

*Choose the role that pulls at you right now, and join others who chose it too

*Brainstorm practical things you could do in the next few months
Step back with the whole group to see how our pieces fit together

This isn’t a personality test, and you won’t leave with a label. You’ll leave with ideas you can act on, a few new allies, and permission to stop feeling guilty about everything you’re not doing.

*WHO IT'S FOR* Longtime community doers, the newly fired-up, and anyone who’s been sitting on the sidelines wondering where to begin.

events.title: Hybrid Public Hearing: Tell EPA & IDEM to Hold Coal Ash Polluters Accountable
events.description:
The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to approve Indiana’s request to handle permitting and enforcement of federal coal ash requirements. IDEM, an agency that has long been understaffed and underfunded, would oversee it. This program must be no more stringent than the federal rule, which is currently strong thanks to our collective advocacy. However, the federal administration is proposing to dismantle it by rolling back protections for communities like Michigan City and risking more coal ash disasters like what happened in the Town of Pines. Mirroring the federal rule leaves us vulnerable. Hoosiers, enduring more coal ash dumps than any state, deserve lasting protections for health and the environment.

Join the virtual public hearing on November 12th to tell IDEM and EPA to protect our communities from coal ash polluters.

And use Earthjustice's toolkit to develop your comments and learn more about the permit: https://earthjustice.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/toolkit-for-indiana-epa-public-hearing-2026.pdf.

*The hearing begins at 1:00 PM CT and will conclude at 5:00 PM CT. You can choose from one of two time slots: 1-3 PM CT or 3-5 PM CT. This is a hybrid hearing, so it will be held online and at the Indiana Government Center – South, Wabash Hall Conference Rooms 4 and 5, 302 W Washington St, Indianapolis, IN 46204.

events.title: Sweet Potato Gleaning in Kinston, NC on Saturday (11/7) Yam Jam 2026!
events.description:
Join Us for a Sweet Potato Gleaning in Kinston, NC!

Saturday, November 7, 2026 | Kinston, North Carolina

Please join us on Saturday, October 31, for a sweet potato gleaning in Kinston, NC! Together, we will harvest fresh sweet potatoes to help provide nutritious food to local food pantries and families in need.

No farming experience is necessary! Whether this is your first gleaning or you have volunteered with us before, we welcome your participation.

Important Information

What to Expect: If you have never been on a farm, do not worry! We will provide instructions on how to harvest sweet potatoes and will be right beside you to offer assistance. All you need is the time, heart, and physical ability to participate. You are not obligated to stay for the entire gleaning. Come and go as your schedule allows.

What to Wear: We recommend wearing long pants, a comfortable shirt, and closed-toe shoes. Waterproof or water-resistant shoes are encouraged, as fields may be wet or muddy. Please wear clothing you do not mind getting dirty.

What to Bring: Please bring bottled water to stay hydrated. We also recommend sunscreen, a wide-brimmed hat, and work gloves if you have them.

Cancellations: If your plans change, please cancel your registration as soon as possible using the link on this page. If threatening weather or field conditions require cancellation, we will notify registered volunteers by email as soon as possible.

Children and Chaperones: Volunteers of all ages are welcome! However, anyone under the age of 18 must be accompanied by an adult.

Directions: Upon successful registration, you will receive a confirmation email containing the farm's address and additional directions.

Restrooms: Please be aware that most farms where gleanings take place do not have restroom facilities available. We encourage volunteers to plan accordingly.

Help Us Make a Difference!

Every sweet potato harvested helps provide fresh, nutritious food to individuals and families experiencing food insecurity in our communities.

Thank you for sharing your time and helping us feed our neighbors! We look forward to seeing you in Kinston on Saturday, October 31!

Join MFF, LRC & the Pretrial Justice coalition for an interactive, fun, and engaging virtual training designed to equip volunteers and community members with the tools to fight for pretrial justice. We’ll explore the harmful history of cash bail, unpack the stereotypes that fuel it, and discuss the real impact it has on Black and brown communities, low-income families, and our neighbors.

Whether you're new to the movement or a long-time advocate, you'll leave with clear next steps to get involved in transforming our pretrial system

What to expect:

-A crash course on the history and harms of cash bail

-Engaging exercises and thoughtful solutions and alternatives to cash bail


Come learn, build community, and take action with us. We can’t wait to see you there!

events.title: Do the Dan: Upstate Owl Prowl
events.description:
Join PAL and our friends at SPACE for our next adventure in the Do the Dan series: the Upstate Owl Prowl at Cottonwood Trail! Professor Jonathan Storm will lead us on a walk through Cottonwood as we learn about the owls native to our area, the calls they make, and what those calls can tell us.

We’ll keep our ears open along the way and hopefully hear a few of Cottonwood’s resident owls calling!

Important disclaimer: Owls are wild animals, and unfortunately, they do not take reservations. We can’t guarantee an owl encounter, but we can guarantee you’ll learn plenty about them! The next time you hear an owl calling in the night, you might just know whooo you’re listening to and what they’re saying.

We’ll meet at the Woodburn Road trailhead entrance to Cottonwood Trail at 6:00 PM.

Please dress for the weather and wear comfortable shoes for walking the trail. We recommend bringing a low-light flashlight to help you navigate without disrupting our night vision or our chances of hearing some owls!

Donations are always appreciated but are not required to attend.

events.title: WILKES-BARRE Rally: Voters Decided — Workers Over Billionaires
events.description:
Join Action Together NEPA, In This Together NEPA, Make the Road Action PA, SEIU PA, and allied people-powered organizations to celebrate hard-fought victories while calling on elected leaders to deliver on voters’ mandate to lower costs and strengthen communities!

The event will bring together community members, elected officials, labor and community partners, and grassroots organizations to celebrate these victories calling for swift action to ensure affordability, immigrant justice, and economic opportunity for all Pennsylvanians.

El evento reunirá a miembros de la comunidad, funcionarios electos, aliados laborales y comunitarios, y organizaciones de base para celebrar estas victorias y hacer un llamado a la acción inmediata para garantizar la asequibilidad, la justicia para los inmigrantes y las oportunidades económicas para todos los habitantes de Pensilvania.

events.title: Saturday School: You Voted. Now What?
events.description:
You voted - now what? Join us for a quick civic training on what happens after Election Day and how to keep the momentum going. 

**Join Bridge North Texas this Saturday, Nov. 7th, from 9 AM-12 PM for the next session in our Saturday School workshops.**  We'll enjoy a hands-on morning exploring the election process: how an election result becomes official across all levels of government; what happens if that process is interrupted; and the impact such disruptions can have, including on the upcoming legislative session and Congress. 

You'll practice drawing the path a ballot takes from the voting booth to a sworn-in official and/or a newly passed law.

Saturday School is Bridge North Texas's monthly training ground for civic leadership. Each session is hands-on: we show you the skill, you practice it with your fellow attendees, then you take it into your own community. Topics build across the year - one-to-one relationship building, leadership development, civic engagement, advocacy, and campaign planning. No experience required, just a willingness to show up and grow. 
9 AM-12 PM, September through May.










  Open to the whole community.

Saturday, December 5, 2026 at 3:00 pm
Old South Church in Boston
645 Boylston Street, Boston, MA
A free-will offering to support BIJAN will be accepted

On Saturday, December 5 from 3:00 – 5:00 pm, a diverse group of musicians, dancers and poets/spoken word artists will combine their talents to support the work of The Boston Immigration Justice Accompaniment Network (BIJAN).  The performance will feature musical contributions from Harmony Grove and Carolyn Waters, improvisational dance from Jody Leader and Karen Bray, and poetry/spoken word from Reason Being and Lisa Breger.  A highlight of the performance will be interaction between artists performing in different genres.   The performance will take place in Gordon Chapel at Old South Church in Boston, 645 Boylston Street, Boston.  Admission is free and a free will offering will be taken to support BIJAN.  This event is sponsored by the participating artists, with co-sponsorship from the Old South Christian Service and Outreach Committee and The Immigration Justice Committee of First Parish in Brookline.

The Boston Immigration Justice Accompaniment Network (BIJAN) is a community network of individuals, faith communities, and other activist groups working to reduce the escalating harm of our immigration system in the current political context.  They provide accompaniment at court and ICE check-ins, legal referrals, fundraising for bond or legal fees, letters of support from the community, rides for families to visit loved ones in detention, logistical assistance with paperwork or bond payments, and help with housing, transportation, and other immediate needs of people released on bond who have no other resources in the community.  For more information about BIJAN, visit https://www.beyondbondboston.org/.

events.title: What You Made Possible in 2026 & What’s Ahead in 2027
events.description:
In 2026, Vote Forward volunteers took on a bigger problem than turnout: millions of Americans no longer believe government works for them, and that distrust makes them less likely to vote. In June, we relaunched with ambitious new programs, innovations in letter writing, and new ways for volunteers to make a difference. 

You helped increase participation and trust in our democracy one person at a time — by writing new kinds of letters and connecting people to the government benefits available to them. Thank you for everything you did this year to make an impact and help us learn what works. 

Join Executive Director Yasmin Radjy and the Vote Forward team to look back on what you accomplished this year. Our Data & Research team will walk through what we tested, what we tried that was new, what we expect to learn, how we’ll measure impact, and how your work this cycle made that research possible. As always, we’ll publish what we find.

We’ll also share more about our two pilots that went beyond letter-writing:

Constituent Connections: Vote Forward volunteers connected constituents with their member of Congress’s office for help with issues in their lives. 

Benefits Connections: To increase trust in government, Vote Forward volunteers had conversations with thousands of New Mexicans to help identify any exemptions to new federal work requirements they qualify for so they can keep their SNAP benefits. We’re studying whether that experience changes how people see government.

Whether you joined a pilot program, wrote ten letters or ten thousand, this call is for you. Come celebrate what you did this year and get the inside scoop on what comes next.

events.title: Creative Activism Workshop
events.description:
Calling all Creatives:
“Make It Matter: A Creative Activism Workshop”
Led by producer/director/ringmaster Christopher Wangro.
____________

Free workshop invites artists of every discipline to turn creativity into action.

Guest artists Norm Magnusson and Judith Levy join the program. 

Beacon NY — The First Presbyterian Church will host Make It Matter: A Creative Activism Workshop on Sunday, Nov 15 at 1:00 PM. The free workshop is open to artists, actors, musicians, writers, copywriters, painters, poets, potters, dancers, designers, activists: Anyone & everyone interested in using creativity to address the issues of the day. All are welcome.

The three hour program will be led by noted producer and activist Christopher Wangro, and will offer an overview of inventive and effective creative activism from the past decade — examining the thinking behind the work, from communication strategies to the practical challenges of bringing ambitious projects to life.

Wangro who has created social action works on a massive scale all over the globe will be joined by guest artists Norm Magnusson and Judith G. Levy, both acclaimed for projects that employ humor, surprise, and bold design to spark thought and inspire change. Attendees will have the chance to compare notes and jump-start their own creative projects alongside fellow participants.

 

"The Hudson Valley has a vast creative community full of people loaded with innovative, compassionate intelligence — but lately what we see are people aghast, angry, afraid and stunned into inaction," said Wangro. "Our goal is to spark creative “Artivism” and offer insights and inspiration that prompt responses to the moment. Seeing what others have done is exciting, and our hope is this workshop gets people moving. No time like the present!"

The workshop is free, but please RSVP to attend; space is limited.  Please also bring an item for our mutual aid network diapers soap personal hygiene items are very welcomed.

EVENT DETAILS
What: Make It Matter: A Creative Activism Workshop
Who: Led by Christopher Wangro, with guest artists Judith G. Levy and Norm Magnusson
When: Sunday, November 15, 1:00-4:00 PM
Where: First Presbyterian Church, Beacon, NY
Cost: Free — RSVP
Audience: All ages welcome
 
About Christopher Wangro, Norm Magnusson & Judith G. Levy
Chris Wangro's career began, improbably, as ringmaster of a Brechtian circus; from that unlikely start he went on to become a producer of events seen by millions of people around the world He has worked with figures from the Dalai Lama to Dolly Parton creating diverse events focused on reproductive rights, AIDS, the climate emergency, immigrant rights, and education. In 2004 he co-founded The Imagine Fest, which featured hundreds of artistic responses to social issues which grew to become the largest political arts festival in U.S. history.  A bit more detail at wangro.net
 
Norm Magnusson is a artist of many talents. He is known for slyly innovative public projects that use humor and bold visual language to prompt reflection on civic and political life. Magnusson founded the art movement “Funism” in 1991 on the premise that art should be as much fun to look at as it is to think about. He is best known for cast-aluminum historical markers that carry social and political messages into public spaces, For decades his work has taken on issues like racial injustice and inequality. His marker Unarmed Black Men is currently on view at the Museum of the City of New York.

There’s lots more at funism.com.

Judith G. Levy is a multimedia artist whose videos, photographs, installations, and public art confront identity, race, immigration, sexuality, and power through a queer lens. Her works lchallenge accepted narratives and make room for the people they leave out. Levy has been shown at museums including the Indianapolis Museum of Art and supported by the Andy Warhol Foundation and the Lilly Endowment.

events.title: Holding the Light of Democracy
events.description:
Count Every Vote!

Bring a light. Bring a neighbor.

Alaska votes on Tuesday. Right now, election workers across this state are still counting — and that is exactly how it is supposed to go. Because Alaska is vast and our communities are spread across millions of acres, ballots are still arriving from rural villages and military members stationed far from home. Final tabulation doesn’t begin until November 18 — not because of ranked choice voting, but because the size of our state and the distribution of our population means it simply takes time for every ballot to arrive and be counted. The wait isn’t a problem to solve. It’s the system doing its job carefully, the way we want it done.

So on Friday we’re going to stand in the light together while that work finishes and every vote is counted.

We’ll meet outside Loussac at 6:30, hold our candles, hear a few short words, and simply be in the same place for a while. Battery candles will be available, or bring your own.

Come if you voted. Come if you worked the polls. Come if you spent the last two weeks driving neighbors to vote. Come if this week has been a lot and you’d rather not sit with it by yourself. Whatever Tuesday turned out to be, this part we do together.

Nevada has moved from purple to blue for the first time in decades:
•	🏆 Statewide: Democrats won all six constitutional offices, a feat last achieved in 1962.
•	🏛️ Carson City: Democrats won a two-thirds Assembly supermajority and are one seat short in the state Senate, with races still in play.
•	🗺️ Congress: With Benitez-Thompson's win, Democrats swept all four Nevada House seats.

🌊 A Historic Realignment
Democrats won control of the House and Senate. Alaska's and Mississippi's Senate seats are still in contention, so Robert Hubbell's figures are preliminary:
•	🗳️ Turnout: Second highest since 1914, behind only the record set in 2018.
•	🏛️ Congress: At least 254 House seats and 54 Senate seats. Both chambers have flipped in only six earlier midterms, and none produced a larger Senate majority. Only the 1894 wave matched this House majority.
•	🏢 The states: Governorships, statewide offices, and legislatures changed hands in record numbers.
•	🗺️ Gerrymanders: Of 15 seats Republicans gerrymandered, Democrats won 13, including four of five in Texas. Voters refused to be "picked."
•	🔄 Voters: Nearly every demographic shifted toward Democrats by double digits.
Hubbell's verdict: on Nov. 3, the American people revoked the "consent of the governed." He says the transfer of control came with "no troops; no seizure of ballots," because leaders feared the collective will of the people. Speaker Mike Johnson won't seek the minority leader post.

🌄 Red States Chose Change
Voters in states long written off elected Democrats to represent them:
•	🤠 Texas: James Talarico beat Ken Paxton, the first Democratic Senate win there since 1988.
•	🌾 Kansas: Adam Hamilton beat Sen. Roger Marshall. No Democrat had been elected senator there in 94 years.
•	🌴 South Carolina: Annie Andrews beat Sen. Darline Graham, the state's first Democratic Senate win since 1998.
•	🌽 Iowa and Ohio: Josh Turek beat Rep. Ashley Hinson, and Sherrod Brown beat Sen. Jon Husted.

⚖️ Now Comes Accountability
This vote was a call to hold Trump and the MAGA regime accountable. Hubbell calls it a mandate to constrain Trump's "unconstitutional, illegal, and corrupt behavior" and restore Congress as a check on the president. He says voters expect Congress to:
•	🛡️ Limit the president's power to make war, name judges and cabinet members, and ignore statutes and budgets.
•	🔍 Oversee the executive branch, especially the Secretary of Defense and the Attorney General.
•	🏥 Tackle affordability, health care, Medicare and Medicaid, education, the environment, and science.
Hubbell warns that what Democrats do with this mandate will effectively become the 2028 presidential platform.
Lawyer up! Rep. Robert Garcia, incoming House Oversight chair, has two words for Trump, his family, and their allies: "Lawyer up." He says businesses "in bed with the Trumps" will have "no choice but to respond to our questions."
Make them vote. Andra Watkins tells Democrats to use the two and a half months before Congress convenes to write the bills, then repeal the "Big Ugly Bill" on Day 1, even if Trump vetoes it. "MAKE THEM VOTE FOR THEIR DREADFUL POLICIES," she writes. Put Republicans on the record on affordability, billionaire tax breaks, ACA credits, school lunches, women's rights, ICE, and Social Security. A likely veto, she says, is no reason to kill a bill.

📣 Join Us Tuesday
Celebrate what we did, then get back to work. "We revoked the consent of the governed on November 3," Hubbell writes. "We can do it again."
•	✊ Rally: Tuesday, Nov. 10, at noon, Federal Building, 400 S. Virginia St., Reno.
•	🪧 Bring: A sign, a friend, and your demands for the new Congress, which takes office Jan. 3, 2027.
•	🧾 Stay watchful: Washoe County's canvass is due by Nov. 13, and the statewide canvass is Nov. 24.

☮️ Stay peaceful, follow Peace Marshals, and keep to the sidewalks. 📧 indivisiblenorthernnevada@gmail.com

events.description:
Meet on the Tower Bridge Overpass over  WI-53 near Costco. Parking off Gooder and Tower, Eau Claire, 54703.

We provide physical messaging in the real world to connect with and activate voters to demonstrate that resistance is possible. Prepare to wave and generally have a good time.

Rules and Protocols

1. We avoid doing anything that could either harm ourselves or anyone else. This includes stepping into traffic, holding a sign where it could fall onto cars below, climbing fencing, etc.

2. We must not block pedestrian and bike traffic, so please keep the middle of the overpass and/or sidewalk clear to allow them to pass.

3. We supply the messages, you supply the waves. However, you are welcome to also display your own poster boards. Just avoid any messaging that would be rated above a PG-13.

4. We don’t litter. If we find litter, we pick it up and throw it away.

5. We are NOT allowed to attach the signs to the fencing on the overpass. We don’t use stickers or anything that leaves a permanent mark on the overpass. However, chalk is okay and even encouraged.

6. If someone from the ‘opposition’ comes up to talk with us, do not engage with them. Best to just ignore them. One member will be designated to handle them and video record any aggressive interaction so that you can go right on waving.

7. We take lots of pictures and videos during our action for circulation on social media. If you prefer not to be included, please let us know and/or consider wearing a mask.

8. Should law enforcement pay us a visit, only the designated point person from the group should address them.

9. Ignore the middle fingers and negativity coming from some of the cars below. For every one of those confused folks, you are providing hope to another 100 people!

10. The Visibility Brigade is a non-violent, informal volunteer group in which we all participate with an understanding that our own actions are our personal responsibility and we accept our own personal liability. You participate with this understanding.

See you at 2:45pm for setup and 3:00pm to wave!

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

location.venue: Vanderbilt Hall, Tishman Auditorium at NYU

events.description:
## Overview

Join Moms First CEO Reshma Saujani and Coterie for a live lecture and filming hosted at NYU Law's Birnbaum Women's Leadership Center.

**America has had universal childcare before. Most people have never heard that story.**

In Season 2 of the Motherhood Lectures, Moms First Founder and CEO, Reshma Saujani, takes on the hidden history of childcare in America: the wartime nurseries that let millions of moms go to work, the bipartisan childcare bill that came within one signature of becoming law, and the military childcare system that quietly became one of the best in the country.

Each moment was a real chance to fix childcare for every family. Each time, it slipped away. Through a series of short, historically grounded stories, Reshma connects these turning points to the choices families face today, and shows why childcare is not a personal problem but an economic one for the whole country.

Season 2 is co-produced by Moms First and baby care brand Coterie. It's hosted by NYU Law's Birnbaum Women's Leadership Center.

This event will be recorded for online distribution and includes a Q&A with Reshma following the lecture. Doors open at 3 PM. 

### What to expect

- A live, in-person lecture on the untold history of childcare in America

- A panel discussion and Q&A with Reshma Saujani after the lecture

- Professional filming and photography during the event

### Why attend

- To understand how America ended up with a childcare system that works for almost no one

- To learn what has worked before, and what it would take to make it work again

- To be part of a community shaping a more honest conversation about motherhood and caregiving

**Registration is free but required for admission. Space is limited, register today.**

### Filming notice

This event will be professionally filmed. By registering and attending, you acknowledge that you may appear in audience footage used in Moms First, Coterie and NYU content. Filming will focus on the lecture and audience shots.

### Accessibility

We aim to make this event welcoming and accessible. If you have an accommodation request, please contact: [hello@momsfirst.us](mailto:hello@momsfirst.us)

COMMUNITY NORMS: Please read before attending one of our events. One of our main objectives is to host PEACEFUL, RESPECTFUL and SAFE EVENTS. Remember, when attending a Williamsburg JCC Indivisible event, your actions represent our group, and you are expected to conform to the Community Norms. Safety is a top priority for our attendees. Please remain out of the median, per instructions from the police. Being in the median puts us at risk and potentially drivers as well. Do not block the right-of-way for others. If someone is on the sidewalk, please step back and let them pass. If an Urgent Situation arises, we will raise a straight arm with our Hand in a Fist to ask for Silence. PLEASE DO THE SAME TO QUIET THE CROWD. This way we can quickly relay an important message to all. We wish to remind everyone that we do not react to those drivers who make it clear they do not support us by aggravating them through screaming obscenities or making certain hand gestures. We do not want to enrage them and potentially make everyone, including other drivers, less safe. It is easier to wave at everyone and say, “Have a nice day.” PLEASE DO NOT BLOW WHISTLES UNLESS ICE IS PRESENT. The purpose of the whistles is to alert the public to be vigilant. Otherwise, blowing them can falsely alert the crowd to a danger that does not exist! At our events, please do not hold signs or otherwise promote other events that Williamsburg JCC Indivisible is not hosting. You may be placing a potential legal liability onto our group that we are NOT willing to accept. Please do not engage in DISRUPTIVE BEHAVIOURS! If you are asked to stop engaging in activities which are disrupting an event to the point people are complaining to the hosts that they are experiencing physical or emotional trauma, it is expected that you will be respectful of others and follow our Community Norms and stop those behaviours. Loud noises, such as, but not limited to, COWBELLS, horns, etc., are usually deployed by counter-protesters to disrupt an event, not by attendees participating in an event. If you refuse to disengage from such thoughtless behaviours, do not ruin the event for everyone else - please be kind and leave! As with our previous events, the same rules apply. We will not engage with counter-protesters. If an issue arises, please notify one of the event organizers, who will be wearing Williamsburg JCC Indivisible T-shirt. We will not engage in any acts of violence or violation of any applicable laws or engage in civil disobedience. All actions will be peaceful. Everyone participating in this event will be required to behave lawfully to ensure the safety of event participants and will seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. We will obey the orders of authorized event marshals and law enforcement authorities. Event organizers will not be responsible for any injury or damage if any were to occur during this event. Each individual is responsible for the consequences of their actions and attends at their own risk. We will park in the Courthouse parking lot without blocking access lanes and will remove any trash that is left. We are committed to maintaining public health measures to practice safe protesting during these times. Please wear a mask and socially distance if that makes you more comfortable - weigh your own risk in attending. Follow all local safety guidelines at minimum, and any safety instructions from hosts that exceed local law.

events.title: Love as Action: Chicago
events.description:
# Love as Action: Pushing for Peace
## Bearing Witness, Building Hope

### Quaker public witness has stood in opposition to authoritarianism around the world and here at home. It is time for us to show this love in action again. 

Please join the American Friends Service Committee and Chicago area Friends to bear witness and show up for all those impacted by ongoing state violence, whether immigrants in our communities or Palestinians targeted by settlers and Israeli military forces in Gaza and the West Bank. With a slate of newly elected officials promising change, we must not relent in our efforts to build a just and lasting peace.

At 1 PM on Saturday, November 21st, we will gather outside Millennium Park on Michigan Avenue for one hour of silent public worship. Please sign up now and we will provide updates. 

Our intent is that our presence will give hope to all who see us – to show that we can choose resistance to authoritarianism - and remind everyone of our moral obligations to one another.

We're gathering monthly across the country, showing our communities love in action as a public witness of our Quaker values in a time of rising fascism.

Join us! 

Visit us at [Love as Action](https://afsc.org/love-action) to find more resources like downloadable posters, an organizer toolkit, and write-ups of past events.

events.title: Discussing Refuse Fascism's Urgent Mission after the Midterms
events.description:
Trump and the MAGA Republican Party suffered historic electoral losses in the midterms, with voters rejecting them by wide margins across the country. And yet Trump and his fascist regime remain in power, enforcing their fascist program. Behind them stands a virulent MAGA fascist movement, decades in the making, backed by powerful sections of ruling institutions, major financial and business interests, and an organized social base with a Christian fascist movement at its core.

All this is happening in a world in flux. What has happened? What has changed, and what hasn’t? What does it mean to drive out the Trump regime?

Join us this Sunday to analyze and discuss our urgent mission in this changed and changing political constellation: In the name of humanity, we refuse to accept a fascist America. The fascist Trump regime must go now!

events.title: Dignity Is Not a Punchline-Write to Your Congressman Now!
events.description:
This is a constituent-pressure movement, not a partisan campaign. Its message: women are not props, athletes are not punchlines, and public office should not be used to sexualize or mock people for applause.

Why these two moments connect

•	October 25, 2026 — the Nicki Minaj “posterior” moment: At a rally, the President singled out Nicki Minaj in the crowd, made a crude comment about her body, and told her to stand as the crowd cheered. The objection is not that he noticed a celebrity. The objection is that a public official used a rally platform to reduce a woman to her body and turn her into a spectacle.

•	October 22, 2026 — the transgender weightlifter imitation: The President pantomimed a transgender female weightlifter with exaggerated panting and body language, turning a policy debate about women’s sports into a crude caricature. The objection is not that Americans disagree about sports eligibility rules. The objection is that athletes—and women’s athletics—were used as a punchline.

The connective thread: both incidents treat women’s bodies and athletic participation as entertainment. One sexualizes a woman in the crowd; the other caricatures an athlete and demeans women’s sports. The movement says: disagreement is allowed; demeaning spectacle is not.

📢The movement’s demands

Write to your Representative and both Senators and ask them to:

📝 Letter template:

Subject: Dignity Is Not a Punchline, Urgent Opposition to Demeaning Conduct Toward Women and Athletes
Dear Representative [Last Name],

I am writing as your constituent to express my profound objection to two recent incidents involving the President: the October 25, 2026 rally comment singling out Nicki Minaj for her body, and the October 22, 2026 mocking imitation of a transgender weightlifter. I urge you to publicly oppose this conduct and to exercise congressional oversight to ensure that public platforms are not used to sexualize women or turn athletes into punchlines.

I want to be clear: my objection is not rooted in partisanship, in any dislike of Nicki Minaj, or in any particular position on transgender athletes in sports. Americans of good faith can disagree about sports eligibility rules. But disagreement is not the same thing as demeaning spectacle, and public officials should not use their platforms to reduce women to their bodies or to mock athletes for applause.

This conduct shows a lack of respect for women.

When the highest office in the country models objectification and mockery, it shapes public discourse—especially for young people. It tells women that their bodies are fair game for public comment. It tells athletes that their participation is entertainment. And it increases stigma against transgender Americans while distracting from the serious policy questions Congress should be debating. A civilization erodes when it treats dignity as a punchline.

Also, rhetoric that sexualizes women and mocks marginalized people can contribute to harassment and violence, and it poisons public debate. Congress should also determine what standards govern official and government-funded communications, whether any taxpayer resources were used for these events, and what processes exist to prevent public platforms from being used for demeaning spectacle.

What I am asking of you.I respectfully urge you to take the following actions:

1.	Publicly denounce the October 25 comment objectifying Nicki Minaj and the October 22 mocking imitation of a transgender weightlifter, and call on the President to stop using public platforms to sexualize women or caricature athletes.

2.	Support a bipartisan resolution affirming that women are not props, athletes are not punchlines, and public officials should not use official or campaign platforms to demean women.

3.	Exercise congressional oversight by asking the White House and relevant agencies what standards govern official and government-funded communications, whether taxpayer resources were used, and how complaints about demeaning conduct are handled.

4.	Support First Amendment–compliant legislative or regulatory action to ensure that official government communications do not sexualize or demean women and athletes.

5.	Meet with constituents—including women, athletes, and LGBTQ+ advocates—about respect and safety in public discourse.

6.	Respond in writing with your position and the specific actions you will take.

Respect is not optional. Women are not props. Athletes are not punchlines. I urge you to act swiftly and forcefully, and to let me know what steps you plan to take.

Respectfully,

[Your Name]
[Your Address]
[City, State, ZIP]
[Email Address]
[Phone Number]

events.title: Ballot Curing Volunteer Sign Up
events.description:
HELP MAKE SURE EVERY VOTE COUNTS!

We're calling on our community to step up and volunteer! More than 3,000 voters across Kern County and Tulare County have had their mail-in ballots flagged due to missing or mismatched signatures, putting their votes at risk of not being counted.

We're organizing a nonpartisan ballot-curing effort to help connect voters with the information and resources they need to resolve these issues and ensure their ballots can be counted.

How can you help?

Phone Banking: Help us reach voters, let them know about their ballot status, and share instructions on how to resolve their signature issues.

Canvassing: Hit the streets with us to connect with voters directly, provide information, and help them navigate the ballot-curing process.

No experience necessary! We'll provide training, resources, and guidance. 

Join us in making sure our community's voices are heard!
