events.title: Speak From the Heart: Storyteller Training for Trans Liberation
events.description:
Our stories are powerful tools in changing hearts and minds. What changes minds isn't a debate. It's a real conversation with someone whose life is affected.

That's where you come in.

In this 1.5 hour-long virtual workshop, you'll learn how to:

- Shape your own experience — as a parent, a trans person, a faith leader, friend, a neighbor, a medical provider, or an ally — into a story that connects
- Lead with empathy instead of argument, so conversations open people up instead of shutting them down
- Bridge from your story to the facts that matter most to movable audiences
- Feel confident having these conversations with your community, friends, family, neighbors, and canvassing contacts

No experience necessary. Whether you're planning to canvass, phone bank, talk to your own family, or just want to feel more prepared for the conversations already happening around you, this training is for you.

events.description:
Join Us! Bell County Democratic Party Monthly CEC Meeting

Interested in learning more about how your County Democratic Party works and how you can get involved? We'd love to have you join us!

The Bell County Democratic Party's County Executive Committee (CEC) meets monthly, and our meetings are open to the public!

The CEC is made up of elected and appointed Precinct Chairs who help govern the County Party, establish priorities, ensure we run fair and free elections, and guide our efforts to elect Democrats and strengthen our local Democratic community.

What to Expect

CEC meetings are official business meetings conducted under Robert's Rules of Order. While these are not open discussion forums, visitors are welcome to attend and observe the work of the County Party.

Attending is a great opportunity to:

Learn how your County Democratic Party operates and makes decisions.

Hear updates about our plans, priorities, activities, and upcoming elections.

Meet County Party officers, Precinct Chairs, and other Democratic leaders.

Discover opportunities to volunteer, serve on committees, support voter outreach, and get more involved!

Meeting Details

📅 When: Third Thursday of the month

🕠 Time: 6:30 PM

📍 Where: Historic Bell County Courthouse, Belton, TX

Everyone is welcome! Whether you're a longtime Democrat, a new volunteer, or simply curious about how your local Party operates, we encourage you to attend.

Please RSVP so we know you're interested and can share any important meeting updates.

We look forward to meeting you and helping you find your place in building a stronger Bell County Democratic Party!

events.title: No Check Can Buy My Vote
Stop the Nonsense. Do the Work-Write to Your Congressman Now!
events.description:
We launch this movement in response to the “Trump Reflecting Pool” speech of November 2, 2026—not because we oppose renovating a landmark, but because we oppose a presidency that treats the country as a stage.

On the eve of a midterm election, the President gathered the press at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and spent his closing pitch on pipes, rust, algae, and granite—and joked about renaming it the “Trump Reflecting Pool.”

Why we are dissatisfied

First, the speech was not a slip. Twenty-four minutes on algae, pipes, and a proposed renaming is a choice—and the choice was to make the election about a puddle. A citizen watching that speech learned nothing about prices, wages, housing, or war. They learned that the highest platform in the country could be spent on a punchline.

Second, the timing tells you the intent. The eve of the vote. At a memorial to the man who held the Union together. Used for a bit about a reflecting pool.

Third, the distraction has a cost paid by someone else. The worker standing in a parking lot at dawn, hoping to be picked for a roofing job, is not a spectacle. He is a person with rent due. If the state’s enforcement presence follows him to the place he looks for work, then the “nonsense” at the top and the fear at the bottom are not two stories—they are one system, and it is working exactly as designed.

We are not against a clean pool. We are against a government that would rather rename one than govern. Our answer to a spectacle is not a bigger spectacle. It is work—the kind of work the Long March did.

The movement’s demands-Write to your Congressman Now!

Letter template

Subject: Constituent Request: A Pool Was Renamed. Workers Are Still Being Stopped in Parking Lots.

Dear Representative [Last Name],

I am writing as your constituent about two things that belong in the same letter, because they are one story.

First: the November 2 speech. On the eve of the midterms, at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, the President spent his closing pitch on pipes, rust, algae, and granite, and joked about renaming the pool after himself. It was widely described as “nonsensical” and “bizarre.” I am not asking you to police a speech. I am asking you to establish whether federal grounds, federal staff, or federal funds were used as a campaign backdrop, and whether any formal proposal to rename the landmark exists—and if so, what public-comment and historic-preservation review it received. A public memorial is not a stage set, and a national landmark is not a signature.

Second: what the spectacle covered. ICE enforcement actions at and around Home Depot parking lots—places where day laborers gather to seek work—have put people who came to be hired in fear of being stopped and detained. I do not ask you to accept every account as established fact. I ask you to examine it, because oversight exists precisely for practices that are invisible until someone counts them. How many operations? In which states? Under what written policy? With what safeguards for U.S. citizens and lawful residents who are swept up by mistake?

These are the same question. Nonsense at the top; fear at the bottom. A government that renames a pool while a worker is afraid to stand in a parking lot has told us what it thinks its job is. We do not need a pool renamed. We need the work done.

I respectfully urge you to:

1.	Issue a public statement on the use of federal grounds and resources for the November 2 event.

2.	Request Interior and GAO review of the renovation and any renaming proposal, with public comment and historic preservation review.

3.	Call for oversight hearings on ICE enforcement at day-labor pickup sites and retail parking lots.

4.	Demand a published written policy on enforcement at places where people seek work or services.

5.	Support legislation protecting those locations.

6.	Support clearing the visa-certification backlog.

Please reply in writing with your position and the specific steps you will take. I will publish your response, as I will publish every response I receive.
Respectfully,

[Your Name]
[Your Address]
[City, State, ZIP]
[Email Address]
[Phone Number]

events.title: Stand Up for Solar in Mesa County
events.description:
Stand Up For Solar in Mesa County

Mesa County Board of County Commissioners are considering the proposed land use code November 17th. The proposed code includes a 1/4 mile setback on community solar gardens— almost eliminating land suitable for solar gardens. 

Join Western Colorado Alliance and Indivisible Grand Junction to plan your public comment or letter! We'll cover talking points, how to craft your comment or letter, and answer your questions.

Tuesday, November 10 5:30-6:30 at the Monument Room
 Central Library, 443 N. 6th Street, Grand Junction.

Can't make it? No problem! 
Contact your Board of County Commissioners at mcadmin@mesacounty.us or  970-244-1885. Written comments sent well before Nov 17 are the most likely to be read.

Show up before the Board of County Commissioners Tuesday, November 17 at 1:30pm at 544 Rood Avenue Grand Junction, CO.

We are urging to avoid speaking about climate change and stick to technical concerns that will be most effective with our County Commissioners. 

The 1,320 ft setback:
-Reduces the land available in Mesa County for community solar gardens by at least 56% and by 75% in a Grand Valley study area
-Is larger than the setback for oil and gas facilities (400 ft), mining, (125 ft), gravel crushers (250 ft), and other uses that are far more intensive and disruptive than a community solar garden
-Was proposed based on a false assumption about solar decreasing property values 
-Restricts agrivoltaics at a time when farms face financial insecurity and seek to diversify their income with solar
-Restricts solar despite a clear need for energy diversification and localized production

Let's save solar in our community!

events.title: Hawai‘i Island Community ‘Due Process Road Show’ Presentation in Hilo
events.description:
Free public events will explain Hawaii‛s new immigrant justice laws and what they meant for local communities. 

The Campaign for Immigrant Justice (CIJ) coalition will hold two free public events in Hilo and Kona on Thursday, November 12, 2026 to present and explain Hawaii's new immigrant justice laws. 

The events are part of a four-county Due Process Roadshow running through January that brings together the people responsible for implementing the laws and the communities most affected by them. 

This event is free and open to everyone. The Hawai'i Coalition for Immigrant Rights (HCIR) is co-hosting the events with Hawai‘i County Council Member Jennifer Kagiwada, The Legal Clinic (TLC), the ACLU of Hawai‘i, A.L.O.H.A. Latinos Association, Kona Indivisible, and North Hawai’i Indivisible. 

“Six Laws, Real Aloha” captures what the Campaign for Immigrant Justice achieved during the 2026 legislative session. Led by the coalition steering committee, which included HCIR, TLC, and the ACLU, in partnership with Indivisible and more than 50 other organizations, the campaign helped secure a legislative package that strengthens immigrant rights and due process protections statewide. 

The public presentations will highlight the following new laws: 
• Act 141, limiting local police cooperation with federalimmigration enforcement;
• Act 142, establishing statewide standards for U and T visa certifications for crime survivors;
• Act 143, reducing the maximum sentence for nonviolent misdemeanors from 365 to 364 days; 
• Act 161, requiring notice of rights for people in state and county custody before any civil immigration interview;
• Act 162, requiring protected community locations to adopt policies for responding to federal immigration enforcement; and
• Act 179, establishing a language access education and workforce development program at the University of Hawai’i. 
In addition to the public presentations, coalition organizers will meet separately with leaders of the agencies charged with implementing these new laws, including county police, prosecutors, corporation counsel, and administrators. 

Location: Hilo/East Hawai‘i:  12:30-1:30PM, St. Joseph’s Parish Rectory Room (behind the pink church), 43 Kapiolani St.

For more information, visit  CIJ 2026 — Campaign for Immigrant Justice · Six Laws · Due Process Roadshow · HCIR.

events.title: 🪞 Every Accusation Is a Confession: Spotting Authoritarian Projection🔦
events.description:
🪞 Ever notice how the loudest accusations often describe exactly what the accuser is up to? There’s a name for that. Accusation in a mirror is a propaganda technique where you pin your own intentions or actions on your opponent, so that when the truth comes out, it just sounds like he-said-she-said. Authoritarian movements have relied on it for generations, and it’s showing up in our politics right now.

🗳️ At this meeting, we’ll break down how the tactic works and look at real examples. In Alaska, Republicans are calling an alleged ballot-stacking scheme in the Senate race an unprecedented attempt to deceive voters, yet in 2024 the Alaska Republican Party intervened in court to keep an imprisoned Democrat who had never lived in Alaska on the U.S. House ballot. And after years of warnings about voter fraud, the most notable recent case in a federal race came in North Carolina in 2018, where the state elections board ordered a new election because of an illegal absentee ballot operation run by an operative hired for the Republican candidate. 🔍

💪 Recognizing the mirror is the first step to beating it. We’ll practice spotting projection in real time, talk about how to call it out without getting dragged into the mud, and share tools you can use with friends, family, and neighbors. Bring your questions, bring a friend, and come ready to see through the spin! ✊

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Celebrate History with the Upper Allen Mechanicsburg Democratic Club
events.description:
On Monday, November 16, please join the Upper Allen Mechanicsburg Democratic Club at Marzoni’s Oven & Brick Pizza and Brewery, 4925 Ritter Road in Mechanicsburg, at 6:00 p.m. We have a lot to celebrate!

What an extraordinary election cycle for Democrats! From historic victories right here in Mechanicsburg to breakthroughs across Central Pennsylvania, throughout the Commonwealth, and across the country, voters sent a powerful message. Here at home, we saw Democrats make tremendous gains, and two Central Pennsylvania victories deserve special recognition.

Sara Agerton made history by flipping Pennsylvania's 88th House District, winning a seat Democrats had been working hard to turn blue for three consecutive election cycles. Her victory not only represents an important breakthrough in our own backyard but also helps strengthen the Democratic majority in the Pennsylvania House.

And then there is Janelle Stelson, whose remarkable victory over Scott Perry flipped Pennsylvania's 10th Congressional District from red to blue. After coming so close in 2024, Janelle persevered and made history as the first woman to represent any part of the Susquehanna Valley in Congress. Her victory is especially meaningful for Central Pennsylvania and a tremendous milestone for our region.

We also want to recognize Jessica St Clair, who ran an outstanding campaign for the 87th Pennsylvania House District. Although she came up short in the district-wide race, she earned an impressive 48% of the vote right here in Upper Allen Township. That is significant progress and a clear indication that we are moving the needle in a district that has been a difficult one for Democrats. We are grateful for her willingness to step up, work tirelessly, and give voters a choice. Her campaign has helped lay important groundwork for the next election cycle.

These victories were part of something even bigger. Democrats flipped four congressional seats in Pennsylvania, regained control of the U.S. House, and secured a Democratic trifecta in Harrisburg for the first time since 1993. What an election! None of this happens without dedicated candidates, hardworking volunteers, and people willing to step up and make a difference.

Let's take an evening to recognize what we've accomplished together, thank the people who made it happen, and start looking ahead. The 2027 elections will be here before we know it, and we're ready to build on this momentum!

The club will provide pizza and salad. Drinks other than water will be at your own expense.

We hope you'll join us for a fun evening of celebration, camaraderie, and looking ahead to even greater things. We've earned this celebration!

events.title: No Kings Alliance Mutual Aid Drive in Ridgecrest
events.description:
**The No Kings Alliance is mobilizing urgent, nationwide action in response to the Republican government shutdown. Join us this weekend as we provide mutual aid and care to our neighbors hurt by the Republican government shutdown.**

Right now Republicans are refusing to protect critical healthcare and nutrition programs which will result in 42 million Americans losing the benefits that keep their families fed. When those in power hoard resources and use our government to punish people, we answer with collective care and resistance, feeding our bodies and fueling our movement.

Join us at 132 N China Lake Blvd from 9-11am to donate food, household, and personal care products to support families in need. Donations will be delivered to Salvation Army.

Salvation Army has requested the following goods: Rice-a-roni, Cup of noodles, pasta, canned protein (tuna, chicken, beef, beef stew), cereal & granola bars, cans of nuts, boxed cookies & crackers, dried fruits, beef jerky, dry milk, bottled water, mac & cheese, single serving cups of fruit & pudding, cereal, oatmeal packets, and jelly/jam (no peanut butter, they have enough.)

Donation drop off by the shopping center sign.

Find more out about our group at ridgecrest50501.com

_A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events._

events.title: No Kings Alliance Mutual Aid Drive in WHITTIER,CA!
events.description:
Join the Whittier Indivisible Chapter at Michigan Park in Whittier, CA on November 15th, from 11-12:30pm to gather together and DONATE non-perishable food to support families in need. 

Our Chapter will also host a fundraising campaign for the entire month of November to help those in need - ALL proceeds to the Chapter will be sent to a local food pantry. You can donate here: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/indivisiblewc1368840224

Let us support and love on our community! Thousands in our own cities will be affected by the ending of SNAP benefits, and we want to help them. Will you join us?

Additionally, if you cannot make this Mutual Aid Drive & Potluck event on November 15th, we will be hosting various “pop-up tables” throughout the La Habra/Fullerton/Whittier areas to gather donations throughout the month. Please view our Facebook and Instagram pages for information on locations of these tables. All donations will be delivered to the Santa Fe Springs Interfaith Food Center.

All attendees will be sent more details, including the specific list of necessary food items, upon registration! We hope to see you there.
**PLEASE NOTE: We will be hosting TWO FOOD DRIVES at Michigan Park: November 15th and November 22nd (which is why you will see 2 Mobilize events.)
Thanks for joining us!
